low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 1, 2, 4, 6.
; Checked: y = x + c (measured, %5 -> %7).
; Clean: the old x rail (%4, rule 6: |0> after the copy) and the inverse t = y - c (%6), both freed.
; Kept: y (%5, measured: a measured rail stays allocated).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; cq_theta on the classical x0 mints alloc_i32(x0) and rotates it in place (rule 2). y = x + c is a mixed Q+C add: the
; classical c is a literal operand of the _hl template and the sum lands in a fresh rail (rule 4). The measurement of
; y is the sink. x is dead after the add and the add is a bijection in x for fixed c, so the old x rail is cleaned (rule 6):
; t = y - c recomputes it, copy_i32 zeroes x, t is uncomputed, both are freed.

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"

  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_sub_i32_hl(i32 %5, i32 %2)    ; IR: rule 6: t = y - c recomputes the old x (the update is a bijection in it)
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %6, i32 %4)    ; IR: rule 6: x ^= t: the dead x rail is now |0>
  call void @cq_template_sub_i32_hl_unc(i32 %6, i32 %5, i32 %2)    ; IR: rule 6: uncompute t

; Clean: the old y rail (%6, rule 6: |0> after the copy) and the inverse t = z - x (%8), both freed.

; each for the other fixed, so rule 6 cleans operand 0 of the IR add (y: t = z - x) and keeps x (its inverse would read

  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_sub_i32(i32 %7, i32 %5)    ; IR: rule 6: t = z - x recomputes the old y (the update is a bijection in it)

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 14, 7, 6, 4, 5, 2.
; Checked: n (measured: the carried rail n_K, %20 -> %40; rule 6 leaves it the only n rail).
; Clean: every x-chain trip rail (the compare flags, the products, sums, the next-x selects and every trip predicate
; a_0..a_{K-1}, the K-th body's included), popped and uncomputed by the reverse loop; the after-trip-K exit test (%26,
; uncomputed at once); the |1> seed (%8, freed directly); the OLD n of every trip (rule 6, in the body: n' = a ? n + 1 : n
; is a bijection in n for every a and the trip predicate does not read n, so the arm's garbage n + 1 is uncomputed first
; and t = a ? n' - 1 : n' is copied onto the old n, uncomputed and both freed; trip 0's old n is the |0> incoming %7).
; Kept: a_K (%27: the exit test x_K > k evaluated after the K-th body, ANDed with the predicate of trip K; rule 14:
; a_K = 1 iff the loop would run a (K+1)-th trip, observable non-convergence; a loop that exits after exactly K trips
; reads 0); x (%6, the rotated user register, loop-carried through the selects: x * a + b is no bijection in x (a may be
; even) and the trip predicate reads x, so rule 6 does not apply and the x chain is reversed); n (%20, measured). x * a + b
; wraps, so LLVM knows no bound on the trip count and the cutoff is K.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; Re-rolled (rule 14): -O1's pre-header guard x > k (%7) is the latch test %14 one trip earlier (SCEV: both test the
; carried x), so it is trip 0 of the loop. Iteration j of the rolled loop evaluates the test on the carried x, forms
; a_j = a_{j-1} & (x_j > k) from the |1> seed, and runs the body (x = x * a + b, n++) under a_j: the select merges
; advance each carried value only where a_j = 1. The loop is cut off after K bodies (K = 4; the literal 4 below is K).
; After the K-th body the exit test is evaluated once more on the final x and a_K = a_{K-1} & (x_K > k) is kept as the
; output rail; that test is uncomputed at once. Each trip pushes its handles on the runtime handle stack; after n is
; copied out, a reverse loop pops them and uncomputes every trip, every trip predicate included (the K-th body's
; predicate is not a_K). The |1> seed is freed directly (rule 7). RULE 6 IN A ROLLED LOOP (2026-10-31): a carried value
; whose trip update is a bijection and whose trip predicate does not read it (n here) is cleaned in the body of the same
; trip: the new rail is the only one that survives, it is not pushed, the reverse loop never sees it, and no copy-out is
; needed (the measurement reads n_K). A carried value the exit test reads (x) cannot be cleaned: x = k and x = k + 1 both
; leave `x -= 1 under x > k` at k, so that update is not injective (149, 54, 68).
; Basis check (a = 1, b = 0xFFFFFFFF, i.e. x = x - 1; k = 2): x0 = 6 tests 6, 5, 4, 3 > 2 (four bodies, n = 4) and the
; test after the K-th body reads 2 > 2 = 0, so a_K = 0 (exact-K exit); x0 = 7 tests 7, 6, 5, 4 and then 3 > 2 = 1, so
; a_K = 1 (the loop would run a fifth trip). In both cases trip K's own predicate a_{K-1} is 1 and is uncomputed.

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 23, 4, 9, 5, 2.
; Checked: fenv_dfl_env: z + f; fenv_narrow_mask: fetestexcept + (int)z; fenv_op_in_arm: fetestexcept + (int)y;
; fenv_quantum_mode: rc + (int)s (each measured, then combined classically).
; Clean: every intermediate rail (dropped flags states, saved masks, gated exception bits, the quantum mode handle and its
; validity flag, the arm values).
; Kept: the user register of each function (x or m) and the final flags rail of each function (an output, rule 23);
; fenv_op_in_arm's merged value rail y and fenv_quantum_mode's result rails are measured.
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x (fenv_dfl_env, fenv_narrow_mask, fenv_op_in_arm); Ry(th) on m (fenv_quantum_mode).
; Four fenv shapes beyond 80-82, same model (rule 23): the host part goes through the real calls, the quantum part is
; rails; the mode is classical until a quantum value is written into it; the flags rail is sticky and advanced out of
; place; the final flags rail is an output that stays. fenv_dfl_env: fesetenv(FE_DFL_ENV) sets mode 0 and EMPTIES the
; flags rail (the dropped rail is uncomputed in the mirror); feupdateenv(FE_DFL_ENV) restores the default and ORs the
; current flags in, and empty | current is current: no gate. fenv_narrow_mask: fegetexceptflag with mask m saves
; flags & m as the object's quantum part; fesetexceptflag reinstates (current & ~m) | (saved & m) as the new flags rail,
; the previous one dropped. fenv_op_in_arm: a constrained op inside a quantum arm raises only on the arm's branch: its
; exception bits enter the flags through select(pred, exc, 0); the op's value merges by the phi's select (rule 9).
; fenv_quantum_mode: fesetround with an arbitrary quantum argument: valid iff (m & ~0xC00) == 0, mode' = valid ? m : mode
; (a handle from here on), the return value valid ? 0 : 1 is quantum; the classical ops after it take the mode handle
; (_rmq). Mode constants are x86-64's: 0, 1024, 2048, 3072.
source_filename = "fenv_extras.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"

  %5 = call i32 @fegetround()    ; IR: round.dynamic: the classical entry mode, read once from the host
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_fmul_f64_hl_rm(i32 %4, double %2, i32 %5)    ; IR: %5 = constrained.fmul(%4, %2, round.dynamic, strict)
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_fmul_f64_hl_rm_exc(i32 %4, double %2, i32 %5)    ; IR: %5: its exception bits  [the flags rail]
  %8 = call i32 @fesetenv(ptr @_FE_DFL_ENV)    ; IR: %6 = fesetenv(FE_DFL_ENV)  (host call; mode = 0; the flags rail %e0 is DROPPED: the rail is empty again)
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f64_hl_rm(i32 %6, double %2, i32 0)    ; IR: %7 = constrained.fadd(%5, %2, round.dynamic, strict)  [mode = classical 0]

name: 101_longjmp_quantum
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 24, 18, 9, 5, 2.
; Checked: r (measured): escaped ? -1 : inner(x, k) + 2.
; Clean: the arm value x*x + 1 + 2, the clone's result and escaped-flag rails (zeroed by the twin, then freed), and every
; rail inside the clone and its twin.
; Kept: the user register x; the merged result rail (measured).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x.
; A longjmp under a quantum predicate is a MULTI-FRAME PREDICATED EARLY RETURN (rule 24), 24/35's early return carried
; across the call boundary: the callee's clone computes the longjmp arm's predicate as an ESCAPED flag rail beside its
; normal result (the normal arm's pure ops run unguarded, as every arm's do) and returns { result, escaped } (the
; aggregate ABI of 64); at the setjmp site the two continuations are the phi over the diamond, merged by a select on the
; escaped flag: setjmp's second return IS the escaped branch. Nested frames generalise it: every intermediate clone
; between the longjmp and its setjmp returns its own result beside an escaped flag that is the OR of its callees' flags
; and its own longjmp arms, and its continuation after each call is predicated on not-escaped exactly as 35's early
; return predicates the rest of a body. The host _setjmp/longjmp calls are NOT executed: the control transfer is what is
; lowered, and jb is a classical slot never written (the IR carries it as the global @jb). setjmp's return value on the
; escaped path is longjmp's classical argument (1 here; a quantum argument would be a rail selected by the flag); here
; -O1 already folded icmp eq %5, 0 into the diamond, so the flag is the whole of it. Any classical effect inside the
; longjmp arm would be a tape entry (47); this arm has none.
source_filename = "longjmp_quantum.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

@jb = internal global [37 x i32] zeroinitializer, align 16    ; IR: @jb  (classical jmp_buf; never written: setjmp/longjmp are not executed)

define i32 @longjmp_quantum(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %4, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %5 = call fastcc { i32, i32 } @__cq_q_inner_10(i32 %4, i32 %2)    ; IR: %5 = setjmp(@jb) (not executed); %8 = call @inner(%4, %2), clone (arg 0 quantum): { result, escaped }
  %6 = extractvalue { i32, i32 } %5, 0    ; IR: %8  [result rail of the normal continuation]
  %7 = extractvalue { i32, i32 } %5, 1    ; IR: %6 = icmp eq i32 %5, 0 is false iff the callee longjmp'd  [escaped flag rail]
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %6, i32 2)    ; IR: %9 = add nsw i32 %8, 2  (the normal continuation, unguarded)
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_lh(i32 %7, i32 -1, i32 %8)    ; IR: %11 = phi [%9, %7], [-1, %3]: escaped ? -1 : %9  [result rail]
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %8, i32 %6, i32 2)    ; IR: uncompute %9
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %8)    ; IR: release the %9 rail (|0>)
  call fastcc void @__cq_q_inner_10_unc(i32 %6, i32 %7, i32 %4, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %8 and the escaped flag (adjoint of the call)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release the %8 rail (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release the escaped flag (|0>)
  %10 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %9)    ; IR: %12 = cq_measure_si32(%11)
  ret i32 %10    ; IR: ret i32 %12
}

define internal fastcc { i32, i32 } @__cq_q_inner_10(i32 %0, i32 %1) {
  %3 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %0, i32 %1)    ; IR: %3 = icmp sgt i32 %0, %1  [predicate of block %4: longjmp(@jb, 1) fires iff set; the host call is not executed]
  %4 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i32(i32 %0, i32 %0)    ; IR: %6 = mul nsw i32 %0, %0  (block %5, unguarded)
  %5 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 1)    ; IR: %7 = add nuw nsw i32 %6, 1
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: ret i32 %7  [result rail of the call]
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %5, i32 %6)    ; IR: ret i32 %7  [copy the result out]
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: block %4 taken  [escaped flag rail of the call]
  call void @cqrt_copy_i1(i32 %3, i32 %7)    ; IR: copy the escaped flag out
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %5, i32 %4, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %7
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %5)    ; IR: release the %7 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_mul_i32_unc(i32 %4, i32 %0, i32 %0)    ; IR: uncompute %6
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %4)    ; IR: release the %6 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %3, i32 %0, i32 %1)    ; IR: uncompute %3
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %3)    ; IR: release the %3 rail (|0>)
  %8 = insertvalue { i32, i32 } poison, i32 %6, 0    ; IR: ret i32 %7: the result handle
  %9 = insertvalue { i32, i32 } %8, i32 %7, 1    ; IR: the escaped-flag handle (setjmp's second return)
  ret { i32, i32 } %9    ; IR: ret i32 %7
}

define internal fastcc void @__cq_q_inner_10_unc(i32 %0, i32 %1, i32 %2, i32 %3) {
  %5 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %2, i32 %3)    ; IR: recompute %3
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i32(i32 %2, i32 %2)    ; IR: recompute %6
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %6, i32 1)    ; IR: recompute %7
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %7, i32 %0)    ; IR: ret i32 %7  [xor the result out of %out]
  call void @cqrt_copy_i1(i32 %5, i32 %1)    ; IR: xor the escaped flag out of %oesc
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %7, i32 %6, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %7
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release the %7 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_mul_i32_unc(i32 %6, i32 %2, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %6
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release the %6 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %5, i32 %2, i32 %3)    ; IR: uncompute %3
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %5)    ; IR: release the %3 rail (|0>)
  ret void
}

name: 102_effect_tape
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 16, 19, 20, 7, 8, 5, 2.
; Checked: raise_handled: x + hit (hit is a classical read by rule 2; its value is witnessed by the output); raise_default: x;
; remove_cond: x (measured).
; Clean: the predicate flag (x > k) in raise_handled and remove_cond; raise_handled's hit rail (rule 2: hit = select(x > k,
; 30, 0) is a function of x alone, so it collapses with x's measurement and is uncomputed at the collapse point against the
; rail that holds m, with the predicate recomputed on that rail for the purpose); @hit's first seed rail (|0>, never
; written: no cell holds it once the slot takes the collapsed value).
; Kept: the user register x of each function; the tape rails (never freed, replayed by the backend); raise_default's
; predicate flag (it is the abort flag, kept and measured at the end of the shot); @hit's slot, which after the collapse
; holds a fresh seed rail of hit's classical value (rule 7: the cell holds a handle on other paths, 160).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x (each function).
; Classical reads (rule 2): 1 (raise_handled's cq_measure(hit): hit is classical after x's measurement, no gate).
; CLASSICAL EFFECTS UNDER A QUANTUM PREDICATE (rule 16). A host effect cannot happen "in superposition" and executing it
; on a classical reading of the predicate would be a measurement, so every effect under a quantum predicate goes the way
; of printf (47): it is RECORDED on the function's tape with its predicate rail and REPLAYED by the backend after the
; program's last own measurement, on the shots where the predicate measured 1. The host call itself is never executed by
; the lowered program.
;   Effect entries: cqrt_tape_effect_controlled(pred, tape, name) opens an effect entry (name = the callee, as a string
;   constant); its arguments follow as the existing field entries (cqrt_tape_write_<W>[_controlled] for quantum values,
;   _lit for classical ones) plus cqrt_tape_write_str_lit(tape, ptr) for a string argument.
; raise(sig) splits by the classical signal table read off the module's signal() calls (closed world, as the callee set
; of 96/97): (a) a handler in the module runs as a CONTROLLED CLONE, the callee's clone with the predicate as its first
; parameter (__cq_q_h_0_ctl, rule 19: a pure clone is called unguarded as in 97, an effectful one takes the predicate
; because its stores must be guarded); the handler's volatile store to the internal global hit is a guarded store,
; hit = pred ? s : hit (67; the later volatile load reads the handle the slot holds). The slot cell is homogeneous (rule
; 20): it holds a handle on every path, so its first classical value, the initializer 0, is materialised once as a seed
; rail alloc_i32(0) by a module constructor (@hit is program-lifetime storage, as 160's global), the guarded store is the
; select_i32_lh of the literal s against that handle, and the classical original h stores a seed rail too; the delivery
; itself is also recorded on the tape; (b) no handler and a terminating default action (SIGABRT) is the noreturn arm of
; 45: the predicate goes to cqrt_abort_i1 and stays allocated, the signal number recorded on the tape as the shot's abort
; status. (c) remove(path) has nothing to run in the module: the tape entry alone. The return values of
; signal/raise/remove are unused and dropped; signal() is a classical host call and stays.
source_filename = "effect_tape.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

@hit = internal global i32 0, align 4    ; IR: @hit  (internal slot of a quantum value: it holds a HANDLE on every path, rule 20; the constructor below seeds it)
@llvm.global_ctors = appending global [1 x { i32, ptr, ptr }] [{ i32, ptr, ptr } { i32 65535, ptr @__cq_slot_init_hit, ptr null }]    ; IR: program start: @hit's storage comes into existence before any entry runs (160)
@.str = private unnamed_addr constant [10 x i8] c"/tmp/cq_x\00", align 1    ; IR: @.str
@.cq.effect.raise = private unnamed_addr constant [6 x i8] c"raise\00", align 1    ; IR: effect entry name for raise
@.cq.effect.remove = private unnamed_addr constant [7 x i8] c"remove\00", align 1    ; IR: effect entry name for remove

define i32 @raise_handled(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_tape_alloc()    ; IR: the function's tape (output and effects)
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %5, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %6 = call ptr @signal(i32 30, ptr @h)    ; IR: %5 = signal(30, @h)  (classical host call; the compiler reads SIGUSR1 -> @h off it)
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %5, i32 %2)    ; IR: %6 = icmp sgt i32 %4, %2  [predicate of block %7]
  %8 = load i32, ptr @hit, align 4    ; IR: the handle the slot holds before the handler runs (the seed rail): the complement operand of the guarded store, read for rule 2's uncompute below
  call void @cqrt_tape_effect_controlled(i32 %7, i32 %4, ptr @.cq.effect.raise)    ; IR: block %7: %8 = raise(30): the delivery, recorded under the predicate (replayed iff it measures 1)
  call void @cqrt_tape_write_i32_lit(i32 %4, i32 30)    ; IR: %8: argument 0, the signal number (classical)
  call fastcc void @__cq_q_h_0_ctl(i32 %7, i32 30)    ; IR: %8 = raise(30): the installed handler h(30) runs under the predicate (controlled clone)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %7, i32 %5, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %6
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release the %6 rail (|0>)
  %9 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %5)    ; IR: %10 = cq_measure_si32(%4)  [outcome m; %5 holds it from here on]
  %10 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %5, i32 %2)    ; IR: rule 2 collapse of hit: the predicate again, on the rail that holds m (its value is classical now)
  %11 = load i32, ptr @hit, align 4    ; IR: %11 = load volatile i32, ptr @hit  (the hit rail the guarded store left in the slot)
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_lh_unc(i32 %11, i32 %10, i32 30, i32 %8)    ; IR: rule 2: uncompute hit = pred ? 30 : seed (its only quantum source is measured)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %11)    ; IR: release the hit rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %10, i32 %5, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute the recomputed predicate
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %10)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  %12 = icmp sgt i32 %9, %2    ; IR: rule 2: m > k  (classical)
  %13 = select i1 %12, i32 30, i32 0    ; IR: rule 2: hit = (m > k) ? 30 : 0 recomputed classically (the seed's value is 0)
  %14 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %13)    ; IR: the slot takes a seed rail of the classical value (rule 7: the cell holds a handle on other paths)
  store i32 %14, ptr @hit, align 4    ; IR: @hit = hit  (slot store, no gate)

name: 103_complex_float_vector
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 1, 3 (lane moves emit no gate; an unread lane gets no gate), 18, 25, 26, 4, 5, 2.
; Checked: crealf(q) + cimagf(q) (measured, the result rail %15 -> %16).
; Clean: z's real lane a + 0 (%7), its scaled copy (%8), w's real lane (%10) and the clone's copied-out result lane
; (%13, zeroed by the __cq_q_twicef_10_unc twin), all uncomputed in LIFO order and freed; the clone-internal fadd rail.
; Kept: a (%5, the rotated user register).
; Rotations: (Ry, a, th, 1).
; The x86-64 ABI passes
; and returns `float _Complex` as the fixed vector <2 x float>, so clang emits insertelement, extractelement,
; shufflevector and lane-wise vector fadd. A FIXED 2-LANE VECTOR IS A PAIR OF LANES exactly as the { f32, f32 }
; aggregate of 64: each lane is a rail or a classical value on its own, insertelement/extractelement/shufflevector move
; lanes (no gate: a classical permutation of handles and values), and a vector op is one scalar template per lane that
; is read: in twicef, -O1 computes `%2 = fadd %0, %0` and `%3 = fadd %0, %0` and the shufflevector <0, 3> reads lane 0
; of %2 and lane 1 of %3 only, so %3's quantum lane 0 is dead and gets no template (rule 3), its classical lane 1 is a
; plain fadd; a poison lane is read by nothing and gets no gate either; a bitcast <2 x float> to i64 would be the two
; lanes' bit views (18) shifted and or'ed. Here lane 1 (the imaginary part) stays classical throughout: the clone
; `__cq_q_twicef_10` takes the two lanes as (handle, float) with mask 10 and returns { i32, float } (the quantum lane
; copied out as 64, the classical lane as a plain value); its _unc twin takes the lane-0 handle first.
source_filename = "complex_float_vector.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

define float @complex_float(float noundef %0, double noundef %1, float noundef %2, float noundef %3) {
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_f32(float %0)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_f32(%0, %1)  [register a]
  call void @cqrt_ry_f32(i32 %5, double %1)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_f32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %6 = fmul float %2, 0.000000e+00    ; IR: %6 = fmul float %2, 0.0  (classical)
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f32_hl(i32 %5, float %6)    ; IR: %7 = fadd float %6, %5  (commutative, quantum operand first)
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_fmul_f32_hl(i32 %7, float %3)    ; IR: %8 = fmul float %7, %3
  %9 = fmul float %2, %3    ; IR: %9 = fmul float %2, %3  (classical)
  %10 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f32(i32 %7, i32 %8)    ; IR: %10 = fadd float %7, %8  [lane 0 of w]
  %11 = fadd float %9, %2    ; IR: %11 = fadd float %9, %2  (classical: lane 1 of w)
  %12 = call fastcc { i32, float } @__cq_q_twicef_10(i32 %10, float %11)    ; IR: %12, %13 = insertelement (lane 0 = %10, lane 1 = %11: no gate); %14 = call @twicef(%13), clone (lane 0 quantum)
  %13 = extractvalue { i32, float } %12, 0    ; IR: %14 lane 0  (handle)
  %14 = extractvalue { i32, float } %12, 1    ; IR: %14 lane 1  (classical)
  %15 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f32_hl(i32 %13, float %14)    ; IR: %15 = shufflevector %14, poison, <1, poison> (lane 0 = %14's lane 1: no gate); %16 = fadd <2 x float> %14, %15: lane 0 = %14[0] + %14[1]  [result rail]; lane 1 is poison (no gate)
  call fastcc void @__cq_q_twicef_10_unc(i32 %13, i32 %10, float %11)    ; IR: uncompute %14's lane 0
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %13)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_fadd_f32_unc(i32 %10, i32 %7, i32 %8)    ; IR: uncompute %10
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %10)    ; IR: release the %10 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_fmul_f32_hl_unc(i32 %8, i32 %7, float %3)    ; IR: uncompute %8
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %8)    ; IR: release the %8 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_fadd_f32_hl_unc(i32 %7, i32 %5, float %6)    ; IR: uncompute %7
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release the %7 rail (|0>)
  %16 = call float @cqrt_measure_f32(i32 %15)    ; IR: %17 = extractelement %16, 0 (the lane-0 rail); %18 = cq_measure_f32(%17)
  ret float %16    ; IR: ret float %18
}

define internal fastcc { i32, float } @__cq_q_twicef_10(i32 %0, float %1) {
  %3 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f32(i32 %0, i32 %0)    ; IR: %2 = fadd <2 x float> %0, %0: lane 0 (the same rail in both slots)
  %4 = fadd float %1, %1    ; IR: %2: lane 1  (classical)
  %5 = fadd float %1, %1    ; IR: %3 = fadd <2 x float> %0, %0: lane 1 (classical); its lane 0 is read by nothing and gets no template (rule 3)
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_f32(float 0.000000e+00)    ; IR: %4 = shufflevector %2, %3, <0, 3> (lane 0 = %2[0], lane 1 = %3[1]: no gate); ret  [result rail: lane 0]
  call void @cqrt_copy_f32(i32 %3, i32 %6)    ; IR: ret <2 x float> %4  [copy lane 0 out]
  call void @cq_template_fadd_f32_unc(i32 %3, i32 %0, i32 %0)    ; IR: uncompute %2's lane 0
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %3)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  %7 = insertvalue { i32, float } poison, i32 %6, 0    ; IR: ret <2 x float> %4: lane 0, the result handle
  %8 = insertvalue { i32, float } %7, float %5, 1    ; IR: ret <2 x float> %4: lane 1, classical
  ret { i32, float } %8    ; IR: ret <2 x float> %4
}

define internal fastcc void @__cq_q_twicef_10_unc(i32 %0, i32 %1, float %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f32(i32 %1, i32 %1)    ; IR: recompute %2's lane 0
  call void @cqrt_copy_f32(i32 %4, i32 %0)    ; IR: ret <2 x float> %4  [xor lane 0 out of %out]
  call void @cq_template_fadd_f32_unc(i32 %4, i32 %1, i32 %1)    ; IR: uncompute %2's lane 0
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %4)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  ret void
}

name: 104_fpclass
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 4, 9, 5, 2.
; Checked: fpclass_d: isnan(y) + 2*isinf(y) + 4*isfinite(y) + 8*isnormal(y) for y = x * c; fpclass_f: the
; fpclassify code of x (each measured).
; Clean: every intermediate rail (compares, fabs, zext, the constant selects, the or chain, the inner merges, y).
; Kept: the user register x of each function; the result rail (measured).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x (fpclass_d, f64); Ry(th) on x (fpclass_f, f32).
; FLOATING-POINT CLASSIFICATION. clang 19 lowers the classification builtins to what suits each: isnan to `fcmp uno`,
; isinf/isfinite to `fcmp oeq/one |y|, inf` over llvm.fabs, isnormal to the intrinsic `llvm.is.fpclass(y, mask)`
; (mask 264 = 0x108: negative normal | positive normal), and __builtin_fpclassify to a chain of branches on compares
; that -O1 leaves as a diamond chain with a four-way phi. Each compare and fabs is its ordinary template (rule 4);
; `llvm.is.fpclass.<W>(y, mask)` is the template cq_template_is_fpclass_<W>_hl(h, mask) with the classical mask (an i1
; rail; the backend tests the bits of the representation against the ten-class mask); the selects on constants are
; select_i32_ll; the phi chain of fpclass_f is the nested select of 23 (condition tree, rule 9), every compare computed
; unguarded. On Darwin the `fpclassify()` macro calls the library's `__fpclassifyf` instead: that is a lifted clone
; (34), not shown.

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"

  %14 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_ll(i32 %13, i32 8, i32 0)    ; IR: %14 = select i1 %13, i32 8, i32 0
  %15 = call i32 @cq_template_or_i32(i32 %14, i32 %7)    ; IR: %15 = or disjoint i32 %14, %7

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 21, 20, 4, 5, 2.
; Checked: *q + *r (measured), q = align_down(&a[x & 7], 16), r = align_down(&a[x & 7] + 12 bytes, 16). With c = x & 7:
; q is cell c & 4 and r is cell (c + 3) & -4 (0, 4 or 8 = one past the end, which reads 0, §2), so *q + *r = 2v (c = 0),
; 2v + 4 (c = 1..3), 2v + 8 (c = 4), v + 4 (c = 5..7). The values never depend on the host address of a.
; Clean: every pointer-arithmetic rail (byte offsets, flat addresses, masked addresses, rebuilt byte offsets, cell
; indices) and both QROM loads.
; Kept: the user register x; the result rail (measured).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x.
; `llvm.ptrmask(p, m)` (clang's __builtin_align_down / __builtin_align_up, and the and-of-ptrtoint idiom when clang
; recognises it) masks the FLAT ADDRESS of a pointer, so on a fat pointer (84, rule 21) it is 89's round trip:
; materialise u = base[tag] + 4 * idx, `and` the mask, and rebuild. The masked integer is DERIVED FROM ptrtoint(p), so
; the rebuilt pointer keeps p's provenance (rule 21; ptrmask is provenance-preserving in LLVM): tag = p's tag, idx =
; (u' - base[tag]) / 4, one-past-the-end included; no range test, so nothing depends on where the host placed a. Object
; table: object 1 = a (%4), 32 bytes, align 16, 8 i32 cells. p = a + (x & 7) has the CLASSICAL tag 1 (one object) and the
; quantum cell idx x & 7 (the GEP's zext and scaling are address arithmetic, never emitted); %24's 12-byte offset is 3
; i32 cells. The byte form exists only inside the flat-address crossing: idx to a byte offset (zext, shl by log2 4), add
; base[1], mask, subtract base[1], back to a cell index (lshr 2, trunc to the logical i32 index rail). Since a is
; 16-aligned the masked address lands on a[0] or a[4] for q, and on a[0], a[4] or a + 32 (cell 8, one past the end:
; the align-up of a + 20..28) for r; the latter is a pointer of a with idx 8, and its deref is the program's own
; undefined behaviour, which the QROM reads as 0 (an out-of-range index, §2). The rebuilt idx is QUANTUM and the tag the
; classical 1, so each deref is a quantum-offset access of a alone (rule 21: no guard, no merge); a only ever holds the
; classical values v + j, so by rule 20 the access is a QROM read over its current contents (cq_template_qrom_load_i32,
; length 8) and a stays ordinary classical memory with its -O1 initializer stores, never a QRAM. A compiler that reads
; the alignment off the object table may equally lower such a mask as the cell-index mask idx' = idx & (m >> 2) = idx & -4
; with the tag unchanged (a fact of the table, not a peephole); the general route is shown. Everything is uncomputed in
; reverse.

name: 106_fork_join
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 24, 18, 20, 7, 5, 2, §1.4.
; Checked: s = a.out + b.out (measured, the result rail %16 -> %17).
; Clean: the a.out rail (%14, the handle the worker clone stored into the slot; zeroed by the __cq_q_worker_11_unc twin
; and freed by the caller), the a.out seed rail (%11, the classical initializer 0 as a handle, restored into the slot by
; the twin and freed, rule 7) and the clone's product rail (%3 of the clone and %6 of the twin), uncomputed and freed.
; Kept: x (%9, the rotated user register, held in the a.in slot).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; SINGLE-THREAD COLLAPSE (Bennett.jl's stance; owner 2026-10-20): a reversible
; program is a function of its inputs, so a thread interleaving that could change the result has nothing to uncompute;
; data-race-free fork/join code gives the same result under every schedule, and the SEQUENTIAL schedule is taken.
; pthread_create(&t, attr, f, arg) becomes a call of f at the create site: f's quantum clone when arg carries quantum data
; (job a: its cell in holds the handle of x), the classical original when it does not (job b). No host thread is started,
; the host pthread_create is not executed, and the pthread_t slots are classical allocas nothing writes or reads.
; pthread_join is nothing: the result already stands in the job struct, a slot of handles (31). Mutex init stays the
; classical memset/store; lock/unlock are no-ops (94's rule: no contention exists on one thread). The clone of worker takes
; the job pointer as a CLASSICAL pointer (31's shape, not 85's (ptr, tag, idx) triple): the pointer value is classical, only
; the cells behind it are quantum, and the callee dereferences it only classically (loads a handle, stores a handle). A
; pointer-to-slot parameter contributes one mask digit per field it carries, 1 iff the cell holds a handle AT THE CALL
; (§1.4): a.in holds x's handle, and a.out holds a handle too, because a slot cell is homogeneous (rule 20): the worker
; stores a handle into it, so the caller's classical a.out = 0 is materialised as the seed rail alloc_i32(0). Hence
; __cq_q_worker_11. The clone's _unc twin takes (args, old slot handles): it zeroes the a.out rail by recomputation and
; restores a.out's handle from before the call (the seed); the caller loads the clone's a.out handle before the twin and
; frees it after, then frees the seed. Job b's cells never hold a handle and stay classical.
; OUT OF SCOPE: condition variables, barriers and busy-waits on another thread's progress need a scheduler and deadlock
; under the sequential schedule. Multi-QPU placement is a backend matter over the handle graph (gates on disjoint rails
; commute); the lowered IR does not change with the number of devices.

name: 107_pointer_int_union
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 18, 20, 21, 26, §1.4.
; Checked: union_ptr_to_int: *u.p + w (measured, %25 -> %26): x odd: a[1] + w = 2 + w; x even: b + 1 + 4 bytes is b's
; cell 2, one past the end, which reads 0 (§2): w. union_int_to_ptr: *u.p = a[x & 3] = w + (x & 3) (measured, %20 ->
; %21). union_slot: *u.p + w (measured, %19 -> %20): x odd: a[1] + w = 2 + w; x even: b[1] + w = 4 + w.
; Clean: in every function every flag, tag/idx, base, flat-address, byte-offset and cell-index rail, the per-object QROM
; loads and their merge; in union_slot also the slot's |0> idx seed (rule 7) and the new idx rail bump's clone stored
; (zeroed by the __cq_q_bump_0011_unc twin, freed by the caller); every clone-internal rail.
; Kept: x (%6 in union_ptr_to_int, %5 in union_int_to_ptr, %7 in union_slot: the rotated user registers) and the three
; measured results.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1) in each of the three functions.
; A UNION of a pointer and an integer on quantum data. The IR never says "union": with plain code SROA folds the union
; into its value, and the member punning is ptrtoint / inttoptr ON VALUES, i.e. example 89: the fat pointer (tag, idx)
; of 84, idx always a CELL index (rule 21), crosses to the flat address u = base[tag] + 4 * idx (a select over the
; classical bases of the object table plus the byte offset of idx) and back. inttoptr of an integer DERIVED FROM
; ptrtoint(p) keeps p's provenance (rule 21, LLVM's rule): tag = p's tag (the same rail), idx = (u' - base[tag]) / 4
; (sub, lshr by log2 4, trunc to the logical i32 index rail), one-past-the-end included; no range test, so no checked
; value depends on where the host placed the arrays. Only an integer of unknown origin would be decoded by range tests.
; The rebuilt cell index is QUANTUM in all three functions, so every deref is a quantum-offset access of each object in
; the provenance (rule 21). The arrays only ever hold classical values (their -O1 initializers), so by rule 20 each
; access is a QROM read over the object's current contents (cq_template_qrom_load_i32, length = the cell count) and the
; arrays stay ordinary classical memory, never QRAMs. The pure per-object loads run unguarded and are merged by one
; select on the object flag g_a = tag == 1 (provenance {a, b}: b is the complement, innermost; rule 9).
; union_ptr_to_int: p = (x & 1) ? a : b + 1 is (select(x & 1 == 0, 2, 1), select(x & 1 == 0, 1, 0)): b + 1 is b's cell
; 1; ptrtoint, + 4, inttoptr gives idx + 1 in the same object: a's cell 1, or b's cell 2 = one past the end of b (the
; program's own UB at the deref; the QROM reads 0 out of range, §2). union_int_to_ptr: the integer is derived from
; ptrtoint(a) (or disjoint a quantum byte offset), so the pointer is a's (tag 1, classical) with the quantum cell idx
; ((u - base[1]) >> 2); one object and a classical tag: one QROM load, no guard, no merge; it is the measured result.
; union_slot: the union's address escapes to a callee, so the union stays an alloca: a SLOT (rule 20: it holds handles
; and is only accessed at classical offsets) whose cell is of POINTER KIND (its defining store is a store ptr) and holds a
; fat pointer, i.e. TWO HANDLES (tag, idx; the classical cell idx 0 becomes a |0> seed rail because a cell holds
; handles, rule 20). A cell's kind is fixed by its defining store; a mismatched access converts at the access: a load of

; (so the cell keeps holding a pair and the caller's load ptr needs no conversion). bump's i64 is derived from the

; is ((base[T] + 4 * I) + 4 - base[T]) / 4. The derived integer is carried as its provenance plus the byte offset 4 * I
; (rule 21's addr - base[tag]); base[T] is never materialised because the integer is never observed as a number (no

; tls_q: tl * 2 (measured, the shl rail %8 -> %9).
; Clean: ctz_q: the or rail (%4) and the cttz rail (%5), uncomputed and freed; tls_q: the slot's rail x + 1 (%5) and
; the clone's rail x + 1 + c (%7, zeroed by the __cq_q_touch_10_unc twin), both freed; trap_q: the old x rail (%4, rule 6:
; dead after x + 1) and t = r - 1 (%7), both freed.
; Kept: x in ctz_q and tls_q (%3 of ctz_q, 64 bits; %4 of tls_q: rotated user registers whose results have no inverse);
; trap_q's result x + 1 (%6, measured) and its
; abort flag x > k (%5): a noreturn-arm predicate passed to cqrt_abort_i1 stays allocated and the backend measures it
; after the program's last own measurement.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1) in each of the three functions (an i64 Ry in ctz_q).
; The three intrinsics the CQ musl architecture headers produce when their asm is spelled as
; builtins (LIBC_COVERAGE.md): llvm.cttz (a_ctz_64 = bsf) is the unary template cq_template_cttz_<W> exactly as 56's ctlz,
; the is_zero_poison literal being a promise about the operand, not an operand; llvm.trap (a_crash = hlt) is a noreturn
; under a quantum predicate, 45's abort arm: the predicate rail goes to cqrt_abort_i1 and stays allocated, the backend
; measures it after the program's last own measurement; llvm.threadlocal.address (every __thread access) and
; llvm.thread.pointer (__get_tp = mov %fs:0) are classical host intrinsics kept as they are: ONE THREAD, so the TLS block is
; one object of the table with a classical base, and a thread_local global is a classical slot holding a handle exactly
; like 67's static global (the quantum value stored into it is a rail, the load after the call yields that handle). The
; Darwin x86-64 backend has no code generation for llvm.thread.pointer, so this host's trace cannot exercise it; its
; lowering is the same as threadlocal.address's (a classical call returning the object's base), only the latter is shown.
; The callee
; touching the slot through a classical pointer is the clone of 106; its mask is per §1.4, left to right: the pointer-to-slot
; formal p carries one quantum field (digit 1), c is classical (digit 0), __cq_q_touch_10. Its _unc twin takes (args..., old
; slot handles in slot order) = (p, c, the cell's previous handle), zeroes the new rail in place and restores the slot; the
; caller frees the new rail.

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 4, 2, 6.
; Checked: the result of each function (measured): x - c, x * y, x << c, x >> y (logical), x >> c (arithmetic), x & c,
; x | y, x ^ y.
; Clean: rule 6 in sub_qc (the old x rail %4 and t = r + c %6) and xor_qq (the old y rail %6, operand 0 of the IR xor,
; and t = r ^ x %8), all freed; nothing else (each result rail is measured).
; Kept: the user registers x (and y) of the other functions (their op has no inverse in them), xor_qq's x, and the
; measured result rails.
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x in sub_qc, shl_qc, ashr_qc, and_qc; Ry(tx) on x and Ry(ty) on y in mul_qq, lshr_qq, or_qq,
; xor_qq.
; Eight integer opcodes, each out of place into a fresh rail (rule 4). A quantum-classical op takes the classical
; operand as a literal (_hl); a quantum-quantum op takes two handles. A commutative op (mul, or, xor) puts the handle
; order as the template spells it; sub, shl, ashr, and take the literal on the right. sub (in x for fixed c) and xor (in
; either operand) are bijections of a dead register, so rule 6 cleans the old rail right after the op; mul, shifts, and,
; or have no inverse and keep their registers.

; (measured, the sext rail %8 -> %9).
; Clean: bitint_u100: the i100 zext of x (%5), the product (%7), the shifted copy (%8), the sum (%9) and the final shift
; (%10), uncomputed in LIFO order and freed; bitint_s7: the i7 trunc of x (%5) and the clone's copied-out i7 result (%7,
; zeroed by the __cq_q_bump7_10_unc twin), both freed; the clone-internal sum rail.
; Kept: x (%4 in both functions: the rotated 64-bit user register).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1) in each of the two functions (an i64 Ry).
; C23 _BitInt(N) reaches -O1 IR as the native iN types (i100, i7), with the ordinary opcodes and casts on them. RULE: the handle ABI is
; width-only, so a template exists for EVERY width N on demand: cq_template_<op>_i<N>[_hl|_lh], cq_template_zext_i<M>_to_i<N>,
; cq_template_trunc_i<N>_to_i<M>, cqrt_alloc_i<N>/cqrt_copy_i<N>; the runtime's width set is a generator parameter, not a
; limit; signedness stays in the opcode (lshr/ashr, sext/zext) as always; a classical iN operand is passed as an iN literal.
; The user register is the i64 x (cq_theta has no _BitInt overload); the i100 rails are minted by the zext template.

; Checked: (float)twice16(h) with h = (_Float16)(f * c + 1) (measured).

; arithmetic, the clone's result rail (zeroed by the twin, then freed), and every rail inside the clone and its twin.
; Kept: the user register f; the result rail (measured).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on f.
; C23 _Float16 reaches -O1 IR as the native half type. On x86-64 clang promotes half arithmetic to float: every op is
; fpext half->float, the float op, fptrunc float->half; only an op inside a function whose ABI keeps half (the callee
; twice16) stays a half op (fadd half). half is one more FP width (rule 25): cq_template_fptrunc_f32_to_f16 /
; fpext_f16_to_f32 are width variants of 19's casts, fadd_f16 of 13's templates, cqrt_alloc_f16/copy_f16 of the handle
; ABI; fmuladd.f32 is UNFUSED (§2, cf. 14): fmul_f32_hl(h, c) into a product rail, then fadd_f32_hl(product, 1.0); the
; product is uncomputed after the sum it fed (rule 5). The clone of twice16 takes and returns half handles (06/07's

name: 112_overflow_fshr_variants
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 4, 9, 5, 6, 2.
; Checked: uadd_overflow_qc: overflow ? c : x + c; usub_overflow_qq: (x - y) + (unsigned long)overflow; rotr_qc:
; rotr(x, k); rotr_qq: rotr(x, k) with a quantum k (each measured).
; Clean: uadd_overflow_qc's wrapped sum and overflow flag; usub_overflow_qq's overflow flag, then by rule 6 its old x
; (operand 0 of the sub; t = d + y); rotr_qc's and rotr_qq's old x (rule 6: a rotate is a bijection in x for any amount;
; t = fshl(r, r, k)); each t uncomputed, all freed.
; Kept: uadd_overflow_qc's x (its select result has no inverse), usub_overflow_qq's y, rotr_qq's k (a rotate is no
; bijection in its amount); the measured result rails (the select, the wrapped difference and
; its zext'd flag, the two funnel shifts).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x (uadd_overflow_qc, rotr_qc); Ry(tx) on x and Ry(ty) on y (usub_overflow_qq); Ry(tx) on x and
; Ry(tk) on k (rotr_qq).
; Width and op variants of 92 and 56, the three intrinsics the LLVM libc census (LIBC_COVERAGE.md) reported without an
; example. llvm.uadd.with.overflow and llvm.usub.with.overflow return { iN, i1 }: as in 92 the aggregate is TWO templates
; over the same operands (rule 4), the value is the plain wrapping opcode (add_i32_hl, sub_i64: that IS element 0) and
; the flag is cq_template_u<op>_overflow_<W>[_hl], an i1 rail with its own _unc; extractvalue picks the rail, zext i1 is
; the cast template. llvm.fshr is the three-operand funnel shift of 56 (fshl): a rotate is fshr(x, x, k), the same rail
; read in both value slots (56's same-operand rule), with the _qql form for a classical amount and the all-quantum form
; cq_template_fshr_i32 (three handles, as fma's unsuffixed form) when the amount is a register. Everything not measured
; is uncomputed in reverse order; a dead register whose kept result is a bijection in it is then cleaned by rule 6.
source_filename = "overflow_fshr_variants.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_uadd_overflow_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 %2)    ; IR: %5: element 1, the overflow flag (%6)
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_lh(i32 %6, i32 %2, i32 %5)    ; IR: %8 = select i1 %6, i32 %2, i32 %7  [result rail]
  call void @cq_template_uadd_overflow_i32_hl_unc(i32 %6, i32 %4, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %6
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release the %6 rail (|0>)

; 6 (the dead old rail of each such update is cleaned by the bijection t_old = t_new ^ c: compute it fresh, cqrt_copy_i1
; it out, uncompute, free), 10 (CRy / CCRy are cqrt_ry_i1_controlled on the register's current rail; the rotated rail is
; frozen), 5, 2, 3.
; Checked: q1 (%14 -> %20), q2 (its final rail %18 -> %22), q3 (its final rail %16 -> %25), q4 (%4 -> %28): the four
; measured rails, q1 in bit 0 of the returned int.
; Clean: q2's two superseded rails (%3, %15) and q3's superseded rail (%8), the CCRy flag chain (zext %7, select %9, or
; %10, icmp %11) and the rule-6 temporaries (%17, %19), all uncomputed and freed.
; Kept: none beyond the four measured registers.
; Rotations: (Ry, q2, 2*acos(sqrt(1/2)), 1); (Ry, q2, 2*acos(sqrt(1/3)), NOT q2_old) with q2_old = q2 before this gate
; (the rail %4 = q3 = q4 of the source); (Ry, q1, 2*acos(sqrt(2/3)), 2*(q2 ^ NOT q2_old) + q2 == 3); (Ry, q1,
; 2*acos(sqrt(1/2)), q1_old ^ q2) (q2 ^= q1 of SCS_{2,1}; q1_old = q1 before this gate).
; Bärtschi–Eidenbenz |D^4_2> written as plain C: CNOT = `t ^= c`, CRy = `if (c) cq_theta(&t, a)`, CCRy = `s = 2*a + b;
; if (s == 3) cq_theta(&t, a)`. What -O1 did to the circuit (read the ; C: comments): the whole SCS_{4,2} prefix is
; classical except its CCRy, which became an unconditional Ry on q2 (`cq_theta_i1(false, θ)`, q2's register minted from
; |0>); its CRy is gone (control q4 == 0 classically); `q4 ^= q2` and SCS_{3,2}'s `q3 ^= q2` are the same value
; `%4 = xor i1 %3, true` (CSE); SCS_{3,2}'s CRy `if (q3)` is spelled as the inverted branch on q2 itself; `q3 ^= q1` with
; q1 == 0 is folded; and the second `q3 ^= q1` (`%32`) is placed after SCS_{2,1}'s rotation of q1 although it reads q1's
; earlier value `%22`.

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 20, 2, 8, 12, 14, 5.
; Checked: m = sum_i cq_measure(x[i]) << i, the n cells measured.
; Clean: the per-edge compare flag x[eu[e]] == x[ev[e]] (uncomputed and freed every trip).
; Kept: the n i1 registers x[0..n-1] (measured).
; Rotations: Ry(pi/2) on each x[i], i = 0..n-1 (control 1); then per layer l = 0..p-1: for each edge e = 0..ne-1,
; P(-gamma[l]) on NOT flag(x[eu[e]] == x[ev[e]]); for each i = 0..n-1, P(pi/2) on x[i], Ry(2 beta[l]) on x[i],
; P(-pi/2) on x[i].
; QAOA MaxCut on a graph given at run time: the vertex count n, the edge count ne, the edge endpoint arrays eu/ev, the
; layer count p and the angle arrays gamma/beta are all parameters, so every loop is a ROLLED classical loop with a
; runtime bound (rule 14) and no size is fixed at compile time.
; `bool x[n]` is a runtime-sized slot array (rule 20): one `alloca i32, n` of handle cells. Every access to it has a
; classical index: i in the H, mixer and measure loops, and the edge endpoints eu[e], ev[e], which are classical host
; loads from the caller's arrays (the sext and the gep into the slots are the same index). It is never a QRAM.
; Gate shapes:
;  (0) H layer `x[i] = 0; cq_theta(&x[i], pi/2)`: -O1 forwards the stored 0 into the theta (`cq_theta_i1(false, ..)`), so
;      each trip mints the cell's register alloc_i1(false) + Ry(pi/2) (rule 2) and stores its handle in slot i; the
;      `store i8 0` before it is overwritten with no read in between and emits nothing.
;  (1) cost phase `if (x[u] != x[v]) cq_phi(-gamma[l])`: -O1 compares the two cells with `icmp eq i8` and puts the phase
;      in the ELSE arm, so the flag is cq_template_icmp_eq_i1 of the two cell rails into a fresh |0> rail and .O1.ll block %52
;      runs under NOT flag: the kickback cqrt_rz_i1 on the flag inside an X bracket (rule 8); the flag is uncomputed from
;      the two (unchanged) cells and freed every trip. The angle gamma[l] is a classical host load that -O1 left in the
;      arm; it is computed unconditionally (it is in bounds whenever the layer runs: l < p).
;  (2) mixer phase `if (x[i]) cq_phi(+-pi/2)`: the condition is a BARE cell rail, its own predicate: cqrt_rz_i1 directly
;      on the user register (diagonal; no flag, no copy). The .O1.ll `br i1 %70` tests the rotated rail, still the same handle.
;  (3) `cq_theta(&x[i], 2 beta[l])`: Ry in place on the cell's rail; the store of its result changes nothing.

; are measured.

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 12, 14, 20.
; Checked: m, the three counting bits x[T-1-j] (the rails %2, %3, %4 behind the slot array; the measure loop loads each
; as %80 and measures it, %81), and y = a^x mod N (the copied-out rail %30 -> %72); the result is m | y << 8.
; Clean: every mod-exp trip rail (the product, the remainder and the select of each trip, popped and uncomputed by the
; mirror loop right after the loop), the rail holding the classical seed y = 1 (%14, popped as %37, never written) and
; the QFT^-1 Toffoli flags (%62, one per (j, k) pair, uncomputed after their kickback).
; Kept: none beyond the measured registers: the three counting rails and the y result rail, entangled as |x>|a^x mod N>.
; Rotations: (Ry, x[j], pi/2, 1) for j = 0, 1, 2 (H on |0>); then for j = 0, 1, 2 over the logical qubit x[T-1-j]:
; (P, flag, -pi / 2^(j-k), x[T-1-k] & x[T-1-j]) for each k < j, (P, x[T-1-j], pi, x[T-1-j]) (rz_i1 on the bare rail), and
; (Ry, x[T-1-j], pi/2, 1). The mod-exp is a permutation (no rotation).
; Shor order finding for N = 15, a = 7, T = 3 counting qubits, end to end: the three parts are examples
; 58 (the bool array is three i1 rails behind classical handle slots), 62 (the controlled modular multiply in a classical
; loop) and 60 (the QFT^-1 loops), composed. H|0> is Ry(pi/2) in place on each cell. Mod-exp: the condition `if (x[j])` is
; a BARE RAIL loaded from slot j, its own flag (59); the arm's mul/urem are hoisted out of the arm into fresh rails and the
; phi is one select on that rail; y is loop-carried, seeded with a rail holding the classical 1; the classical recurrence
; ap = ap*ap % N runs beside it and is pushed on the handle stack for the mirror. The loop is MIRRORED RIGHT AFTER IT
; (62's placement): the final y is copied out and every trip's rails are uncomputed while the controls x[j] still hold the
; values the trips read; the reverse trip reloads its control from the slot. After the mirror only the three counting
; rails and the y result rail remain, entangled: |x>|a^x mod N>. QFT^-1: `if (x[T-1-k] && x[T-1-j]) cq_phi` is two nested
; bare-rail branches folded into one Toffoli flag, a kickback with the classical angle, un-Toffoli, free (60);
; `if (x[T-1-j]) cq_phi(pi)` is a phase on a bare rail: cqrt_rz_i1 directly on the register (a diagonal gate needs no
; flag); then Ry(pi/2) in place (H = Ry(pi/2)·Z on a superposed qubit). The measure loop reads the slots; y is measured
; last. Replayed on a state vector: m uniform on {0, 2, 4, 6}, y in {1, 7, 4, 13}.

  %39 = getelementptr inbounds [3 x i32], ptr %1, i64 0, i64 %38    ; IR: (slot of x[j])

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 12, 14, 19, 20, 22.
; Checked: m, the t counting bits c[j] (the rails behind the runtime-sized slot array %6; the measure loop loads each and
; measures it; c[j] lands in bit t-1-j).
; Clean: inside every __cq_q_grover_1000_ctl call: both value(x) accumulator walks (zext, shl, or rails and the |0> seed of
; each, pushed per trip and uncomputed by their mirror loops), the compare flags v == marked[k] (k = 0 .. nmark-1) and
; v == 0, the edge flags of the phase blocks, and is_marked's predicate chain (the seed a_0 = pred & v != marked[0] and
; every continue predicate a_k, the last included, rule 14 classical bound with a quantum exit); in the caller the
; QFT^-1 Toffoli flags (one per (k, j) pair).
; Kept: the nq work rails x[i]: never measured, rotated under control by A and A^dag inside the composite (frozen) and
; left entangled with the counting register; the t counting rails are measured.
; Rotations: (Ry, c[j], pi/2, 1) for j = 0..t-1; (Ry, x[i], pi/2, 1) for i = 0..nq-1; then for j = 0..t-1, repeated 2^j
; times (one controlled grover call each): (P, flag, pi, c[j] & v == marked[0]), and for k = 1..nmark-1
; (P, flag, pi, c[j] & v != marked[0] & .. & v != marked[k-1] & v == marked[k]) [O over the marked list, v = value(x)],
; (Ry, x[i], -pi/2, c[j]) for i = 0..nq-1 [A^dag], (P, flag, pi, c[j] & value(x) != 0) [R], (Ry, x[i], pi/2, c[j]) for
; i = 0..nq-1 [A]; then for j = t-1..0: (P, flag, -pi / 2^(k-j), c[k] & c[j]) for k = t-1..j+1, (P, c[j], pi, c[j])
; (rz_i1 on the bare rail), (Ry, c[j], pi/2, 1). nq <= 0 skips both value walks and R; nmark <= 0 skips O.
; Quantum counting (QPE on the Grover iterate), general size: nq, t and the marked list are inputs, so every register is
; a runtime-sized slot array (rule 20: `bool c[t], x[nq]` are `alloca i32, n` of handle cells) and every loop has a
; classical runtime bound (rule 14). The zero-fill loops -O1 turned into memsets are one seed rail alloc_i1(0) per cell
; (rules 20, 22). The defining operation is a CONTROLLED COMPOSITE U: `if (c[j]) grover(x, nq, marked, nmark)` where
; grover holds loops, rotations and phases. The condition is a bare rail loaded from slot j (59); the callee runs as a
; CONTROLLED CLONE (rule 19: the predicate is the first parameter) and the control is pushed into every gate of the
; composite: a rotation becomes cqrt_ry_i1_controlled on the control; a phase block becomes a kickback on a Toffoli flag
; pred & <edge predicate>, one kickback per incoming edge (the edges are disjoint, so the phases add). Clone mask 1000
; (§1.4) over (x, nq, marked, nmark): x is a pointer to a slot array of RUNTIME length whose cells all hold handles at
; the call; §1.4's one digit per cell cannot be spelled for a runtime length, so the pointer contributes ONE digit, 1;
; nq, marked (a classical int table) and nmark are classical. Inside grover: value(x) is the quantum accumulator of 28 over
; the cells (zext, shl, or into fresh rails, mirrored with the handle stack right after its consumers, before A^dag rotates
; the cells); its seed rail also stands for the phi incoming 0 of the nq <= 0 path. is_marked(v) is the early-return list
; loop with a classical bound and a quantum exit: -O1 peels trip 0 into the edge `marked[0] == v` -> %38 and keeps a loop
; whose exhausted edge carries %35 = false (classical: no phase) and whose found edge from %30 carries %35 = true, so each
; found edge is a kickback on a_k & (v == marked[k+1]); every trip computes its continue predicate as the general rule
; does (the last one is read by no gate: the exhausted edge carries no phase); every chain predicate is a function of the
; inputs and is uncomputed by the mirror (pop per trip), then the seed and the trip-0 compare. R = 2|0><0| - I is the kickback on
; pred & NOT (value == 0). The caller's part is the H^t and A loops, the classical repetition loop `for (k < 2^j)` (-O1
; skips j == 31 and runs smax(1 << j, 1) trips), the QFT^-1 (two nested branches c[k], c[j] are one Toffoli flag;
; `if (c[j]) cq_phi(pi)` is cqrt_rz_i1 directly on the bare rail) and the classical measure loop.
; Replayed on a state vector against exact QPE on G (every free asserted |0>; only the registers stay allocated): call 1
; (nq = 3, t = 4, marked {3, 5}): max |p - p_exact| = 1.4e-15, P(round(M~) = 2) = 0.6885; call 2 (nq = 3, t = 3,
; marked {1}): max |p - p_exact| = 9.4e-16, P(round(M~) = 1) = 0.9816. Off-corpus checks of the chain: nq = 3, t = 3,
; marked {1, 3, 5, 6} (two pushed trips) gives P(round(M~) = 4) = 1.0000, and nmark = 0 gives m = 0 with p = 1.

name: 118_qft4_demorgan
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 8, 4, 2, 5.
; Checked: c0 (%2 -> %16), c1 (%3 -> %18), c2 (%4 -> %21), c3 (%5 -> %24), all measured and packed into the returned int.
; Clean: every negation rail (NOT c3 %6, NOT c1 %8, NOT c2 %10, NOT c0 %12) and every flag rail (%7, %9, %11, %13, %14,
; %15), each |0> at its free.
; Kept: the four user registers c0..c3 (measured; a measured rail stays allocated).
; Rotations: (Ry, c0, th, 1); (Ry, c1, th, 1); (Ry, c2, th, 1); (Ry, c3, th, 1); (P, c3, pi, c3); (Ry, c3, pi/2, 1);
; (P, flag, -pi/2, c3&c2); (P, c2, pi, c2); (Ry, c2, pi/2, 1); (P, flag, -pi/4, c3&c1); (P, flag, -pi/2, c2&c1);
; (P, c1, pi, c1); (Ry, c1, pi/2, 1); (P, flag, -pi/8, c3&c0); (P, flag, -pi/4, c2&c0); (P, flag, -pi/2, c1&c0);
; (P, c0, pi, c0); (Ry, c0, pi/2, 1). A middle-four control c_i&c_j is the X-bracketed flag NOT(NOT c_i | NOT c_j).
; The 4-qubit QFT^-1 written with `a && b` conditions: -O1 keeps the first and last conjunctions as
; `select i1 a, i1 b, i1 false` (the Toffoli flag of 59/60), but De-Morgans the middle four: it hoists the NEGATIONS as
; values (%9 = xor i1 %8, true = NOT c3, %16 = NOT c1, %20 = NOT c2, %27 = NOT c0 in the -O1 IR), rewrites each condition
; as `select i1 NOT a, i1 true, i1 NOT b` (= NOT(a && b)) and INVERTS the branches, so the phase block runs under the
; negated flag. Lowered as spelled:
;  - a negation value is a fresh rail: cq_template_xor_i1_hl(rail, 1) (out of place; the register is untouched);
;  - the or-select of two rails, `select i1 NOT a, i1 true, i1 NOT b` = NOT a | NOT b, is a branch flag: cqrt_or_i1 of the
;    two negation rails into a fresh |0> flag (rule 8); the phase block runs under NOT of that flag, so it is an X-bracketed
;    kickback (21, 39); the flag is re-applied (self-inverse) and freed right after;
;  - the two `select i1 a, i1 b, i1 false` conjunctions are the Toffoli flag of 59 (cqrt_and_i1), kickback, un-Toffoli;
;  - `if (q) cq_phi(pi)` on a bare register is cqrt_rz_i1 on that rail (115); cq_theta rotates the rail in place.
; A negation rail is uncomputed after its LAST use and before the next in-place gate on its operand, because the
; uncompute needs the operand's value unchanged: NOT c1 (%8) dies before c1's rotation, NOT c0 (%12) before c0's;
; NOT c3 and NOT c2 die at the end (their registers are not rotated again). Every flag is |0> at its free.
; Replayed on alg_test's sim_qpe.py: |+>^4 (th = pi/2) -> |0000> with p = 1, no ancilla left allocated.
source_filename = "qft4_demorgan.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

define i32 @qft4_demorgan(double noundef %0) {
  %2 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: %2 = cq_theta_i1(false, %0)  [register c0]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i1(i32 %2, double %0)    ; IR: %2 = cq_theta_i1(false, %0)  [Ry]
  %3 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: %3 = cq_theta_i1(false, %0)  [register c1]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i1(i32 %3, double %0)    ; IR: %3  [Ry]

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 18, 12, 8, 5, 2.
; Checked: even_step(x, n, k) (measured).
; Clean: every rail inside the clones (arm values, callee results through the twins, the phase flag) and inside the
; twins; only the outermost result rail survives.
; Kept: the user register x; the result rail (measured).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x; P(0.25) on the flag (x_d > k) at every odd_step level d reached, x_d the level's argument
; (the forward clone only; the pure clones and twins fire no phase).
; MUTUAL RECURSION WITH CLASSICAL DEPTH: even_step and odd_step call each other with n - 1; n is classical, so the
; recursion is ordinary classical control in the clones (rule 18): each clone tests n with a real br and calls the
; other clone, and LLVM's call stack carries the frames (no K bound: the depth is a classical runtime value, unlike
; 98's quantum depth). Each clone follows the call-chain discipline of 33: the result is copied out of a fresh rail
; (the base case copies its argument, it never returns the argument handle itself), the callee's result is uncomputed
; through the callee's _unc twin. odd_step carries a PHASE ARM (03 in a callee, as 35): the flag x > k takes the
; kickback cqrt_rz_i1 and is uncomputed at once. A phase is an effect, not part of the pure value, so a twin must not
; replay it (as 67's tape): the twins recompute through phase-free PURE clones (_pure), and the forward clones (_100)
; are the only ones that fire the phase. Four functions per source function: forward clone, pure clone, twin (the pure
; clone's adjoint xor-out). The twin recursion costs 2^n calls of the deepest level (Bennett's cost for an unrolled
; call tree). Mask suffix as 98: arg 0 quantum, args 1-2 classical.

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 4, 2, 1.
; Checked: sdiv_qc: x / c (measured, %5 -> %6); udiv_qc: x / c (measured, %5 -> %6); srem_qc: x % c (measured,
; %5 -> %6); urem_qq: x % y (measured, %7 -> %8).
; Clean: none to free: each function allocates only its register(s) and the measured result rail.
; Kept: x (%4 in sdiv_qc, udiv_qc and srem_qc; %5 in urem_qq) and y (%6 in urem_qq): the rotated user registers, sources
; of the measured results.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1) in sdiv_qc, udiv_qc and srem_qc; (Ry, x, tx, 1); (Ry, y, ty, 1) in urem_qq.
; Integer division and remainder are ordinary out-of-place templates (rule 4): the signedness lives in the opcode name
; (sdiv/udiv, srem/urem) and the width in the suffix. A classical divisor is a literal of the _hl form; urem_qq divides
; two rails and takes the plain two-handle template. Division by zero and INT_MIN / -1 need no guard: every template
; is total (§2: udiv(a, 0) = 2^W - 1, urem(a, 0) = a, sdiv(a, 0) = -1 or +1 by the sign of a, srem(a, 0) = a,
; sdiv(INT_MIN, -1) = INT_MIN, srem(INT_MIN, -1) = 0), so the same call covers them.

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 4, 5, 10, 20.
; Checked: table_2d's GRID[r & 3][c & 3] (the QROM result %11 -> %12, measured); register_grid's q[0][1] (%36 -> %55) and
; q[rows-1][1] (%40 -> %57), measured and summed.
; Clean: table_2d's index chain (r & 3 %7, c & 3 %8, the row offset %9, the linear index %10), each |0> at its free.
; Kept: table_2d's registers r (%5) and c (%6) and the measured QROM result %11; register_grid's four cells q[i][j]
; (%5..%8, user registers; two of them measured) and, on the rows == 1 path only, the flag %53 (a copy of q[0][1] taken
; before the rotation it controls, entangled with the rotated cell).
; Rotations: (Ry, r, tr, 1); (Ry, c, tc, 1) in table_2d; (Ry, q[i][j], theta[2i+j], 1) per cell in order; then
; (Ry, q[i][1], c, q[i][0]) per row i; then (Ry, q[rows-1][1], c, q[0][1]) (rows > 1) or (Ry, q[0][1], c, flag = copy of
; q[0][1] before the gate) (rows == 1).
; table_2d: a constant 2D table read with a quantum row AND a quantum column is a QROM (29) over the FLATTENED table: -O1
; keeps one getelementptr [4 x [4 x i32]] with two quantum indices, whose element offset is row * 4 + col. That linear
; index is computed into a fresh rail at the width of the C index expressions (i32: shl of r & 3 by the row stride, add
; c & 3), the QROM selects the entry into a fresh result rail, and the index chain is uncomputed LIFO. -O1's zexts to i64
; and the gep's byte scaling are address arithmetic and are not emitted (rule 20); the row flattening is the logical index
; of the 2-D table, not address arithmetic. The table is passed as a pointer literal with 16 cells.
; register_grid: `bool q[2][2]` is a 2D array of classical SLOTS (58), one i1 rail per cell; classical-index accesses
; q[i][j] load the cell's handle; `if (q[i][0]) cq_theta(&q[i][1], c)` is cqrt_ry_i1_controlled with the bare control rail
; (59). The cross-row arm `if (q[0][1]) cq_theta(&q[rows - 1][1], c)` ALIASES when rows == 1: control and target are then
; the SAME cell, i.e. 66's self-conditioned rotation on a bare rail, and a controlled gate whose control is its own target
; is not a gate. The two cell addresses are classical, so the alias question is a classical runtime test on the two slot
; pointers: distinct -> one cRy(q[0][1], q[rows-1][1]); equal -> 66's discipline: the condition is copied into a fresh |0>
; flag BEFORE the rotation (a CNOT copies the basis label the branch reads), cRy(flag, cell), and the flag STAYS ALLOCATED,
; entangled with the cell (it cannot be uncomputed from a cell that changed under it). The four cells are user registers
; and stay allocated.

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 14, 20.
; Checked: quantum_strlen's n (the copied-out result %56 -> %57, measured); quantum_strcmp's `i < cap ? a[i] - b[i] : 0`
; (the copied-out result %86 -> %87, measured).
; Clean: every trip rail (the trip predicates, exit flags, per-trip selects, strcmp's difference and its sexts), popped
; and uncomputed by the reverse loop; the |1> seed and the chain's |0> seed rail (%11; %20), freed directly; the |0>
; cell rails replaced by the 'a' seeds, freed directly.
; Kept: the cells s[i] (strlen) and a[i], b[i] (strcmp), user registers (the 'a' seeds %19; %31, %30 rotated in place),
; and the measured result rail. No predicate is kept: the bound cap is classical, so every trip and exit predicate,
; the last trip's a_last included, is a function of the inputs and is uncomputed by the mirror (rule 14, classical
; bound with a quantum exit).
; Rotations: (Ry, s[i], th[i], 1) per trip i of the fill loop; (Ry, a[i], ta[i], 1), (Ry, b[i], tb[i], 1) per trip i.
; A STRING SEARCH OVER QUANTUM CHARS: -O1 turns `while (n < cap && s[n] != 0) n++` into a classical counted loop over
; cap (the buffer bound) with a quantum EARLY EXIT, and computes n from the classical induction variable in the exit
; block (%28 = trunc %20) merged by the exit phi %30 [0 (cap <= 0), %28 (NUL at trip i), %1 (no NUL)]. So n is never a
; loop-carried quantum value: which EXIT is taken is quantum. The loop stays a classical loop of cap trips (26's shape)
; under the trip predicate a_i = a_(i-1) & NOT z_i (seed |1>), and each exit gets its own predicate: e_i = a_(i-1) & z_i
; for the NUL exit at trip i, a_last for the fall-through exit. These predicates are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE and exactly one is
; 1. The exit phi is merged per rule 9: one cq_template_select_i32 per incoming, chained with the complement arm innermost
; into fresh rails: r_i = select(e_i, i, r_(i-1)) in trip i (the literal incoming %28 is the trip index: _lh), seeded by
; a |0> rail (the incoming 0 of the cap <= 0 edge; a seed, rule 7), and after the loop r = select(a_last, cap, r_last),
; the result. Each trip pushes its predicates and r_(i-1); a reverse loop pops them, uncomputes r_i by its select's _unc,
; then the predicates (the result does not depend on them staying alive).
; quantum_strcmp has two quantum exits from one trip into the same exit block %37 (NUL in a, or a[i] != b[i]): the exit
; flag of the trip is x_i = e1_i | e2_i (or_i1 into a fresh flag, rule 8; e1, e2 exclusive), the block's value
; d = a[i] - b[i] (classical trip index i, quantum chars) is computed unconditionally (pure), merged by
; r_i = select(x_i, d, r_(i-1)); d and its two sexts stay alive (pushed with the trip) and the reverse trip uncomputes
; r_i, x_i, d and the sexts in exact LIFO order (rule 5);
; the fall-through exit and the cap <= 0 edge contribute 0, the value of the |0> seed, so no select is spent on them. The
; last trip's r is copied out (alloc + copy, rule 14) and the reverse loop uncomputes every trip's r.
; Cells: `char s[4]` is an array of classical SLOTS (58), one i8 rail per cell, |0> from the punned zero store; the
; classical store 'a' into a cell replaces the cell's handle by a fresh basis-state seed cqrt_alloc_i8(97) (rule 4: no
; in-place write on a rail; the |0> rail it replaces was never written and is freed directly, rule 7), then cq_theta
; rotates the seed in place. The cells are user registers and stay allocated.

define i32 @quantum_strlen(ptr nocapture noundef readonly %0, i32 noundef %1) {
  %3 = alloca [4 x i32], align 4    ; IR: %3 = alloca [4 x i8]  (classical slots: one handle per cell)
  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i8(i8 0)    ; IR: store i32 0, ptr %3: cell 0 = 0  [register cell 0]
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i8(i8 0)    ; IR: store i32 0, ptr %3: cell 1 = 0  [register cell 1]
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i8(i8 0)    ; IR: store i32 0, ptr %3: cell 2 = 0  [register cell 2]
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i8(i8 0)    ; IR: store i32 0, ptr %3: cell 3 = 0  [register cell 3]
  store i32 %4, ptr %3, align 4    ; IR: (slot 0)
  %8 = getelementptr inbounds [4 x i32], ptr %3, i64 0, i64 1
  store i32 %5, ptr %8, align 4    ; IR: (slot 1)
  %9 = getelementptr inbounds [4 x i32], ptr %3, i64 0, i64 2
  store i32 %6, ptr %9, align 4    ; IR: (slot 2)
  %10 = getelementptr inbounds [4 x i32], ptr %3, i64 0, i64 3
  store i32 %7, ptr %10, align 4    ; IR: (slot 3)
  %11 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: %30 = phi i32 [ 0, %7 ], [ %28, %27 ], [ %1, %24 ]: the innermost arm of the exit select chain, the incoming 0 of the cap <= 0 edge  [seed rail]
  %12 = icmp sgt i32 %1, 0    ; IR: %4 / %8  (classical; -O1 tests it twice)
  br i1 %12, label %13, label %55    ; IR: br i1 %4

13:
  %14 = zext nneg i32 %1 to i64    ; IR: %6 / %10  (classical)
  br label %15

15:
  %16 = phi i64 [ 0, %13 ], [ %22, %15 ]    ; IR: %12  (classical i)
  %17 = getelementptr inbounds [4 x i32], ptr %3, i64 0, i64 %16    ; IR: %13  (slot of s[i])
  %18 = load i32, ptr %17, align 4    ; IR: (handle of s[i]: the |0> rail of the zero initializer, never written)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %18)    ; IR: store i8 97, ptr %13: the cell's old rail is released (a seed in a known basis state)
  %19 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i8(i8 97)    ; IR: store i8 97, ptr %13  [the classical 'a' as a fresh basis-state seed: register s[i]]
  store i32 %19, ptr %17, align 4    ; IR: (the slot takes the seed's handle)
  %20 = getelementptr inbounds double, ptr %0, i64 %16    ; IR: %14  (classical)
  %21 = load double, ptr %20, align 8    ; IR: %15  (classical angle)
  call void @cqrt_ry_i8(i32 %19, double %21)    ; IR: %16 = cq_theta_c(97, %15)  [Ry in place on s[i]]; store i8 %16: handle unchanged
  %22 = add nuw nsw i64 %16, 1    ; IR: %17  (classical)
  %23 = icmp eq i64 %22, %14    ; IR: %18  (classical)
  br i1 %23, label %24, label %15    ; IR: br i1 %18

24:
  %25 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 true)    ; IR: predicate of reaching the first test in %19 (always 1)
  br label %26

26:
  %27 = phi i64 [ 0, %24 ], [ %37, %26 ]    ; IR: %20  (classical trip i)
  %28 = phi i32 [ %25, %24 ], [ %36, %26 ]    ; IR: predicate of reaching this trip's test
  %29 = phi i32 [ %11, %24 ], [ %35, %26 ]    ; IR: %30: the exit select chain so far (r_(i-1))
  %30 = getelementptr inbounds [4 x i32], ptr %3, i64 0, i64 %27    ; IR: %21  (slot of s[i])
  %31 = load i32, ptr %30, align 4    ; IR: %22 = load i8, ptr %21  (handle of s[i])
  %32 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i8_hl(i32 %31, i8 0)    ; IR: %23 = icmp eq i8 %22, 0
  %33 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: predicate of block %27 at this trip (the NUL exit)
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %28, i32 %32, i32 %33)    ; IR: br i1 %23, label %27  taken
  %34 = trunc nuw nsw i64 %27 to i32    ; IR: %28 = trunc nuw nsw i64 %20 to i32  (classical)
  %35 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_lh(i32 %33, i32 %34, i32 %29)    ; IR: %30 incoming %28 from %27: r_i = e_i ? i : r_(i-1)  [fresh rail]
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %32)    ; IR: NOT %23
  %36 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: predicate of block %24 at this trip (continue)
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %28, i32 %32, i32 %36)    ; IR: br i1 %23, ..., label %24  taken
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %32)    ; IR: restore %23
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %28)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %32)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %33)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %29)
  %37 = add nuw nsw i64 %27, 1    ; IR: %25  (classical)
  %38 = icmp eq i64 %37, %14    ; IR: %26  (classical bound: the buffer size)
  br i1 %38, label %39, label %26    ; IR: br i1 %26

39:
  %40 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_lh(i32 %36, i32 %1, i32 %35)    ; IR: %30 incoming %1 from %24 (no NUL in the buffer): r = a_last ? cap : r_last  [result rail; exclusive with every e_i]
  br label %41

41:
  %42 = phi i64 [ %14, %39 ], [ %45, %41 ]    ; IR: reverse trip index (counts down)
  %43 = phi i32 [ %36, %39 ], [ %49, %41 ]    ; IR: continue-predicate of this trip
  %44 = phi i32 [ %35, %39 ], [ %46, %41 ]    ; IR: r_i of this trip
  %45 = add nsw i64 %42, -1    ; IR: the trip being undone
  %46 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: r_(i-1)
  %47 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: e_i
  %48 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: %23 of that trip
  %49 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: a_(i-1)
  %50 = trunc nuw nsw i64 %45 to i32    ; IR: %28 of that trip (classical)
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_lh_unc(i32 %44, i32 %47, i32 %50, i32 %46)    ; IR: uncompute r_i
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %44)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %48)
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %49, i32 %48, i32 %43)    ; IR: uncompute the continue-predicate
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %48)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %43)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %49, i32 %48, i32 %47)    ; IR: uncompute the exit predicate
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %47)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  %51 = getelementptr inbounds [4 x i32], ptr %3, i64 0, i64 %45    ; IR: %21 of that trip
  %52 = load i32, ptr %51, align 4    ; IR: (handle of s[i])
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i8_hl_unc(i32 %48, i32 %52, i8 0)    ; IR: uncompute %23
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %48)    ; IR: release the %23 rail (|0>)
  %53 = icmp eq i64 %45, 0
  br i1 %53, label %54, label %41

54:
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %49)    ; IR: seed predicate back to |0>
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %49)    ; IR: release the seed (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %11)    ; IR: release the chain's seed rail (never written, |0>)
  br label %55

55:
  %56 = phi i32 [ %11, %2 ], [ %40, %54 ]    ; IR: %30: the seed itself when cap <= 0 (incoming 0), else the chain's result
  %57 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %56)    ; IR: %31 = cq_measure_si32(%30)
  ret i32 %57    ; IR: ret i32 %31
}

define i32 @quantum_strcmp(ptr nocapture noundef readonly %0, ptr nocapture noundef readonly %1, i32 noundef %2) {
  %4 = alloca [4 x i32], align 4    ; IR: %4 = alloca [4 x i8]  (classical slots: one handle per cell)
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i8(i8 0)    ; IR: store i32 0, ptr %4: cell 0 = 0  [register cell 0]
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i8(i8 0)    ; IR: store i32 0, ptr %4: cell 1 = 0  [register cell 1]
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i8(i8 0)    ; IR: store i32 0, ptr %4: cell 2 = 0  [register cell 2]
  %8 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i8(i8 0)    ; IR: store i32 0, ptr %4: cell 3 = 0  [register cell 3]
  store i32 %5, ptr %4, align 4    ; IR: (slot 0)
  %9 = getelementptr inbounds [4 x i32], ptr %4, i64 0, i64 1

  %10 = getelementptr inbounds [4 x i32], ptr %4, i64 0, i64 2

  %11 = getelementptr inbounds [4 x i32], ptr %4, i64 0, i64 3
  store i32 %8, ptr %11, align 4    ; IR: (slot 3)
  %12 = alloca [4 x i32], align 4    ; IR: %5 = alloca [4 x i8]  (classical slots: one handle per cell)
  %13 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i8(i8 0)    ; IR: store i32 0, ptr %5: cell 0 = 0  [register cell 0]
  %14 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i8(i8 0)    ; IR: store i32 0, ptr %5: cell 1 = 0  [register cell 1]
  %15 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i8(i8 0)    ; IR: store i32 0, ptr %5: cell 2 = 0  [register cell 2]
  %16 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i8(i8 0)    ; IR: store i32 0, ptr %5: cell 3 = 0  [register cell 3]
  store i32 %13, ptr %12, align 4    ; IR: (slot 0)
  %17 = getelementptr inbounds [4 x i32], ptr %12, i64 0, i64 1
  store i32 %14, ptr %17, align 4    ; IR: (slot 1)
  %18 = getelementptr inbounds [4 x i32], ptr %12, i64 0, i64 2

  %20 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: %44 = phi i32 [ %42, %37 ], [ 0, %9 ], [ 0, %25 ]: the innermost arm of the exit select chain; both 0 incomings are its value  [seed rail]

24:
  %25 = phi i64 [ 0, %22 ], [ %36, %24 ]    ; IR: %14  (classical i)
  %26 = getelementptr inbounds [4 x i32], ptr %12, i64 0, i64 %25    ; IR: %15  (slot of b[i])
  %27 = getelementptr inbounds [4 x i32], ptr %4, i64 0, i64 %25    ; IR: %16  (slot of a[i])
  %28 = load i32, ptr %27, align 4    ; IR: (handle of a[i]: the |0> rail of the zero initializer, never written)
  %29 = load i32, ptr %26, align 4    ; IR: (handle of b[i]: likewise)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %29)    ; IR: store i8 97, ptr %15: b[i]'s old rail is released (a seed in a known basis state)
  %30 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i8(i8 97)    ; IR: store i8 97, ptr %15  [the classical 'a' as a fresh basis-state seed: register b[i]]

  %32 = getelementptr inbounds double, ptr %0, i64 %25    ; IR: %17  (classical)

  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %46)    ; IR: restore %32
  %49 = getelementptr inbounds [4 x i32], ptr %12, i64 0, i64 %41    ; IR: %34  (slot of b[i])

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 4, 5, 8, 12, 18, 20.
; Checked: quantum_bitfield's updated word w (the new word %14 -> %15, measured); bitfield_through_pointer's f.c (the
; lshr-8 result %10 -> %11, measured).
; Clean: quantum_bitfield's field chain (a %7, a + v %8, b %9, the flag %10, the shifted and masked new field %11, %12,
; the cleared word %13); bitfield_through_pointer's field-a rail %8, its flag %9 and the clone's new-word rail %7 (zeroed
; by the _unc twin), all freed.
; Kept: the register w in each function (%6, rotated; frozen) and the measured result rail.
; Rotations: (Ry, w, th, 1); (P, flag, ph, f.b > k) in quantum_bitfield; (Ry, w, th, 1); (P, flag, ph, f.a == 5) in
; bitfield_through_pointer.
; A bit-field is not a memory object: it is a view of its storage unit (here one i32), and -O1 has already spelled every
; field access as integer arithmetic on that word. A read of field b is `lshr`+`and`, a write is the read-modify-write
; `(word & ~mask) | ((v << off) & mask)`: two `and`s and a disjoint `or`, each a fresh rail (nothing in place). When the
; struct is a local whose bytes never escape, SROA dissolves it and the word is an SSA value (first function; -O1 even
; forwards f.b from the computed field instead of re-reading the new word). The condition on the field just written is a
; phase arm on that field's compare flag. The garbage of the RMW (the two masked halves and the field computation) is
; uncomputed after the disjoint or; the new word is measured. Uncompute order is dependency order (rule 5): the cleared
; word (%13) reads only w and is independent of the field chain, so it is undone last; the chain is undone in reverse.
