; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 13, 8, 9, 4, 5, 2.
; Checked: y (the result rail %16 -> %17, measured) and m (%5 -> %18, measured), summed.
; Clean: the four case flags e0..e3 (%6..%9), the two OR predicates (%11, %12), the GREEN-body select %14 and the BLUE
; product %15, each |0> at its free.
; Kept: the enum register m (%5, rotated and measured) and the result rail y (%16, measured).
; Rotations: (Ry, m, th, 1); (P, e0, p, m == 0); (P, e3, -p, m == 3).
; The scrutinee is a quantum enum (enum mode * matches unsigned int * in cq_theta's _Generic: an enum is its compatible
; integer type, i32 in IR). Each case label gets one equality flag; the flags are mutually exclusive, and the missing
; default is the implicit no-op arm (a value outside 0..3 runs no case, so its predicate is the complement and needs no
; flag). Fallthrough is not a C-level notion in IR: it is a block reached from several switch edges, so a block's
; predicate is the disjoint OR of the case flags that reach it:
;   block %6 (RED body)   e0              -> phase arm: kickback cq_phi(p) onto e0
;   block %7 (GREEN body) e0 | e1         -> value: %8 = y0 + 1 (classical: y0 is a parameter)
;   block %9 (BLUE body)  e0 | e1 | e2    -> value: %10 = phi selects %8 when entered from %7 (e0|e1), y0 from the switch (e2)
;   block %12 (ALPHA)     e3              -> phase arm: kickback cq_phi(-p) onto e3
; The two OR predicates are cqrt_or_i1 into fresh |0> flags (rule 8; the edge flags are disjoint); the second reuses the
; first. The phase of the RED body is fired once, on e0 alone, not on the OR: the phase belongs to the block where cq_phi
; stands, and the value code it falls into is shared (method matches arm class: the phase goes to a flag, the values
; merge by select). %10 has two classical data operands (select _ll); the final merge %15 is the quantum %11 when the
; BLUE block ran (e0|e1|e2) and the classical y0 otherwise (select _hl; the ALPHA and no-case edges both carry y0).
; Everything but the result and the enum register is uncomputed LIFO; the enum register is rotated, so it stays (frozen)
; and is measured.

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"

  call void @cqrt_rz_i1(i32 %6, double %3)    ; IR: block %6: cq_phi(%3)  [kickback onto the RED flag only]

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %9)    ; IR: release it (|0>)

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %8)    ; IR: release it (|0>)

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release it (|0>)

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release it (|0>)

  %18 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %5)    ; IR: %17 = cq_measure_ui32(%5)
  %19 = add nsw i32 %18, %17    ; IR: %18  (classical)

name: 124_callee_controlled_ry_in_loop
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 19, 10, 8, 18, 20, 5, 2.
; Checked: r + x + b (measured).
; Clean: inside every trip's clone call, the callee flag f = (x > k + i) and the composed flag g = b & f.
; Kept: the user registers x and b (control and compare inputs only, measured); r (rotated in place under control,
; frozen, measured).
; Rotations: Ry(tx) on x; Ry(tb) on b; for each trip i = 0..n-1 (classical, n > 0): Ry(t) on r under b & (x > k + i).
; A CONTROLLED RY UNDER A COMPOSED CONTROL, ACROSS A CALL, INSIDE A CLASSICAL LOOP THAT SITS IN A QUANTUM ARM. Three
; pieces, each from an existing example:
;   (1) -O1 fuses the outer `if (b)` with the loop guard `n > 0` into one `and i1 %10, %11`. One operand is the bare
;       _Bool rail b (59: a rail is a condition by itself), the other is classical. A classical conjunct is split off as
;       a classical branch (rule 8): when it is false nothing runs, when it is true the predicate IS b. No AND flag is
;       computed in the caller, and the trip counter, the bound and `k + i` all stay classical.
;   (2) The call to step runs under the quantum predicate b, and step has an effect (the store through r that rotates
;       the caller's register in place), so it becomes a CONTROLLED CLONE with the predicate as its first parameter
;       (rule 19, 102: __cq_q_<fn>_ctl_<mask>). The mask is over step's four arguments: the slot pointee *r is quantum
;       (r's address escapes, so r lives in a classical slot holding its handle, 61) and x is quantum; k and t are

; flag (i < x - k), Ry(-th[i]) on r under (i < x - k).

; else (rule 14, classical bound: the loop stays a classical loop; each trip computes its flag, rotates r in place under

; gate inverted; so the trips come out in reverse order (the adjoint of U_{n-1}...U_0 is U_0^dag...U_{n-1}^dag, and the

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 6 (witness: bijective update of a dead value, both outcomes), 3, 5, 18, 2, 4.
; Checked: x2 = f(x, y) ^ z (the final x, %8 -> %10, measured).
; Clean: y = x0 + 1 (%5), z = x0 * c (%6), the clone's result x1 (%7, |0> after the rule-6 copy), the inverse t (%9), and
; the clone's internal rails, all freed.
; Kept: x0 (%4, the rotated register: its composite update has no inverse, so it stays allocated, entangled with the
; result) and x2 (%8, measured).
; Rotations: (Ry, x0, th, 1).
; x has three forward consumers (y, z, the call), so it is a fan-out source; it is the Ry-prepared user register.
; `x = f(x, y)` and `x ^= z` rebind the NAME x: x0 (the register) -> x1 = f(x0, y) = (y + 1) * x0 (the clone's copied-out
; result, rule 18; -O1 rewrote f's body to (b + 1) * a) -> x2 = x1 ^ z (a fresh rail, rule 4). Rule 6 is asked once per
; dead rail, after the rails that read it are uncomputed:
;   x1 is dead once x2 exists and x2 = x1 ^ z is a bijection in x1 for fixed z, so the old rail is cleaned by rule 6:
;   t = x2 ^ z recomputes x1 into a fresh rail, copy_i32(t, x1) zeroes it, t is uncomputed, x1 is freed. Nothing calls
;   the clone's _unc twin, so it is not defined (§1.4).
;   x0 is needed to uncompute z and y, so those are uncomputed first (LIFO: z, then y). Then rule 6 does NOT apply: the
;   composite update x2 = ((x0 + 2) * x0) ^ (x0 * c) is not a bijection in x0 for the other operand c (c = 0 sends x0 and
;   -2 - x0 to the same value), so no inverse exists and x0 stays allocated (garbage policy, 0): it is entangled with the
;   measured result and is never freed.

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 10, 4, 3.

; Clean: none (no garbage rail is minted).
; Kept: measure_then_reuse: the measured x rail (never reused, uncomputed or freed), the then-arm's fresh rotated
; register and the else-arm's classical-value rail (one of them measured at the join); measure_entangled_rotate_other:
; x (rotated in place, measured) and the measured y rail (not provably |0> once x is rotated).
; Rotations: measure_then_reuse: Ry(th) on x; Ry(t) on a fresh register seeded with m, under the classical condition
; m > k. measure_entangled_rotate_other: Ry(th) on x; Ry(t) on x under the classical condition m > k.
; A measurement is the one place where a NAME and its register diverge (rule 2): after `m = cq_measure(x)` the source
; keeps reading x, and every later read of %5 denotes m, a classical value. So the branch on m is ordinary classical
; control (a real br, handle phi at the join, no flag), the then-arm rotation is a fresh register seeded with m and
; rotated, and the else-arm `x += 1` is classical m + 1, put on a rail only because the join merges it with a quantum
; value. The measured rail itself is never reused, uncomputed or freed (it is not provably |0>). In
; measure_entangled_rotate_other the MEASURED name is y; x is never measured, so x keeps naming its own rail (collapsed
; to m - c by the measurement of y, but the compiler never derives that) and the classical-controlled rotation fires in
; place on it. The measured y rail stays allocated: uncomputing y = x + c against x is only valid until x is rotated,
; and a measured rail is never touched.

!0 = !{i32 2, !"SDK Version", [2 x i32] [i32 26, i32 4]}
!1 = !{i32 1, !"wchar_size", i32 4}
!2 = !{i32 8, !"PIC Level", i32 2}
!3 = !{i32 7, !"uwtable", i32 2}
!4 = !{i32 7, !"frame-pointer", i32 2}
!5 = !{!"Homebrew clang version 19.1.7"}
!6 = !{!7, !7, i64 0}
!7 = !{!"int", !8, i64 0}
!8 = !{!"omnipotent char", !9, i64 0}
!9 = !{!"Simple C/C++ TBAA"}
!10 = !{!11, !7, i64 0}
!11 = !{!"pair", !7, i64 0, !7, i64 4}
!12 = !{!11, !7, i64 4}
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 18, 20, 21, §1.4.
; Checked: ptr_select_rmw's a and b after the two increments, a + 2*[x > k] and b + 2*[x <= k] (the cells %29 and %30,
; measured and summed); guarded_field_store's s[0].f + s[1].f + s[i].g (the result rail %32 -> %33, measured).
; Clean: ptr_select_rmw's flag x > k (%14), the tag (%15), the two object flags (%16, %21), the load (%19), the sum
; (%20), the OLD registers a (%12) and b (%13) and the first-increment cells (%22, %23), each cleaned by rule 6 in the
; caller (inverses %24..%27 before the call, %31..%34 after it), and the clone's own rails; guarded_field_store's
; predicate B (%17), the hoisted arm chain (%18..%20), the in-arm select (%21), the stored cell (%25), the post-merge add
; (%28) and the two f seed rails (%11, %15, never written, rule 7), all freed.
; Kept: ptr_select_rmw's x (%11, the rotated register) and the final a and b cells (%29, %30: the clone's stores,
; measured); guarded_field_store's x (%9), y (%10) and the measured result rail %32.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1); (Ry, a, ta, 1); (Ry, b, tb, 1) in ptr_select_rmw; (Ry, x, th, 1); (Ry, y, ty, 1) in
; guarded_field_store.
; ptr_select_rmw: -O1 keeps a and b in memory because the select of their addresses escapes into bump. The two allocas
; are SLOTS (31): each holds the HANDLE of its register. The selected pointer is a fat pointer (84): tag rail =
; select(x > k, 1, 2) over the object table a = 1, b = 2, idx the classical cell 0 (one cell per object). The load
; through it is a select over the reachable cells on the flag tag == 1 (77's read over quantum cells); the store gives
; each reachable cell a new rail w_o = (tag == o) ? sum : cell_o and writes that handle into o's slot. The update is a
; BIJECTION of each old cell for the given tag (w_o = cell_o + [tag == o]) and the old cells are dead once the load and
; the sum (their only other readers) are uncomputed, so rule 6 cleans them: t_o = (tag == o) ? w_o - 1 : w_o is computed
; fresh, copy_i32(t_o, cell_o) zeroes the old rail, t_o is uncomputed and the old rail freed. The registers a and b are
; thereby MOVED into the new cells: nothing stays beside them. A QUANTUM POINTER ARGUMENT crosses the clone boundary as
; the rule-21 triple (object, tag, idx): the object part of a fat pointer over several objects is the caller's OBJECT
; TABLE (%10: the host address of each object in its provenance, in tag order, filled by the caller), the tag its rail,
; idx the i32 cell index. The mask is per §1.4 over the triple: the table gets no digit, tag 1, idx 0, then one digit
; per pointee cell the callee accesses (a's and b's cells, both holding handles at the call): __cq_q_bump_1011. The clone
; repeats the read-add-write on the slots at cell idx of each object and returns with the slots holding the new cells.
; It does NOT clean the cells it overwrote: a clone is shared by every call site with its mask and only the caller knows
; whether the old handles are dead (rule 18). Here they are (nothing else reads %22, %23 after the call), so the CALLER
; cleans them by rule 6 after the call, with the same inverse t_o = (tag == o) ? w_o - 1 : w_o. Nothing is left for an
; _unc twin to undo, and none is defined (§1.4: a twin nobody calls is not defined). The flags and the tag are then
; uncomputed and the final cells measured in place.
; guarded_field_store: a classical index i keeps s in memory, the store s[i].f = ... sits in an arm under the quantum
; predicate B = x > k, and the stored value is an IN-ARM SELECT. The object table gives s one cell kind per field column:
; the store's gep reaches only the f cells (offsets 0 and 8, stride 8), so those hold handles from the start (fresh
; rails holding c and c + 1), the g cells stay classical. The arm's chain (%17..%20) is hoisted and runs unguarded
; (pure); the guarded store is w = B ? %20 : old with old the handle in cell s[i].f, resolved at run time by the
; classical gep. After the merge the loads read whatever handle each f cell holds. Before the measurement the post-merge
; add, the stored w (the slot gets old back), the in-arm select AND its operand chain %19, %18, %17, then B are
; uncomputed. The f seed rails were never written and hold the classical c, c + 1; they are released like 28's seed rail
; (rule 7).
source_filename = "quantum_ptr_select_store.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

%struct.pair = type { i32, i32 }

define i32 @ptr_select_rmw(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2, i32 noundef %3, double noundef %4, i32 noundef %5, double noundef %6) {
  %8 = alloca i32, align 4    ; IR: %8 = alloca i32  (object 1: a, a slot holding a's handle)
  %9 = alloca i32, align 4    ; IR: %9 = alloca i32  (object 2: b, a slot holding b's handle)
  %10 = alloca [2 x ptr], align 8    ; IR: the object table of %14's provenance {a, b}: host address per tag, classical (the object part of the rule-21 triple)
  %11 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %10 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %11, double %1)    ; IR: %10 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %12 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %3)    ; IR: store i32 %3, ptr %8; %11 = cq_theta_si32(%3, %4)  [register a]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %12, double %4)    ; IR: %11 = cq_theta_si32(%3, %4)  [Ry]
  store i32 %12, ptr %8, align 4    ; IR: store i32 %11, ptr %8  (the handle into slot a)
  %13 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %5)    ; IR: store i32 %5, ptr %9; %12 = cq_theta_si32(%5, %6)  [register b]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %13, double %6)    ; IR: %12 = cq_theta_si32(%5, %6)  [Ry]
  store i32 %13, ptr %9, align 4    ; IR: store i32 %12, ptr %9  (the handle into slot b)
  %14 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %11, i32 %2)    ; IR: %13 = icmp sgt i32 %10, %2
  %15 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_ll(i32 %14, i32 1, i32 2)    ; IR: %14 = select i1 %13, ptr %8, ptr %9  [the pointer's tag: a (1) or b (2); its idx is the classical cell 0]
  %16 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %15, i32 1)    ; IR: %15 = load i32, ptr %14: object a addressed iff tag == 1, else b
  %17 = load i32, ptr %8, align 4    ; IR: %15: the handle in slot a (no gate)
  %18 = load i32, ptr %9, align 4    ; IR: %15: the handle in slot b (no gate)
  %19 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %16, i32 %17, i32 %18)    ; IR: %15 = load i32, ptr %14  [the read over both quantum cells]
  %20 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %19, i32 1)    ; IR: %16 = add nsw i32 %15, 1
  %21 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %15, i32 2)    ; IR: store i32 %16, ptr %14: object b addressed iff tag == 2
  %22 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %16, i32 %20, i32 %17)    ; IR: store: a = (tag == 1) ? %16 : a
  %23 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %21, i32 %20, i32 %18)    ; IR: store: b = (tag == 2) ? %16 : b
  store i32 %22, ptr %8, align 4    ; IR: store i32 %16, ptr %14  (slot a holds the new cell)
  store i32 %23, ptr %9, align 4    ; IR: store i32 %16, ptr %14  (slot b holds the new cell)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %20, i32 %19, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %16 (the new cells keep its value)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %20)    ; IR: release the %16 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %19, i32 %16, i32 %17, i32 %18)    ; IR: uncompute the load %15 (the old cells' last reader)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %19)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  %24 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %22, i32 -1)    ; IR: rule 6 on the old a: new a - 1
  %25 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %16, i32 %24, i32 %22)    ; IR: rule 6: t = (tag == 1) ? new a - 1 : new a, the old a recomputed fresh
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %25, i32 %17)    ; IR: rule 6: the old a rail ^= t: |0>
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %25, i32 %16, i32 %24, i32 %22)    ; IR: uncompute t
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %25)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %24, i32 %22, i32 -1)    ; IR: uncompute new a - 1
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %24)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %17)    ; IR: release the old a rail (|0>)
  %26 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %23, i32 -1)    ; IR: rule 6 on the old b: new b - 1
  %27 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %21, i32 %26, i32 %23)    ; IR: rule 6: t = (tag == 2) ? new b - 1 : new b, the old b recomputed fresh
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %27, i32 %18)    ; IR: rule 6: the old b rail ^= t: |0>
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %27, i32 %21, i32 %26, i32 %23)    ; IR: uncompute t
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %27)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %26, i32 %23, i32 -1)    ; IR: uncompute new b - 1
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %26)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %18)    ; IR: release the old b rail (|0>)
  store ptr %8, ptr %10, align 8    ; IR: table[1] = &a  (classical)
  %28 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %10, i64 8    ; IR: table[2]
  store ptr %9, ptr %28, align 8    ; IR: table[2] = &b  (classical)
  call fastcc void @__cq_q_bump_1011(ptr %10, i32 %15, i32 0)    ; IR: call fastcc void @bump(ptr %14): clone, %14 as the rule-21 triple (object table, tag, cell idx 0); mask 1011: tag quantum, idx classical, the two accessed pointee cells (a, b) hold handles
  %29 = load i32, ptr %8, align 4    ; IR: %17 = load i32, ptr %8  (the handle the clone stored: a)
  %30 = load i32, ptr %9, align 4    ; IR: %19 = load i32, ptr %9  (the handle the clone stored: b)
  %31 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %29, i32 -1)    ; IR: rule 6 in the CALLER on the first-increment a cell %22 (dead after the call): new a - 1
  %32 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %16, i32 %31, i32 %29)    ; IR: rule 6: t = (tag == 1) ? new a - 1 : new a, the old cell recomputed fresh
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %32, i32 %22)    ; IR: rule 6: the old a cell ^= t: |0>
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %32, i32 %16, i32 %31, i32 %29)    ; IR: uncompute t
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %32)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %31, i32 %29, i32 -1)    ; IR: uncompute new a - 1
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %31)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %22)    ; IR: release the first-increment a cell (|0>)
  %33 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %30, i32 -1)    ; IR: rule 6 in the caller on the first-increment b cell %23: new b - 1
  %34 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %21, i32 %33, i32 %30)    ; IR: rule 6: t = (tag == 2) ? new b - 1 : new b
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %34, i32 %23)    ; IR: rule 6: the old b cell ^= t: |0>
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %34, i32 %21, i32 %33, i32 %30)    ; IR: uncompute t
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %34)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %33, i32 %30, i32 -1)    ; IR: uncompute new b - 1
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %33)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %23)    ; IR: release the first-increment b cell (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl_unc(i32 %21, i32 %15, i32 2)    ; IR: uncompute the b flag
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %21)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl_unc(i32 %16, i32 %15, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute the a flag
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %16)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_ll_unc(i32 %15, i32 %14, i32 1, i32 2)    ; IR: uncompute the tag
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %15)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %14, i32 %11, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %13
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %14)    ; IR: release the %13 rail (|0>)
  %35 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %29)    ; IR: %18 = cq_measure_si32(%17)
  %36 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %30)    ; IR: %20 = cq_measure_si32(%19)
  %37 = add nsw i32 %36, %35    ; IR: %21 = add nsw i32 %20, %18  (classical)
  ret i32 %37    ; IR: ret i32 %21
}

define internal fastcc void @__cq_q_bump_1011(ptr %0, i32 %1, i32 %2) {
  %4 = load ptr, ptr %0, align 8    ; IR: %0: object 1 (a's slot) from the table
  %5 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %0, i64 8    ; IR: table[2]
  %6 = load ptr, ptr %5, align 8    ; IR: %0: object 2 (b's slot)
  %7 = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %4, i32 %2    ; IR: %0 in a: cell idx (classical)
  %8 = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %6, i32 %2    ; IR: %0 in b: cell idx
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %1, i32 1)    ; IR: %2 = load i32, ptr %0: object a iff tag == 1, else b
  %10 = load i32, ptr %7, align 4    ; IR: %2: the handle in a's cell
  %11 = load i32, ptr %8, align 4    ; IR: %2: the handle in b's cell
  %12 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %9, i32 %10, i32 %11)    ; IR: %2 = load i32, ptr %0
  %13 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %12, i32 1)    ; IR: %3 = add nsw i32 %2, 1
  %14 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %1, i32 2)    ; IR: store i32 %3, ptr %0: object b iff tag == 2
  %15 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %9, i32 %13, i32 %10)    ; IR: store: a = (tag == 1) ? %3 : a
  %16 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %14, i32 %13, i32 %11)    ; IR: store: b = (tag == 2) ? %3 : b
  store i32 %15, ptr %7, align 4    ; IR: store i32 %3, ptr %0  (a's cell)
  store i32 %16, ptr %8, align 4    ; IR: store i32 %3, ptr %0  (b's cell)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %13, i32 %12, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %3 (the new cells keep its value)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %13)    ; IR: release the %3 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %12, i32 %9, i32 %10, i32 %11)    ; IR: uncompute %2
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %12)    ; IR: release the %2 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl_unc(i32 %14, i32 %1, i32 2)    ; IR: uncompute the b flag
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %14)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl_unc(i32 %9, i32 %1, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute the a flag
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %9)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  ret void    ; IR: ret void  (the slots hold the new cells; the old cells stay the caller's, which cleans them by rule 6)
}

define i32 @guarded_field_store(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2, i32 noundef %3, double noundef %4, i32 noundef %5, i32 noundef %6) {
  %8 = alloca [2 x %struct.pair], align 16    ; IR: %8 = alloca [2 x %struct.pair]  (object 1: s; f cells hold handles, g cells classical)
  %9 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %9 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %9, double %1)    ; IR: %9 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %10 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %3)    ; IR: %10 = cq_theta_si32(%3, %4)  [register y]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %10, double %4)    ; IR: %10 = cq_theta_si32(%3, %4)  [Ry]
  %11 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %5)    ; IR: store i32 %5, ptr %8  [s[0].f: a quantum store reaches it, so it is a rail holding c]
  store i32 %11, ptr %8, align 16    ; IR: store i32 %5, ptr %8  (the handle into cell s[0].f)
  %12 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %8, i64 4    ; IR: %11
  store i32 7, ptr %12, align 4    ; IR: store i32 7, ptr %11  (classical: s[0].g)
  %13 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %8, i64 8    ; IR: %12
  %14 = add nsw i32 %5, 1    ; IR: %13 = add nsw i32 %5, 1  (classical)
  %15 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %14)    ; IR: store i32 %13, ptr %12  [s[1].f: a rail holding c + 1]
  store i32 %15, ptr %13, align 8    ; IR: store i32 %13, ptr %12  (the handle into cell s[1].f)
  %16 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %8, i64 12    ; IR: %14
  store i32 8, ptr %16, align 4    ; IR: store i32 8, ptr %14  (classical: s[1].g)
  %17 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %9, i32 %2)    ; IR: %15 = icmp sgt i32 %9, %2  [predicate B of block %16]
  %18 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %10, i32 %5)    ; IR: %17 = icmp sgt i32 %10, %5  (block %16, hoisted: pure)
  %19 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i32_hl(i32 %10, i32 3)    ; IR: %18 = mul nsw i32 %10, 3  (hoisted)
  %20 = call i32 @cq_template_sub_i32_hl(i32 %10, i32 %5)    ; IR: %19 = sub nsw i32 %10, %5  (hoisted)
  %21 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %18, i32 %19, i32 %20)    ; IR: %20 = select i1 %17, i32 %18, i32 %19  [the in-arm select]
  %22 = sext i32 %6 to i64    ; IR: %21 = sext i32 %6 to i64  (classical)
  %23 = getelementptr inbounds [2 x %struct.pair], ptr %8, i64 0, i64 %22    ; IR: %22  (classical address of s[i].f)
  %24 = load i32, ptr %23, align 8    ; IR: store i32 %20, ptr %22: the handle the cell held before
  %25 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %17, i32 %21, i32 %24)    ; IR: store i32 %20, ptr %22 under B: s[i].f = B ? %20 : s[i].f
  store i32 %25, ptr %23, align 8    ; IR: store i32 %20, ptr %22  (the cell holds the new rail)
  %26 = load i32, ptr %8, align 16    ; IR: %24 = load i32, ptr %8  (handle of s[0].f)
  %27 = load i32, ptr %13, align 8    ; IR: %25 = load i32, ptr %12  (handle of s[1].f)
  %28 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32(i32 %27, i32 %26)    ; IR: %26 = add nsw i32 %25, %24
  %29 = sext i32 %6 to i64    ; IR: %27  (classical)
  %30 = getelementptr inbounds [2 x %struct.pair], ptr %8, i64 0, i64 %29, i32 1    ; IR: %28  (classical address of s[i].g)
  %31 = load i32, ptr %30, align 4    ; IR: %29 = load i32, ptr %28  (classical: a g cell)
  %32 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %28, i32 %31)    ; IR: %30 = add nsw i32 %26, %29  [result rail]
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_unc(i32 %28, i32 %27, i32 %26)    ; IR: uncompute %26
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %28)    ; IR: release the %26 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %25, i32 %17, i32 %21, i32 %24)    ; IR: uncompute the stored cell
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %25)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  store i32 %24, ptr %23, align 8    ; IR: adjoint of the store: the cell holds its old handle
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %21, i32 %18, i32 %19, i32 %20)    ; IR: uncompute the in-arm select %20
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %21)    ; IR: release the %20 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_sub_i32_hl_unc(i32 %20, i32 %10, i32 %5)    ; IR: uncompute %19
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %20)    ; IR: release the %19 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_mul_i32_hl_unc(i32 %19, i32 %10, i32 3)    ; IR: uncompute %18
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %19)    ; IR: release the %18 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %18, i32 %10, i32 %5)    ; IR: uncompute %17
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %18)    ; IR: release the %17 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %17, i32 %9, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %15
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %17)    ; IR: release the %15 rail (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %15)    ; IR: release s[1].f's seed rail (never written, holds the classical c + 1)

; by the mirror), the |1> seed predicate and the 0.0 seed of acc (rule 7), and the final flag acc > 2 lim.
; Kept: the user register x; the copied-out acc rail (measured); r (rotated under control, frozen, measured).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x; Ry(tr) on the fresh |0> rail r under (acc > 2 lim), acc the copied-out loop result.
; Three mechanisms composed: the loop-carried fp rail of 28 (one unfused multiply-add per trip, §2: an fmul_hl product
; rail x * c[i] and an fadd into u_i, both pushed on the handle stack; the mirror after the copy-out), the quantum break
; of 26, and the controlled Ry of 39 conditioned on the loop's RESULT (rule 14, classical bound with a quantum break).
; -O1 tests the break AFTER the body and folds it with the classical exit into `select i1 %17, i1 true, i1 %19`; the
; classical half %19 keeps the loop a classical loop over all n trips, the quantum half becomes the trip predicate: trip
; i's body runs iff a_{i-1} (no break before it), a_i = a_{i-1} AND NOT (u_i > lim), u_i = (c[i] * x) + acc_{i-1} (two
; roundings) computed unguarded (pure), and the carried value is acc_i = a_{i-1} ? u_i : acc_{i-1}. After the last trip
; acc_n is the exit phi %22 for every break point. WHICH-PATH RAILS: every trip predicate a_i and break flag e_i is

; the value the trips read; nothing of the loop survives except the copied-out acc. The mirror runs BEFORE the
; controlled Ry (62/116 placement), so the Ry's flag is computed from the copy: f = acc > 2 lim, Ry(tr) on the fresh |0>

; trip, and the old acc), popped and uncomputed by the reverse loop; the seed rail holding the classical 1 (%5, popped
; as %40), never written and freed directly.

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 11, 15, 9, 8, 5, 2.
; Checked: phi_angle_select and nested_angle_select: x; theta_angle_select and shared_angle_select: r + x (measured).
; Clean: every select flag (x > k, x > k1, x > k2), every angle rail A and nested_angle_select's inner angle rail, all
; uncomputed and freed.
; Kept: the user register x of each function; r (rotated by the angle rail, measured) in theta_angle_select and
; shared_angle_select.
; Rotations: phi_angle_select: (Ry, x, th, 1); (P, A, val(A), 1) with A = select(x > k, a, b). theta_angle_select:
; (Ry, x, th, 1); (Ry, r, val(A), 1) with A = select(x > k, a, b). nested_angle_select: (Ry, x, th, 1); (P, A, val(A), 1)
; with A = select(x > k1, a, select(x > k2, b, c)). shared_angle_select: (Ry, x, th, 1); (P, A, val(A), 1);
; (Ry, r, val(A), 1) with the one A = select(x > k, a, b).
; An ANGLE SELECT is a QUANTUM ANGLE (rule 11): the angle depends on a quantum flag, so it is computed into an f64 rail
; by the ordinary select template (rule 9; the arms a, b, c are runtime-classical doubles, so cq_template_select_f64_ll,
; and a select of selects nests: the inner select's rail is the else arm of the outer one, select_f64_lh), and ONE
; primitive consumes the rail (rule 15): cqrt_rz_qangle(A) for cq_phi (register-free; no quantum predicate is in scope,
; so the phase e^{i val(A)} lands on each branch of A and stays on the branches of x when A and the flag are
; uncomputed) and
; cqrt_ry_i32_qangle(r, A) for cq_theta on the seeded register r. The compiler never expands the select into per-arm
; controlled rotations; the N-bit ladder is the backend's. One select read by two consumers (shared_angle_select) is
; one angle rail read by both primitives and uncomputed once, after the second. Each angle chain is uncomputed LIFO and
; freed (rule 5), then the flags.

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"

define i32 @phi_angle_select(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2, double noundef %3, double noundef %4) {
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]

  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %6, i32 %2)    ; IR: %7 = icmp sgt i32 %6, %2  [the select's flag]
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_select_f64_ll(i32 %7, double %3, double %4)    ; IR: %8 = select i1 %7, double %3, double %4  [angle rail A]
  call void @cqrt_rz_qangle(i32 %8)    ; IR: cq_phi(%8)  [phase e^{i val(A)}, no quantum predicate in scope]
  call void @cq_template_select_f64_ll_unc(i32 %8, i32 %7, double %3, double %4)    ; IR: uncompute %8

  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %7, double %1)    ; IR: %7 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %7, i32 %2)    ; IR: %8 = icmp sgt i32 %7, %2  [the select's flag]
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_select_f64_ll(i32 %8, double %4, double %5)    ; IR: %9 = select i1 %8, double %4, double %5  [angle rail A]
  %10 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %3)    ; IR: %10 = cq_theta_si32(%3, %9)  [register r, seeded with r0]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32_qangle(i32 %10, i32 %9)    ; IR: %10 = cq_theta_si32(%3, %9)  [Ry(val(A)) on r]
  call void @cq_template_select_f64_ll_unc(i32 %9, i32 %8, double %4, double %5)    ; IR: uncompute %9
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %9)    ; IR: release the angle rail (|0>)

}

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %10)    ; IR: release the %10 rail (|0>)

name: 133_state_prep_overwrite
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 10, 8, 12, 5, 2.
; Checked: r + x in each function (measured).
; Clean: every predicate flag (x == k; x > k; x > k1, x < k2) and prep_twice's conjunction flag.
; Kept: the user register x of each function; r (prepared in place under control, frozen, measured).
; Rotations: prep_const_incoming: Ry(th) on x; Ry(t) on r under (x == k), after xorc(7) on r under the same flag.
; prep_beside_phase: Ry(th) on x; Ry(t) on r under (x > k) after xorc(r0) under the same flag; P(p) on NOT (x > k).
; prep_twice: Ry(th) on x; Ry(t1) on r under (x > k1) after xorc(r0) under it; Ry(-t1) on r under (x > k1) & (x < k2),
; then xorc(r0) on r under the same conjunction; xorc(r0) on r under (x < k2); Ry(t2) on r under (x < k2).
; A STATE PREP under a quantum condition is a controlled Ry on the variable's own rail (39, rule 10); when the arm first
; RESETS the variable (r = 0) and the straight-through value is something else (7, r0, or an earlier prep), the reset
; is a controlled XOR with the value the rail holds there: cqrt_xorc_<W>_controlled(flag, r, v) takes r from v to 0
; exactly where the arm runs, and the controlled Ry follows. No second rail, no merge copy. A phase in the other arm is
; the kickback under NOT the flag (39/21). OVERWRITING a register that an earlier arm may have prepared: where both
; conditions hold the earlier prep must be undone first, by its own adjoint under the conjunction flag (Ry(-t1), then
; the XOR back to r0); then the rail is r0 under the second flag and the second prep proceeds. The adjoint is sound
; because nothing read r between the two preps (a live reader would have entangled it; then the register is not dead
; and the program is 38/66's shape instead).
source_filename = "state_prep_overwrite.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

define i32 @prep_const_incoming(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2, double noundef %3) {
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %5, double %1)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %5, i32 %2)    ; IR: %6 = icmp eq i32 %5, %2  [path predicate of block %7]
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 7)    ; IR: %10 = phi i32 [ %8, %7 ], [ 7, %4 ]  [register r, starts as the straight-through 7]
  call void @cqrt_xorc_i32_controlled(i32 %6, i32 %7, i32 7)    ; IR: block %7: r = 0 (the prep seed) where the arm runs: 7 -> 0 under the flag
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32_controlled(i32 %6, i32 %7, double %3)    ; IR: block %7: %8 = cq_theta_si32(0, %3)  [Ry under the predicate]
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl_unc(i32 %6, i32 %5, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %6
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release the %6 rail (|0>)
  %8 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %7)    ; IR: %11 = cq_measure_si32(%10)
  %9 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %5)    ; IR: %12 = cq_measure_si32(%5)
  %10 = add nsw i32 %9, %8    ; IR: %13 = add nsw i32 %12, %11  (classical)
  ret i32 %10    ; IR: ret i32 %13
}

define i32 @prep_beside_phase(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2, i32 noundef %3, double noundef %4, double noundef %5) {
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %7 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %7, double %1)    ; IR: %7 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %7, i32 %2)    ; IR: %8 = icmp sgt i32 %7, %2  [path predicate of %9; its negation is the predicate of %11]
  %9 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %3)    ; IR: %13 = phi i32 [ %10, %9 ], [ %3, %11 ]  [register r, starts as %3]
  call void @cqrt_xorc_i32_controlled(i32 %8, i32 %9, i32 %3)    ; IR: block %9: r = 0 where the arm runs: %3 -> 0 under the flag
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32_controlled(i32 %8, i32 %9, double %4)    ; IR: block %9: %10 = cq_theta_si32(0, %4)  [Ry under the predicate]

name: 136_callee_measure
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 18, 2, 4, 5.
; Checked: m + cq_measure(y), m = max(cq_measure(x), k) returned classically by the callee, y = x + c (y is a classical
; read by rule 2; its value is witnessed by the output).
; Clean: the y rail (%6): computed before x's measurement, it collapses with it (rule 2) and is uncomputed at the collapse
; point against x's rail, which holds the outcome; then freed.
; Kept: the user register x (measured inside the clone, never freed).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x.
; Classical reads (rule 2): 1 (cq_measure(y): y is classical after x's measurement, no gate).
; A callee that MEASURES its quantum argument is not a pure function and has no _unc twin (rule 18): its clone measures
; the handle where the source measures the value, and from there on the callee is classical (the smax is classical
; arithmetic on the outcome). The clone returns the classical int, not a handle, so the caller's call result is
; classical: nothing to copy out, nothing to uncompute. The measurement is the user's: it collapses x and, through
; y = x + c, the entangled y.
; CLASSICAL COLLAPSE (rule 2, ruling 2026-10-29): y's only quantum source is x, and x is measured when the clone returns,
; so y is classical from there on although its rail was computed before the measurement. The clone returns smax(m, k),
; not m, so the caller RE-READS x's rail (cqrt_measure_i32 on a measured rail is a classical re-read of the outcome, not
; a measurement: rule 2, ABI 1.3; the backend logs no event), uncomputes y against that rail (which still holds m) and
; recomputes y = m + c by a classical add. The user's cq_measure(y) is a classical read and emits no gate. The argument
; rail is consumed by the measurement and is never freed.
source_filename = "callee_measure.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

define i32 @callee_measure(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2, i32 noundef %3) {
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %5, double %1)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %5, i32 %3)    ; IR: %6 = add nsw i32 %5, %3  [y, entangled with x]
  %7 = call fastcc i32 @__cq_q_readout_10(i32 %5, i32 %2)    ; IR: %7 = call @readout(%5, %2), quantum clone (arg 0 quantum): measures x inside, returns a CLASSICAL int

  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %6, i32 %5, i32 %3)    ; IR: rule 2 collapse of y: its only quantum source is measured; %5 holds m
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release the y rail (|0>)

  %10 = add nsw i32 %9, %7    ; IR: %9 = add nsw i32 %8, %7  (classical)

; old acc %19 and EVERY predicate a_j, the inner chain's last a_{m-1} included), popped and uncomputed by the nested
; reverse loop; each outer trip's |1> seed (%16) and the |0> seed of acc (%7), never written and freed directly.
; Kept: x (%6, the rotated register) and the measured result rail. No predicate is kept: both bounds are classical, so
; every predicate is a function of the inputs and the mirror uncomputes it (rule 14, classical bound with a quantum exit).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; 27's nested rolled loops composed with 26's quantum break, the break confined to the INNER loop. -O1 tests the break
; after the body and folds it with the classical exit into `select i1 %22, i1 %24, i1 false`; the classical half keeps
; the inner loop a classical loop over all m trips, the quantum half is the trip predicate: inner trip j of outer trip i
; runs iff a_{j-1} (no break before it in THIS inner loop), u_j = acc_{j-1} + (x ^ (i + j)) is computed unguarded
; (pure), the break flag is e_j = u_j > lim, the carried value is acc_j = a_{j-1} ? u_j : acc_{j-1}, and
; a_j = a_{j-1} AND NOT e_j. Each outer trip starts a fresh predicate chain (a_{-1} = |1>): the break resets with the
; inner loop, the outer loop continues. Every trip's rails are pushed and the nested reverse loop pops them (27). If
; n <= 0 or m <= 0 no inner trip ever runs: one classical edge, acc is the seed rail. Both bounds are classical: no K.

; predicate a_{m-1} (%26 of inner trip m-1, pushed by block %29 and popped as %37 = %42 of the first inner reverse trip),

; (%5 -> %6), fneg_q's -x (%4 -> %6), each the function's measured return.
; Clean: fneg_q: the old x rail (%3, rule 6: |0> after the copy) and t = -(-x) (%5), both freed.
; Kept: the rotated f64 register(s) of the other functions (FP arithmetic has no inverse) and every measured result rail.

; is one cq_template_<op>_f64 into a fresh rail. A classical operand is a literal: the handle-first form is _hl (x + c)
; and the classical-first form is _lh (c / x, where the order is not commutative); a quantum-quantum op takes two handles.

name: 140_nonreconverging_returns
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 10, 8, 2 (measurement in arms; classical collapse), 5.
; Checked: x (%7 -> %10, measured once; the returned int is x or x + 1 by the classical re-derivation of which arm ran).
; Clean: the condition flag x > k (%8), uncomputed before the measurement and freed.
; Kept: x (%7, the rotated register, measured) and r (%9, rotated by a different angle in each arm and never measured:
; frozen, never reverse-played, never freed).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1); (Ry, r, t1, x > k); (Ry, r, t2, NOT (x > k)).
; The source has two return arms that never meet; at -O1 clang merges every return, so the IR reconverges in a phi of
; the two MEASURED values (%17) under the quantum condition. What remains to lower: the dead register r is rotated by a
; different angle in each arm (the controlled Ry of 39 and its NOT-bracketed twin) and never measured, so it stays
; allocated (frozen). Both arms measure x at the same point, so by rule 2 the two cq_measure calls are ONE unconditional
; measurement of x (the second a classical re-read). The merge phi %17 is then decided by rule 2's CLASSICAL COLLAPSE:
; its condition %8 = (x > k) is computed only from the measured rail x and the classical k, so it is classical. Its rail
; is uncomputed while x still holds the outcome's source state (here before the measurement, right after the last
; controlled Ry it guards), the condition is recomputed from the outcome by an ordinary `icmp sgt` (%11), and the merge
; is a classical `select` (%13); no quantum mux and no select template. No measurement is inserted: the user measures x
; in both arms, and that one measurement decides the return.
source_filename = "nonreconverging_returns.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

define i32 @nonreconverging_returns(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2, i32 noundef %3, double noundef %4, double noundef %5) {

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 18, 9, 15, 2, 10, 5.
; Checked: call_result_as_target's y (the clone's result rail %8 -> %9) and x (%7 -> %10); call_result_as_theta_angle's r
; (%10 -> %11) and x (%6 -> %12); call_result_as_phi_angle's x (%5 -> %9), all measured.
; Clean: every clone-internal rail; call_result_as_theta_angle's and call_result_as_phi_angle's clone result v (%7; %6,
; zeroed by the _unc twin), its uitofp (%8; %7) and the angle register A = fl(s * v) (%9; %8), all freed.
; Kept: x in each function (the rotated register, measured); call_result_as_target's y (%8, rotated in place, frozen,
; measured); call_result_as_theta_angle's r (%10, rotated by the angle rail, frozen, measured).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1); (Ry, y = pick(x, k, a, b), t, 1) in call_result_as_target; (Ry, x, th, 1);
; (Ry, r, val(A), 1) with A = fl(s * pick8(x, k)) in call_result_as_theta_angle; (Ry, x, th, 1); (P, A, val(A), 1) with
; the same A in call_result_as_phi_angle.
; call_result_as_target: the lifted clone __cq_q_pick_1000 (mask left to right, §1.4) hoists both arms, merges them by
; ONE cq_template_select_i32 on the compare flag (rule 9), copies the merge out as the result rail and uncomputes the
; merge and its operands; the caller's second cq_theta is then a plain Ry on the RESULT RAIL: no alloc (the register
; exists), and y is frozen afterwards (rule 10). A QUANTUM-VALUED ANGLE (rule 15, as 79): the angle s * v is computed
; into an f64 REGISTER by ordinary templates (uitofp of the clone's result, fmul_hl by the classical s: the program's
; IEEE double, bit-exact), and the rotation is ONE gate primitive reading that register: cqrt_ry_i32_qangle(r, A) for
; cq_theta, cqrt_rz_qangle(A) for cq_phi (a relative phase, kicked back onto the sources by A's uncompute). The backend
; supplies the N-bit ladder; the IR never spells it. The angle register is only read, so the LIFO spine uncomputes it,
; then the clone's _unc twin (__cq_q_pick8_10_unc) zeroes the result rail as in 07. (Laddering the integer result
; directly, s*2^k per bit, would realize s*v over the reals, not the rounded double fl(s*v).)

  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %7, double %1)    ; IR: %7 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %8 = call fastcc i32 @__cq_q_pick_1000(i32 %7, i32 %2, i32 %3, i32 %4)    ; IR: %8 = call @pick(%7, %2, %3, %4), quantum clone (arg 0 quantum): y
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %8, double %5)    ; IR: %9 = cq_theta_si32(%8, %5): Ry on the result rail itself (no alloc, the register exists)
  %9 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %8)    ; IR: %10 = cq_measure_si32(%9)
  %10 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %7)    ; IR: %11 = cq_measure_si32(%7)

  %9 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: ret i32 %8  [result rail of the call]
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %8, i32 %9)    ; IR: copy the result out
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %8, i32 %7, i32 %5, i32 %6)    ; IR: uncompute the merge
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %8)    ; IR: release the merge rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %7, i32 %0, i32 %1)    ; IR: uncompute %5
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release the %5 rail (|0>)

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release the %7 rail (|0>)

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %5)    ; IR: release the %6 rail (|0>)
  ret i32 %9    ; IR: ret i32 %8
}

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 14 (classical bound; quantum-dependent exit with cutoff K), 9, 8, 7, 6, 5.
; Checked: continue_classical_bound: acc + x (measured); continue_kloop: s + x (measured: s is the carried rail s_K,
; %21 -> %44, rule 6 leaves it the only s rail; x is the copied-out x_K, %29 -> %45).
; Clean: every trip rail of continue_classical_bound; in continue_kloop every x-chain trip rail (the exit test, x - 1, its
; parity, the skip flag, the all-literal select and the next-x select), every trip predicate (the K-th included) and the
; after-trip-K exit test (%27, uncomputed at once); the OLD s of every trip of continue_kloop (rule 6, in the body:
; s' = a ? s + sel : s is a bijection in s for every (a, sel) and the trip predicate does not read s, so the arm's garbage
; s + sel is uncomputed first and t = a ? s' - sel : s' is copied onto the old s, uncomputed and both freed; trip 0's old s
; is the |0> incoming %6). continue_classical_bound's acc seed and continue_kloop's |1> seed are freed directly (rule 7).
; Kept: continue_kloop's a_K (%28: the exit test x_K > k evaluated after the K-th body, ANDed with trip K's predicate;
; rule 14: a_K = 1 iff the loop would run a (K+1)-th trip, which is observable; a loop that exits after exactly K trips
; reads 0); continue_kloop's s_K (%21, measured) and its copied-out x_K (%29, measured). continue_classical_bound keeps
; nothing: acc = acc * c + i is no bijection in acc (c may be even), so rule 6 does not apply there and its acc chain is
; reversed. The user register x stays allocated in both.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, tx, 1) in each function.
; continue_classical_bound: the bound is classical, so the loop stays a classical loop with no predicate chain (131). -O1
; folds the quantum `continue` into `select e, acc, acc*c + i`: the skip flag e = (x == i + k) is a flag rail per trip and
; the carried acc advances by one select (rule 9: the skipped arm is the old acc itself). Each trip pushes its rails;
; after the result is copied out a reverse loop pops and uncomputes every trip LIFO; the acc seed is freed directly (7).
; continue_kloop: the exit depends on x, so the loop is re-rolled to K = 4 trips under the chain a_j = a_{j-1} & (x_j > k)
; (the pre-header guard is trip 0's test). -O1 folds the `continue` into a select too, so the skip never reaches the
; chain: it is the all-literal select (c or 0) added to s; both carried values advance by a select on a_j. The exit value
; of x is the carried x_K: -O1's phi spells it as the literal k (SCEV: an unsigned x decremented by 1 from above k leaves
; the loop exactly at k), which the carried rail equals on every branch where the loop has exited (a_K = 0). x_K is
; copied out (alloc + copy) before the mirror, which reverses the x chain; the user register x stays allocated. After the
; K-th trip the exit test is evaluated once more on x_K and a_K = (predicate of trip K) & (x_K > k) is kept (rule 14);
; the test is uncomputed at once and the mirror uncomputes every trip predicate, the K-th included.
; RULE 6 IN A ROLLED LOOP (2026-10-31, as 05): a carried value whose trip update is a bijection and whose trip predicate
; does not read it (s here: s' = a ? s + sel : s, sel = (x - 1) & 1 == 0 ? c : 0 reads x, not s) is cleaned in the body
; of the same trip: the arm's garbage s + sel is uncomputed first (its _unc reads the old s), then t = a ? s' - sel : s'
; is computed fresh, copied onto the old s, uncomputed and freed, and the old s is freed. The new rail is the only s
; rail that survives, it is not pushed, the reverse loop never sees it, and no copy-out is needed (the measurement reads
; s_K). The carried x cannot be cleaned: the exit test reads it, and x = k and x = k + 1 both leave `x -= 1 under x > k`
; at k, so that update is not injective; its chain is pushed and reversed as before (05, 54, 68).

define i32 @continue_classical_bound(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2, i32 noundef %3, i32 noundef %4) {
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %6, double %1)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: incoming 0 of phi %15 / %9  [acc before trip 0]
  %8 = icmp sgt i32 %2, 0    ; IR: %7 = icmp sgt i32 %2, 0  (classical)
  br i1 %8, label %13, label %9    ; IR: br i1 %7, label %13, label %8

9:
  %10 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %7)    ; IR: %10 = cq_measure_si32(%9), %9 = 0 from %5
  %11 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %6)    ; IR: %11 = cq_measure_si32(%6)
  %12 = add nsw i32 %11, %10    ; IR: %12 = add nsw i32 %11, %10  (classical)
  ret i32 %12    ; IR: ret i32 %12

13:
  %14 = phi i32 [ 0, %5 ], [ %21, %13 ]    ; IR: %14 = phi i32 [ %21, %13 ], [ 0, %5 ]  (classical)
  %15 = phi i32 [ %7, %5 ], [ %20, %13 ]    ; IR: %15 = phi i32 [ %20, %13 ], [ 0, %5 ]  [carried acc]
  %16 = add nsw i32 %14, %3    ; IR: %16 = add nsw i32 %14, %3  (classical)
  %17 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %6, i32 %16)    ; IR: %17 = icmp eq i32 %6, %16  [the continue flag]
  %18 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i32_hl(i32 %15, i32 %4)    ; IR: %18 = mul nsw i32 %15, %4
  %19 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %18, i32 %14)    ; IR: %19 = add nsw i32 %18, %14
  %20 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %17, i32 %15, i32 %19)    ; IR: %20 = select i1 %17, i32 %15, i32 %19  [next acc: the continue keeps the old acc]
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %15)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %17)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %18)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %19)
  %21 = add nuw nsw i32 %14, 1    ; IR: %21 = add nuw nsw i32 %14, 1  (classical)
  %22 = icmp eq i32 %21, %2    ; IR: %22 = icmp eq i32 %21, %2  (classical)
  br i1 %22, label %23, label %13    ; IR: br i1 %22, label %8, label %13

23:
  %24 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: %9 = phi i32 [ %20, %13 ]  [copied-out result]
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %20, i32 %24)    ; IR: %9
  br label %25

25:
  %26 = phi i32 [ %14, %23 ], [ %33, %25 ]    ; IR: trip being undone, from the last down to 0 (its classical i)
  %27 = phi i32 [ %20, %23 ], [ %31, %25 ]    ; IR: %20 of this trip
  %28 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %29 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %30 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %31 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %32 = add nsw i32 %26, %3    ; IR: %16 of that trip (classical)
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %27, i32 %30, i32 %31, i32 %28)    ; IR: uncompute %20
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %27)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %28, i32 %29, i32 %26)    ; IR: uncompute %19
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %28)    ; IR: release the %19 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_mul_i32_hl_unc(i32 %29, i32 %31, i32 %4)    ; IR: uncompute %18
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %29)    ; IR: release the %18 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl_unc(i32 %30, i32 %6, i32 %32)    ; IR: uncompute %17
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %30)    ; IR: release the %17 rail (|0>)
  %33 = add nsw i32 %26, -1
  %34 = icmp sge i32 %33, 0    ; IR: trips n-1 down to 0
  br i1 %34, label %25, label %35

35:
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %31)    ; IR: release incoming 0 of phi %15 directly (rule 7: never written, |0>)
  %36 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %24)    ; IR: %10 = cq_measure_si32(%9)
  %37 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %6)    ; IR: %11 = cq_measure_si32(%6)
  %38 = add nsw i32 %37, %36    ; IR: %12 = add nsw i32 %11, %10  (classical)
  ret i32 %38    ; IR: ret i32 %12
}

define i32 @continue_kloop(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2, i32 noundef %3) {
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %5, double %1)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: incoming 0 of phi %8 / %18  [s before trip 0: trip 0's old s, cleaned by rule 6 in the body]
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 true)    ; IR: predicate of reaching the loop guard in %4 (always 1)
  br label %8

8:
  %9 = phi i32 [ 0, %4 ], [ %24, %8 ]    ; IR: trip index, bounded by K  [K]
  %10 = phi i32 [ %5, %4 ], [ %20, %8 ]    ; IR: %9 = phi i32 [ %10, %7 ], [ %5, %4 ]
  %11 = phi i32 [ %6, %4 ], [ %21, %8 ]    ; IR: %8 = phi i32 [ %14, %7 ], [ 0, %4 ]
  %12 = phi i32 [ %7, %4 ], [ %14, %8 ]    ; IR: predicate of reaching this trip's test
  %13 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_ugt_i32_hl(i32 %10, i32 %2)    ; IR: %6 = icmp ugt i32 %5, %2 (trip 0) / %15 = icmp ugt i32 %10, %2
  %14 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: predicate of this trip
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %12, i32 %13, i32 %14)    ; IR: br i1 %6 (trip 0) / br i1 %15 taken: a_j = a_{j-1} & cond_j
  %15 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %10, i32 -1)    ; IR: %10 = add i32 %9, -1
  %16 = call i32 @cq_template_and_i32_hl(i32 %15, i32 1)    ; IR: %11 = and i32 %10, 1
  %17 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %16, i32 0)    ; IR: %12 = icmp eq i32 %11, 0  [the continue, folded by -O1 into the select below]
  %18 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_ll(i32 %17, i32 %3, i32 0)    ; IR: %13 = select i1 %12, i32 %3, i32 0  (both arms classical: _ll)
  %19 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32(i32 %18, i32 %11)    ; IR: %14 = add i32 %13, %8  [the arm's garbage: s + sel]
  %20 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %14, i32 %15, i32 %10)    ; IR: next %9 = a ? %10 : %9
  %21 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %14, i32 %19, i32 %11)    ; IR: next %8 / %18 = a ? %14 : %8  [s_{j+1}: the only s rail after this trip]
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_unc(i32 %19, i32 %18, i32 %11)    ; IR: rule 6: the arm's garbage %14 is uncomputed first (its _unc reads the old s)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %19)    ; IR: release %14 (|0>)
  %22 = call i32 @cq_template_sub_i32(i32 %21, i32 %18)    ; IR: rule 6: s' - sel
  %23 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %14, i32 %22, i32 %21)    ; IR: rule 6: t = a ? s' - sel : s' recomputes the old s (the composite update s' = s + a * sel is a bijection in s)
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %23, i32 %11)    ; IR: rule 6: old s ^= t: |0> (trip 0: the |0> incoming %6, unchanged)
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %23, i32 %14, i32 %22, i32 %21)    ; IR: rule 6: uncompute t
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %23)    ; IR: release t (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_sub_i32_unc(i32 %22, i32 %21, i32 %18)    ; IR: rule 6: uncompute s' - sel
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %22)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %11)    ; IR: rule 6: release the old s rail (|0> after the copy); it is not pushed
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %10)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %12)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %13)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %15)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %16)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %17)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %18)
  %24 = add nuw nsw i32 %9, 1
  %25 = icmp ult i32 %24, 4    ; IR: K-bounded br i1 %15, label %7, label %16  [K]
  br i1 %25, label %8, label %26

26:
  %27 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_ugt_i32_hl(i32 %20, i32 %2)    ; IR: %15 = icmp ugt i32 %10, %2 after trip K: the exit test that would admit a (K+1)-th trip
  %28 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: a_K = predicate of trip K & that test  [output rail, kept]
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %14, i32 %27, i32 %28)    ; IR: br i1 %15 taken once more (rule 14)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_ugt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %27, i32 %20, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute that test
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %27)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  %29 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: %17 = phi i32 [ %5, %4 ], [ %2, %7 ]  [copied-out x: the carried x_K, which is the literal k wherever the loop has exited]
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %20, i32 %29)    ; IR: %17
  br label %30

30:
  %31 = phi i32 [ 0, %26 ], [ %41, %30 ]    ; IR: reverse trip index
  %32 = phi i32 [ %20, %26 ], [ %40, %30 ]    ; IR: %9 written by this trip
  %33 = phi i32 [ %14, %26 ], [ %39, %30 ]    ; IR: predicate of this trip
  %34 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %35 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %36 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %37 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %38 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %39 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %40 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %32, i32 %33, i32 %37, i32 %40)    ; IR: uncompute next %9
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %32)    ; IR: release next %9 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_ll_unc(i32 %34, i32 %35, i32 %3, i32 0)    ; IR: uncompute %13
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %34)    ; IR: release %13 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl_unc(i32 %35, i32 %36, i32 0)    ; IR: uncompute %12
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %35)    ; IR: release %12 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_and_i32_hl_unc(i32 %36, i32 %37, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %11
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %36)    ; IR: release %11 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %37, i32 %40, i32 -1)    ; IR: uncompute %10
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %37)    ; IR: release %10 (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %39, i32 %38, i32 %33)    ; IR: uncompute the predicate of this trip (every trip 1..K; a_K is a separate rail)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %33)    ; IR: release the predicate (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_ugt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %38, i32 %40, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %6 / %15
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %38)    ; IR: release %6 / %15 (|0>)
  %41 = add nuw nsw i32 %31, 1
  %42 = icmp ult i32 %41, 4    ; IR: K  [K]
  br i1 %42, label %30, label %43

43:
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %39)    ; IR: release the |1> seed directly (rule 7: known basis state)
  %44 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %21)    ; IR: %19 = cq_measure_ui32(%18)  [s_K, the carried rail: rule 6 left no other s rail, so no copy-out]
  %45 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %29)    ; IR: %20 = cq_measure_ui32(%17)
  %46 = add i32 %45, %44    ; IR: %21 = add i32 %20, %19  (classical)
  ret i32 %46    ; IR: ret i32 %21
}

name: 14_fmuladd
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 1, 2, 4, 5.
; Checked: fmuladd_qcc's x * a + b (%6 -> %7) and fmuladd_qqq's x * y + z (%10 -> %11), each the function's measured
; return.
; Clean: each function's product rail (x * a; x * y), uncomputed by its fmul _unc after the fadd read it, then freed.
; Kept: each function's rotated f64 register(s) (%5; %7, %8, %9) and its measured result rail.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1) in fmuladd_qcc; (Ry, x, tx, 1); (Ry, y, ty, 1); (Ry, z, tz, 1) in fmuladd_qqq.
; clang contracts `x * a + b` into one llvm.fmuladd.f64 at -O1. llvm.fmuladd is UNFUSED (§2): the x86-64 baseline has
; no FMA unit, so the classical program rounds twice, and the lowering is an fmul into a fresh product rail, then an
; fadd of that product into a fresh result rail (rule 4, each out of place); only a genuine llvm.fma is one fused
; template. The product rail is garbage: its fmul _unc returns it to |0> once the fadd has read it (rule 5), and it is
; freed. The measurement is the sink.
source_filename = "fmuladd.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

; Function Attrs: nounwind ssp uwtable
define double @fmuladd_qcc(double noundef %0, double noundef %1, double noundef %2, double noundef %3) local_unnamed_addr #0 {
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_f64(double %0)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_f64(%0, %1)  [register]
  call void @cqrt_ry_f64(i32 %5, double %1)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_f64(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_fmul_f64_hl(i32 %5, double %2)    ; IR: %6 = tail call double @llvm.fmuladd.f64(double %5, double %2, double %3)  [product x * a]
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f64_hl(i32 %6, double %3)    ; IR: %6 = tail call double @llvm.fmuladd.f64(double %5, double %2, double %3)  [sum + b]
  call void @cq_template_fmul_f64_hl_unc(i32 %6, i32 %5, double %2)    ; IR: %6 [uncompute the product rail]
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: %6 [free the product rail]
  %8 = call double @cqrt_measure_f64(i32 %7)    ; IR: %7 = cq_measure_f64(%6)
  ret double %8    ; IR: ret double %7
}

; Function Attrs: nocallback nofree nosync nounwind speculatable willreturn memory(none)
declare double @llvm.fmuladd.f64(double, double, double) #1

; Function Attrs: nounwind ssp uwtable
define double @fmuladd_qqq(double noundef %0, double noundef %1, double noundef %2, double noundef %3, double noundef %4, double noundef %5) local_unnamed_addr #0 {
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_f64(double %0)    ; IR: %7 = cq_theta_f64(%0, %3)  [register]
  call void @cqrt_ry_f64(i32 %7, double %3)    ; IR: %7 = cq_theta_f64(%0, %3)  [Ry]
  %8 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_f64(double %1)    ; IR: %8 = cq_theta_f64(%1, %4)  [register]
  call void @cqrt_ry_f64(i32 %8, double %4)    ; IR: %8 = cq_theta_f64(%1, %4)  [Ry]
  %9 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_f64(double %2)    ; IR: %9 = cq_theta_f64(%2, %5)  [register]
  call void @cqrt_ry_f64(i32 %9, double %5)    ; IR: %9 = cq_theta_f64(%2, %5)  [Ry]
  %10 = call i32 @cq_template_fmul_f64(i32 %7, i32 %8)    ; IR: %10 = tail call double @llvm.fmuladd.f64(double %7, double %8, double %9)  [product x * y]
  %11 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f64(i32 %10, i32 %9)    ; IR: %10 = tail call double @llvm.fmuladd.f64(double %7, double %8, double %9)  [sum + z]
  call void @cq_template_fmul_f64_unc(i32 %10, i32 %7, i32 %8)    ; IR: %10 [uncompute the product rail]
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %10)    ; IR: %10 [free the product rail]
  %12 = call double @cqrt_measure_f64(i32 %11)    ; IR: %11 = cq_measure_f64(%10)
  ret double %12    ; IR: ret double %11
}

declare i32 @cqrt_alloc_f64(double)

name: 150_do_while_quantum
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 14 (quantum-dependent exit, cutoff K), 9, 6, 7, 5.
; Checked: x + n (measured: x as the copied-out x_K, %26 -> %42; n as the carried rail n_K, %18 -> %43, measured directly
; because rule 6 leaves it the only n rail).
; Clean: every x-chain trip rail except a_K (the products, sums, next-x selects, the tests and the predicates a_1..a_{K-1}),
; popped and uncomputed by the reverse loop; the |1> seed is freed directly; the OLD n of every trip (rule 6, in the body:
; n' = a ? n + 1 : n is a bijection in n for every a and the trip predicate reads x, never n, so the arm's garbage n + 1 is
; uncomputed first and t = a ? n' - 1 : n' is copied onto the old n, uncomputed and both freed; trip 0's old n is the |0>
; incoming %7, and trip 0's predicate is the |1> seed, so there t = n' - 1 = 0).
; Kept: a_K, the predicate computed by the last trip's test (the first rail popped by the reverse loop; rule 14: a_K
; = 1 means a fifth body would have run, which is observable). The user register x (%6) stays allocated: x = x * a + b is
; no bijection in x (a may be even) and the exit test reads x, so rule 6 does not apply and the x chain is pushed and
; reversed (x_K is copied out for the measurement).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, tx, 1).
; A do-while: the body runs before the test, so trip 0's body is unconditional (its predicate is the |1> seed) and the
; test at the END of trip j produces the predicate of trip j+1: a_{j+1} = a_j & (x_{j+1} > k), on the CARRIED value
; (where the loop has already exited the carried x is frozen and a_j = 0 absorbs the test). The loop is re-rolled to K = 4
; bodies and K tests; both carried values advance by a select on a_j (rule 9). Each trip pushes its x-chain rails; x_K is
; copied out (alloc + copy) and a reverse loop pops and uncomputes every trip LIFO, skipping a_K on its first
; iteration. RULE 6 IN A ROLLED LOOP (2026-10-31, as in 05): a carried value whose trip update is a bijection and whose
; trip predicate does not read it (n here) is cleaned in the body of the same trip: the new rail is the only one that
; survives, it is not pushed, the reverse loop never sees it, and no copy-out is needed (the measurement reads n_K). The
; do-while changes nothing: trip 0's clean-up is the same code under the |1> seed. A carried value the exit test reads (x)
; cannot be cleaned: x = k and x = k + 1 both leave `x -= 1 under x > k` at k, so that update is not injective (05, 149,
; 54, 68).
source_filename = "do_while_quantum.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

define i32 @do_while_quantum(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2, i32 noundef %3, i32 noundef %4) {
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %6, double %1)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: incoming 0 of phi %9  [n before trip 0: trip 0's old n, freed by rule 6 in the body]
  %8 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 true)    ; IR: predicate of trip 0's body (a do-while body runs unconditionally once)
  br label %9

9:
  %10 = phi i32 [ 0, %5 ], [ %23, %9 ]    ; IR: trip index, bounded by K  [K]
  %11 = phi i32 [ %6, %5 ], [ %17, %9 ]    ; IR: %8 = phi i32 [ %6, %5 ], [ %11, %7 ]
  %12 = phi i32 [ %7, %5 ], [ %18, %9 ]    ; IR: %9 = phi i32 [ 0, %5 ], [ %12, %7 ]
  %13 = phi i32 [ %8, %5 ], [ %22, %9 ]    ; IR: predicate of this trip's body
  %14 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i32_hl(i32 %11, i32 %2)    ; IR: %10 = mul nsw i32 %8, %2
  %15 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %14, i32 %3)    ; IR: %11 = add nsw i32 %10, %3
  %16 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %12, i32 1)    ; IR: %12 = add nuw nsw i32 %9, 1
  %17 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %13, i32 %15, i32 %11)    ; IR: next %8 = a ? %11 : %8
  %18 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %13, i32 %16, i32 %12)    ; IR: next %9 = a ? %12 : %9  [n_{j+1}: the only n rail after this trip]
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %16, i32 %12, i32 1)    ; IR: rule 6: the arm's garbage %12 is uncomputed first (its _unc reads the old n)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %16)    ; IR: release %12 (|0>)
  %19 = call i32 @cq_template_sub_i32_hl(i32 %18, i32 1)    ; IR: rule 6: n' - 1
  %20 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %13, i32 %19, i32 %18)    ; IR: rule 6: t = a ? n' - 1 : n' recomputes the old n (the composite update n' = n + a is a bijection in n)
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %20, i32 %12)    ; IR: rule 6: old n ^= t: |0> (trip 0: the |0> incoming %7, unchanged; its predicate is the |1> seed, so t = n' - 1 = 0)
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %20, i32 %13, i32 %19, i32 %18)    ; IR: rule 6: uncompute t
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %20)    ; IR: release t (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_sub_i32_hl_unc(i32 %19, i32 %18, i32 1)    ; IR: rule 6: uncompute n' - 1
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %19)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %12)    ; IR: rule 6: release the old n rail (|0> after the copy); it is not pushed
  %21 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %17, i32 %4)    ; IR: %13 = icmp sgt i32 %11, %4  (on the carried x)
  %22 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: predicate of the next trip's body
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %13, i32 %21, i32 %22)    ; IR: br i1 %13 taken: a_{j+1} = a_j & cond
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %11)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %13)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %14)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %15)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %21)
  %23 = add nuw nsw i32 %10, 1
  %24 = icmp ult i32 %23, 4    ; IR: K-bounded br i1 %13, label %7, label %14  [K]
  br i1 %24, label %9, label %25

25:
  %26 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: %15 = cq_measure_si32(%11): the carried x  [copied-out result; n needs none: rule 6 left n_K the only n rail]
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %17, i32 %26)    ; IR: %11 of the last trip
  br label %27

27:
  %28 = phi i32 [ 0, %25 ], [ %39, %38 ]    ; IR: reverse trip index
  %29 = phi i32 [ %17, %25 ], [ %35, %38 ]    ; IR: %8 written by this trip
  %30 = phi i32 [ %22, %25 ], [ %34, %38 ]    ; IR: predicate produced by this trip's test
  %31 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %32 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %33 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %34 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %35 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %36 = icmp eq i32 %28, 0    ; IR: reverse index 0 is trip K-1: the predicate its test produced is a_K, the output rail (rule 14)
  br i1 %36, label %38, label %37

  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %34, i32 %31, i32 %30)    ; IR: uncompute the predicate produced by this trip (trips 0..K-2)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %30)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  br label %38

  call void @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %31, i32 %29, i32 %4)    ; IR: uncompute %13
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %31)    ; IR: release %13 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %29, i32 %34, i32 %32, i32 %35)    ; IR: uncompute next %8
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %29)    ; IR: release next %8 (|0>)

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %32)    ; IR: release %11 (|0>)

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 14 (quantum-dependent exit, cutoff K), 8, 9, 7, 5.
; Checked: i (measured).
; Clean: every trip rail, every trip predicate (the K-th included) and the after-trip-K return test; the |1> seed and
; the i seed are freed directly.
; Kept: a_K (%22: the return test x_K == k evaluated after the K-th body, negated and ANDed with trip K's predicate;
; rule 14: a_K = 1 iff the loop would run a (K+1)-th trip, i.e. the return was not taken within K trips nor at the
; test after them, which is observable; a loop whose return is taken at that test reads 0). The user register x stays
; allocated.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, tx, 1).
; `for (;;) { if (x == k) return cq_measure(i); ... }` is a loop whose only exit is the return, tested at the top of each
; trip (-O1: the pre-header `x == k` is trip 0's test, the latch `x/2 == k` the next trip's). It is re-rolled to K = 4 trips
; under the chain a_j = a_{j-1} & NOT(x_j == k): the exit flag is X-bracketed into the Toffoli (rule 8). The returned
; value is the carried i, which the selects on a_j freeze at the trip where the return was taken (rule 9), so the
; fall-through after K trips and every early return read the same copied-out rail. After the K-th trip the return test
; is evaluated once more on x_K and a_K = (predicate of trip K) & NOT(x_K == k) is kept (rule 14); the test is uncomputed
; at once. Each trip pushes its rails; the mirror pops and uncomputes LIFO, every trip predicate included.

  %31 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %32 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %33 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %34 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %27)    ; IR: release next %10 (|0>)

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 14 (quantum-dependent exit, cutoff K), 8, 10, 12, 9, 7, 5.
; Checked: r + x (measured).
; Clean: every trip rail and every trip predicate, the K-th included (the phase-arm flags are uncomputed inside their
; trip); the after-trip-K exit test; the |1> seed is freed directly.
; Kept: a_K (%24: the exit test x_K > k evaluated after the K-th body, ANDed with trip K's predicate; rule 14: a_K = 1
; iff the loop would run a (K+1)-th trip; a loop that exits after exactly K trips reads 0). r is a user register: it
; is rotated in place under a_j every trip and FROZEN (rule 10: never reverse-played, never freed), then measured. The
; user register x stays allocated.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, tx, 1); for each trip j = 0..3: (P, h_j, p, a_j && (x_j & 1) != 0), (Ry, r, t, a_j) where a_j =
; AND_{i<=j} (x_i > k) and x_i = x >> i.
; The loop is 05's K-loop (trip j runs under a_j = a_{j-1} & (x_j > k)) with two gates in its body. The phase arm `if (x & 1)
; cq_phi(p)` is a nested quantum branch inside the trip: its path predicate a_j & NOT(x_j & 1 == 0) is one X-bracketed
; Toffoli into a fresh |0> flag h_j (rule 8; -O1 tests the FALSE edge `== 0`), the phase is a kickback on h_j (rule 12),
; and h_j, the compare and the `and` are uncomputed right after the kickback, inside the trip (rule 5: their sources x_j
; and a_j are unchanged, so no push is needed). The in-place cq_theta(&r, t) under the trip is rule 10:
; cqrt_ry_i32_controlled(a_j, r, t) on the one r rail seeded with the classical 0; nothing reads r, so a_j can still be
; uncomputed afterwards (it reads x only). The carried x advances by a select on a_j; after K trips it is copied out and the
; mirror pops and uncomputes LIFO, every trip predicate included. Before the copy the exit test is evaluated once more
; on x_K and a_K = (predicate of trip K) & (x_K > k) is kept (rule 14); the test is uncomputed at once.
source_filename = "phase_in_kloop.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"

  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %6, double %1)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: incoming 0 of phi %9 / %20  [register r: the classical 0, rotated in place below, frozen]
  %8 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 true)    ; IR: predicate of reaching the loop guard in %5 (always 1)

  %10 = phi i32 [ 0, %5 ], [ %20, %9 ]    ; IR: trip index, bounded by K  [K]
  %11 = phi i32 [ %6, %5 ], [ %19, %9 ]    ; IR: %10 = phi i32 [ %16, %14 ], [ %6, %5 ]
  %12 = phi i32 [ %8, %5 ], [ %14, %9 ]    ; IR: predicate of reaching this trip's test
  %13 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_ugt_i32_hl(i32 %11, i32 %2)    ; IR: %7 = icmp ugt i32 %6, %2 (trip 0) / %17 = icmp ugt i32 %16, %2
  %14 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: predicate of this trip (block %8)
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %12, i32 %13, i32 %14)    ; IR: br i1 %7 / %17 taken: a_j = a_{j-1} & cond_j
  %15 = call i32 @cq_template_and_i32_hl(i32 %11, i32 1)    ; IR: %11 = and i32 %10, 1
  %16 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %15, i32 0)    ; IR: %12 = icmp eq i32 %11, 0  (block %13 is its FALSE edge)
  %17 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: path predicate of block %13 = a_j & NOT %12  [fresh |0> flag]
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %16)    ; IR: bracket: block %13 runs under NOT %12
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %14, i32 %16, i32 %17)    ; IR: br i1 %12 inside the trip, false edge
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %16)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_rz_i1(i32 %17, double %3)    ; IR: block %13: cq_phi(%3)  [kickback on the path predicate]
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %16)    ; IR: bracket

  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %16)    ; IR: bracket

  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl_unc(i32 %16, i32 %15, i32 0)    ; IR: uncompute %12

  call void @cq_template_and_i32_hl_unc(i32 %15, i32 %11, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %11
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %15)    ; IR: release the %11 rail (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32_controlled(i32 %14, i32 %7, double %4)    ; IR: block %14: %15 = cq_theta_si32(%9, %4)  [Ry in place on r under a_j; r frozen]

  %19 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %14, i32 %18, i32 %11)    ; IR: next %10 = a ? %16 : %10
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %11)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %12)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %13)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %18)

  %21 = icmp ult i32 %20, 4    ; IR: K-bounded br i1 %17, label %8, label %18  [K]
  br i1 %21, label %9, label %22

22:
  %23 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_ugt_i32_hl(i32 %19, i32 %2)    ; IR: %17 = icmp ugt i32 %16, %2 after trip K: the exit test that would admit a (K+1)-th trip
  %24 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: a_K = predicate of trip K & that test  [output rail, kept]
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %14, i32 %23, i32 %24)    ; IR: br i1 %17 taken once more (rule 14)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_ugt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %23, i32 %19, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute that test
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %23)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  %25 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: %19 = phi i32 [ %6, %5 ], [ %16, %14 ]  [copied-out result: the carried x]
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %19, i32 %25)    ; IR: %19
  br label %26

26:
  %27 = phi i32 [ 0, %22 ], [ %34, %26 ]    ; IR: reverse trip index
  %28 = phi i32 [ %19, %22 ], [ %33, %26 ]    ; IR: %10 written by this trip
  %29 = phi i32 [ %14, %22 ], [ %32, %26 ]    ; IR: predicate of this trip
  %30 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %31 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %32 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %33 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %28, i32 %29, i32 %30, i32 %33)    ; IR: uncompute next %10
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %28)    ; IR: release next %10 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_lshr_i32_hl_unc(i32 %30, i32 %33, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %16  (the controlled Ry on r is frozen: not reverse-played)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %30)    ; IR: release %16 (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %32, i32 %31, i32 %29)    ; IR: uncompute the predicate of this trip (every trip 1..K; it reads x only, never r)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %29)    ; IR: release the predicate (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_ugt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %31, i32 %33, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %7 / %17
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %31)    ; IR: release %7 / %17 (|0>)
  %34 = add nuw nsw i32 %27, 1
  %35 = icmp ult i32 %34, 4    ; IR: K  [K]
  br i1 %35, label %26, label %36

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %32)    ; IR: release the |1> seed directly (rule 7: known basis state)
  %37 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %7)    ; IR: %21 = cq_measure_si32(%20): the r rail itself
  %38 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %25)    ; IR: %22 = cq_measure_ui32(%19)
