name: 153_nested_kloops_in_arm
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 14 (nested quantum-dependent exits, cutoff K, chain seeded by the arm flag), 9, 8, 7, 5.
; Checked: s (measured).
; Clean: every trip rail of both loops and every trip predicate, the K-th of each chain included; the after-trip-K exit
; tests (uncomputed right after their output rail is formed); the else-arm value, the arm flag and the s seed are freed.
; Kept: (rule 14) A_K (%40: the outer exit test x_K > k evaluated after outer trip K, ANDed with that trip's
; predicate) and, per outer trip, B_K (%33: the inner exit test z_K > k evaluated after inner trip K, ANDed with that
; trip's predicate; minted in the outer latch, never pushed): 5 output rails in all. A_K = 1 iff the outer loop would run
; a (K+1)-th trip; a B_K = 1 iff that outer trip's inner loop would; a loop that exits after exactly K trips reads 0.
; The user registers x and y stay allocated.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, tx, 1); (Ry, y, ty, 1).
; Two nested K-loops inside the then-arm of `if (x > c)`. The arm flag F = (x > c) SEEDS the outer chain (rule 14: a loop
; in an arm takes the arm flag instead of |1>): A_i = A_{i-1} & (x_i > k) with A_{-1} = F, so where the arm is not taken
; nothing in the loops changes. Each outer trip's inner chain is seeded by that trip's predicate: B_j = B_{j-1} & (z_j > k)
; with B_{-1} = A_i (-O1's hoisted guard %13 is inner trip 0's test); z_0 is the user register y. Every carried value (s, z,
; x) advances by a select on its chain's predicate (rule 9). The arm itself merges by one select on F between the loops'
; final s (the seed 0 where no trip ran, covering the [0, %10] incoming) and the else-arm value x + y, computed unguarded;
; the merge is a fresh result rail, so nothing is copied out. The mirror is 139's nested reverse: pop the outer trip's
; rails, run the inner reverse (every inner predicate uncomputed), uncompute the outer predicate and its compare.
; F is uncomputed last, after the chain it seeded has been torn down.

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 8, 18, 19, 12, 5, 2.
; Checked: x (measured).
; Clean: the left flag F = (x > k), the clone's result rail, the right flag E = (f(x, c) == m) and the conjunction
; flag G, all freed before the Ry(-tx) on x.
; Kept: none.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, tx, 1); (P, G, p, x > k && x * c + 1 == m); (Ry, x, -tx, 1).
; The right operand of `&&` is a noinline call, so -O1 keeps the short-circuit diamond (block %9 under %8) instead of
; folding to `and i1`. f has no non-pure gate, so under the quantum predicate it is called UNGUARDED (rule 19) as the
; lifted clone __cq_q_f_10 (rule 18, §1.4 mask: x quantum, c classical): the clone computes x * c + 1 out of place,
; copies the result into a fresh rail, uncomputes its body and returns the copy; its twin __cq_q_f_10_unc recomputes,
; XORs the result out and uncomputes, after which the caller frees the result rail. The compare is one flag E on the
; result rail; the phase block's path predicate F & E is one and_i1 into a fresh |0> flag G (rule 8), the phase is a
; kickback on G (rule 12: a quantum predicate is in scope). Teardown is LIFO: G, E, the call result (twin), F, all before
; the non-diagonal Ry on their source x (rule 5). The original f is dead and dropped.

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"

  %9 = call fastcc i32 @__cq_q_f_10(i32 %7, i32 %3)    ; IR: block %9: %10 = call @f(%7, %3): pure callee, lifted and evaluated unguarded
  %10 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %9, i32 %4)    ; IR: block %9: %11 = icmp eq i32 %10, %4  [the right conjunct]
  %11 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: path predicate of block %12 = %8 & %11  [fresh |0> flag]
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %8, i32 %10, i32 %11)    ; IR: br i1 %11 inside block %9: %8 & %11 (Toffoli into the |0> flag)
  call void @cqrt_rz_i1(i32 %11, double %5)    ; IR: block %12: cq_phi(%5)  [kickback on the conjunction]
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %8, i32 %10, i32 %11)    ; IR: uncompute the %12 predicate (%8, %11 unchanged)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %11)    ; IR: release it (|0>)

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %10)    ; IR: release the %11 rail (|0>)
  call fastcc void @__cq_q_f_10_unc(i32 %9, i32 %7, i32 %3)    ; IR: uncompute %10 (the twin XORs the result out of its rail)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %9)    ; IR: release the %10 rail (|0>)

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %8)    ; IR: release the %8 rail (|0>)

define internal fastcc i32 @__cq_q_f_10(i32 %0, i32 %1) {

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %4)    ; IR: f: release the %3 rail (|0>)

name: 155_measure_in_arm
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 5, 8, 9.
; Checked: the returned int R = m + x_m with m = (x_m > k) ? y_m : c (classical: x and y measured).
; Clean: the flag F = (x > k) and the select rail m, uncomputed after x's measurement (classical collapse, rule 2).
; Kept: the user registers x and y (both measured).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, tx, 1); (Ry, y, ty, 1).
; A cq_measure INSIDE A QUANTUM ARM (rule 2). A measurement is never conditioned on quantum data: the cq_measure of y
; is executed UNCONDITIONALLY at its program point, so y is collapsed on the F = 0 branch as well, a deviation from the
; C program's branch-conditioned measurement that is the user's responsibility (the compiler may warn). The flag F is
; never measured. At the arm's merge F still reads the unmeasured x, so m = F ? y_m : c is a quantum select (rule 9)
; into a fresh rail. Then x is measured. From that point F and m depend only on measured rails and classical values,
; so CLASSICAL COLLAPSE (rule 2) applies: m's select and F's compare are uncomputed while x's rail still holds its
; outcome (§1.3: a measured rail may be read as an operand), and F, m and R are recomputed by ordinary classical
; instructions from the outcomes. The function returns a plain int; no handle escapes. 140 is the same collapse with
; the measurement before the merge.

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"

  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %7, double %1)    ; IR: %7 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %8 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %2)    ; IR: %8 = cq_theta_si32(%2, %3)  [register y]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %8, double %3)    ; IR: %8 = cq_theta_si32(%2, %3)  [Ry]
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %7, i32 %4)    ; IR: %9 = icmp sgt i32 %7, %4  [flag F: path predicate of block %10]
  %10 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %8)    ; IR: block %10: %11 = cq_measure_si32(%8)  [executed unconditionally (rule 2): never conditioned on F]
  %11 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_ll(i32 %9, i32 %10, i32 %5)    ; IR: %13 = phi i32 [ %11, %10 ], [ %5, %6 ]  [m = F ? y_m : c, a quantum select while x is unmeasured]
  %12 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %7)    ; IR: %14 = cq_measure_si32(%7)  [from here F and m depend only on measured rails: classical collapse]

; Checked: each function's measured result.
; Clean: the shift-amount mask rails of shl_qq_i16 / ashr_qq_i64 (uncomputed and freed before the measurement).
; sub_qq_i8: the old a rail (%5, rule 6, operand 0 of the IR sub: |0> after the copy) and t = r + b (%8), both freed.
; Kept: the two rotated registers of every other function (no inverse), sub_qq_i8's b, and the measured result rail.
; Rotations: Ry(ta) on a and Ry(tb) on b in every function.
; Both operands quantum at every width the earlier examples lacked (10/12/13/19 covered i32 qq and the _hl/_lh mixed
; forms; sub_qq_i8's sub is a bijection in the dead a for fixed b, so rule 6 cleans a): the template is the bare qq shape cq_template_<op>_<W>(a, b) (§1.2: shape omitted = all handles), operands in
; the IR's order, into a fresh rail (rule 4). The classical mask of a quantum shift amount (b & 7, b & 63) is a _hl and,
; a garbage rail uncomputed right after the shift (rule 5). Totalization (§2): sdiv/srem/udiv by a quantum zero and
; sdiv(INT_MIN, -1) take the table's values; a quantum SHIFT AMOUNT is taken mod W (x86 semantics) although both masks

; Checked: r = table[(i + 1) & 7] + c (measured).
; Clean: the index rails (i & 7, i + 1, (i + 1) & 7), the load's copy-out rail and the value handle of v.
; Kept: the register i (frozen); the global QRAM `table` with the store LEFT IN PLACE (an output: the next call reads
;       it, so its store is never popped and the array is never freed); the unpopped store's tape slot (holding the
;       displaced cell, entangled with i; §1.3: an unpopped store keeps its slot allocated), one more slot per call, so
;       the kept slots grow with the number of calls; the measured result rail.

; object is a QRAM, one call per access (§1.3). A global's storage exists for the whole program, so its 8 cells are
; allocated ONCE, before any entry runs: a module constructor (@llvm.global_ctors) calls cqrt_qram_alloc_host_i32(@table,
; 8): the bus whose cells start as the host object's contents at program start (here the zeroinitializer: all |0>; the
; compiler never reads an initializer, so an extern of unknown extent takes the same call with n = 0, rule 20). The
; global keeps its definition (its storage is what seeds the bus) and the array handle lives in the compiler-made
; @table.qram (a classical word, like the slot globals of 67 / 71). The entry loads the handle and issues the accesses: the store is ONE
; cqrt_qram_store_i32(table, idx, val) with the logical-i32 index rail i & 7 (-O1's zext to i64 and the gep scaling are
; address arithmetic and are not emitted) and the classical v materialised as a basis-state handle (the contract: a value
; is always a handle); the load is ONE cqrt_qram_load_i32(table, idx2) -> fresh rail with idx2 = (i + 1) & 7. The
; global PERSISTS: table[i & 7] = v is the program's visible state after the call, so the store is NOT popped: its

; Clean: the clone result r (cleared by the twin, then freed).
; Kept: the register x (measured) and the returned rail (escapes with the return; never freed).
; Rotations: Ry(tx) on x.
; ext_fn has no body in this module, so rule 27 applies: the call becomes a call to the DECLARED clone named by §1.4
; from the call site alone, mask 10 (x quantum, c classical), no _b bounds. Its result is a handle by rule 27, its
; twin always exists, and both use the default calling convention (they cross translation units). Whatever is linked
; defines them; if nothing does, linking fails with an undefined symbol. Both take the loop cutoff K as a trailing
; classical i32 (rule 27; here the corpus default 4): the clone's quantum-exit loops run min(K, B) trips.
; r is quantum, so r + m is the out-of-place add_hl with the classical outcome m as the literal (rule 4). The twin
; runs after r's last use (the add). x is measured by then, which is allowed (§1.3: a measured rail may still be read as
; an operand); after the measurement every branch holds r = ext_fn(m, c), which the twin recomputes and XORs out.

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"

; Checked: arr[(i + 2) & 3].v + arr[(i + 1) & 3].w (measured).
; Clean: the three index rails, old, sum, the second load, every initializer handle, both field arrays (every store
;        popped LIFO per array, then released).
; Kept: the register i (frozen) and the measured result rail.
; Rotations: Ry(ti) on i.
; An array of structs written AND read at a quantum index is a QRAM (rule 20, owner ruling 2026-10-25); by rule 26 a
; struct cell is its fields, so the object is ONE QRAM PER FIELD COLUMN: arr_v and arr_w, 4 i32 cells each (the stride
; of the struct gep is the column choice, -O1's zext to i64 and the gep scaling are address arithmetic and are not
; emitted; the index rail is the logical-i32 index at the C expression's width). The memcpy of the constant initializer
; is one cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl(col, j, cqrt_alloc_i32(v)) per cell per column (the value always a handle; a
; basis-state seed, freed once its store is popped; rule 22's per-cell fixed-index stores). `arr[i & 3].v += c` is 77's
; READ-MODIFY-WRITE on the v column at idx1 = i & 3: ONE cqrt_qram_load_i32(arr_v, idx1) -> old (copy-out, cells
; preserved), sum = add_hl(old, c) into a fresh rail, ONE cqrt_qram_store_i32(arr_v, idx1, sum). The second statement
; stores the SAME rail sum (-O1 forwarded the re-read of arr[i & 3].v) into the w column at idx2 = (i + 1) & 3, and the
; final read is a load of the v column at idx3 = idx1 ^ 2 (-O1's spelling of (i + 2) & 3), added to sum into the
; result rail. Uncomputation runs in reverse (rule 5): the second load is un-copied, idx3 uncomputed, the w store popped
; (the only store on arr_w) and idx2's chain uncomputed, the v store popped (cell[idx1] holds old again), sum and then
; old uncomputed (old against the restored cell), idx1 uncomputed; then the initializer stores are popped LIFO per

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 26, 18, 8, 9, 4, 5, 7, 13, 14, 19, 23, 24 (and 3, 1).
; Checked: complex_div_q_c: creal(q) + cimag(q) (measured); complex_div_c_qq: creal(q) and cimag(q) (two measurements, classical sum).
; Clean: every rail but the registers (re; c and d), the measured result rails and the one Kept rail below; this includes
;   the fenv rails of the strictfp ilogb clone (the caller's empty flags rail, the two INVALID selects, the two ORed flags
;   states, the flags phi of logb and both clones' returned flags copies: fenv state the program never reads, dropped).
; Kept: a_K of __cq_q_ilogb_1 (ilogb's subnormal-loop exit test i<<1 >= 0 evaluated after the K-th body, ANDed with
;   trip K's predicate a_4; rule 14: a_K = 1 iff the loop would run a (K+1)-th trip, an exact-K exit reads 0; the shl
;   recurrence has no LLVM range bound below K, so it is kept): one rail per ACTIVATION of the loop (rule 14, as a nested
;   loop keeps one inner a_K per outer trip): __cq_q___divdc3_0011 runs __cq_q_logb_1 forward once and its twin once, and
;   the twin re-runs the forward ilogb clone (strictfp ilogb cannot be inlined into it), so complex_div_c_qq keeps two;
;   __cq_q_ilogb_1_unc itself keeps nothing).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on re (first entry); Ry(tc) on c, Ry(td) on d (second entry). The clones hold no rotation.
; Complex division has no inline fast path: clang always calls __divdc3, the compiler-rt body reproduced in the .c file, so the
; whole divide is one lifted call (rule 18). The two entries reach it with different taint: mask 1000 (a = creal(z) quantum,
; b, c, d classical) and mask 0011 (c, d quantum), one clone each; every classical op of the body stays classical IR and every
; op with a handle operand is an out-of-place template (rule 4, the _hl/_lh shapes with the classical value as a literal). The
; libm calls inside the body follow the same taint: logb/scalbn with classical arguments are the plain calls of the O1.ll,
; a quantum argument makes them clones of the injected musl bodies (rule 18): __cq_q_scalbn_10 and __cq_q_scalbn_11
; (musl scalbn.c), __cq_q_logb_1 (musl logb.c) and __cq_q_ilogb_1 (musl ilogb.c). The PINNED SOURCE AS BUILT is normative
; for every function the .c does not define (owner ruling 2026-10-29, cq-ezan): the bundle's clang -O1 IR of musl b1efda5,
; whose values the `; IR:` comments of the clones name. ilogb.c carries `#pragma STDC FENV_ACCESS ON`, so its IR is
; strictfp: it cannot be inlined into logb (no pragma) and its clone follows 82's fenv ABI (rule 23): the caller's mode
; and flags rail as two trailing parameters, { result, flags' } returned, both copied into fresh rails before the body is
; uncomputed, the _unc twin taking both returned handles first. __divdc3 has no FENV_ACCESS, so its environment is the
; default: __cq_q___divdc3_0011 passes the mode literal 0 (FE_TONEAREST) and mints an EMPTY flags rail (|0>, rule 7) that
; it frees directly after the twins; the returned flags are fenv state the program never reads and are dropped (uncomputed
; by the twin, freed). logb calls ilogb only in its finite-nonzero block, under a quantum predicate: the clone is called
; UNGUARDED (rule 19: its body has no non-pure gate) and merged, so logb's result phi AND its flags phi are the same nested
; selects, the flags arms of the blocks that do not call ilogb being the caller's flags. In __cq_q_ilogb_1 the subnormal
; loop `for (e = -0x3ff; i>>63 == 0; e--, i<<=1);` has a quantum exit: it runs as rule 14's chain of K = 4 trips (lines
; tagged [K]) seeded by the arm predicate (e == 0 & i<<12 != 0), the pre-header guard %12 being trip 0 of the latch test
; %21, each carried value advancing by a select on the trip predicate; the trips are written out (a rolled loop emits the
; same gates). After the K-th body the latch test is evaluated once more and a_K = a_4 & test is kept; that test and every
; trip predicate a_1..a_4 (the K-th body's included) are uncomputed. The two FORCE_EVAL(0/0.0f) of ilogb (the zero arm,
; block %13 under S0 & i<<12 == 0, and the inf/nan arm, block %22 under S2047) are constrained.sitofp(0) = 0.0f and
; constrained.fdiv(0.0f, 0.0f): two literals, so the quotient is a classical NaN stored volatile to a dead local (no gate,
; rule 24), and its INVALID bit is fenv state: flags' = flags | select(pred, FE_INVALID = 1, 0) (65's spelling); the mode
; is passed but not read (a NaN in every rounding mode). The `switch` on the exponent field is one equality flag per case
; and the default is the complement (rule 13). fabs/fmax(maxnum)/copysign/fptosi/sitofp and every fcmp predicate (ueq = !isfinite, une, ord, uno) are templates.

; product (both factors classical, quantum addend) is a classical fmul and an fadd_hl with the addend's handle first
; (commutative); otherwise the product factors are commutable, so a handle is put first (fmul _hl). Each clone copies its two results into fresh rails,

; results). The garbage of the caller is uncomputed
; before the measurement (rule 5).

; Checked: cabs_quantum_re: hypot(re, im) (measured, %60 -> %61); cabs_quantum_both: hypot(re, im) with both quantum
; (measured, %62 -> %63).
; Clean: every flag, select and arithmetic rail of both entries, all freed before the measurement.
; Kept: the registers (re %4; re %5 and im %6) and the two measured result rails (%60, %62).
; Rotations: (Ry, re, tr, 1) in cabs_quantum_re; (Ry, re, tr, 1), (Ry, im, ti, 1) in cabs_quantum_both.
; cabs is hypot; musl's body is static and clang -O1 inlines it, so no clone appears: the whole function is
; straight-line templates in the entry. The `union { double f; unsigned long long i; }` views are SSA values (rule 20):
; a bitcast template between f64 and i64, the exponent read is lshr + trunc, and fabs clears the sign. The conditional
; swap `if (ux.i < uy.i)` is one icmp flag and two selects (rule 9). Every `return` of the if ladder is an exit edge:
; the four-incoming phi of %63 is three nested selects on the local branch flags (%18: return y; %22 = or_i1 of the two
; equality flags: return x; %25: x + y), innermost the sqrt path, so each select is dominated by the previous flag's
; false case and no path conjunction is needed; the three-incoming phis of %38 (the scaling by 2^+-700 and z) are two
; nested selects on %29 and %34 the same way. The split x = hx + lx goes through fptrunc / fpext templates, the two

; addend, the product uncomputed after the sum, and sqrt is a template. In the second entry the compare, the selects and
; the sum are two-handle templates (both operands quantum). Everything but the result rail is uncomputed LIFO and freed
; before the measurement.

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 18, 20, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 2 (and 1).
; Checked: cbrt(x) (measured, %56 -> %57); scalbn(x, n) (measured, %33 -> %34); exp(x) + atan2(x, y) (measured, %7 -> %8);
; sin(x) + log(x) + pow(x, y) (measured, %9 -> %10).
; Clean: every flag, select and arithmetic rail of the four entries, the two clone result rails of the third and the three
; of the fourth (zeroed by the _unc twins, then freed), and the partial sum %7 of the fourth, all freed before each
; measurement.
; Kept: the registers (x %3; x %5 and n %6; x %4; x %4) and the four measured result rails (%56, %33, %7, %9).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, tx, 1) in libm_cbrt_q; (Ry, x, tx, 1), (Ry, n, tn, 1) (cqrt_ry_i32 on the integer register) in
; libm_scalbn_qq; (Ry, x, tx, 1) in libm_exp_atan2_q; (Ry, x, tx, 1) in libm_sin_log_pow_q.
; cbrt_musl and scalbn_musl are static and clang -O1 inlines them, so their musl bodies lower in the entries: the
; `union { double f; unsigned long long i; }` views are bitcast templates (rule 20), the exponent arithmetic is integer
; templates (lshr, trunc, and, udiv, add, zext, shl, or), and the polynomial / Newton steps are fmul, fdiv, fadd, fsub
; templates with the constants as literals (each llvm.fmuladd is UNFUSED, §2: an fmul into a fresh product rail, then an
; fadd, the product uncomputed by its fmul _unc right after the sum and freed). Branches are flags (rule 8) and every merge is a select chain on the local
; flags (rule 9): the %53 phi of cbrt is select(%8, x + x, select(%12 & %19, x, %52)) with one and_i1 for the %13 -> %53 edge;
; the five-incoming phis of %26 in scalbn are four nested selects on %7, %11, %17, %21 with both x and n quantum, so the
; smin/smax clamps and the compares are _hl templates on the n rail. The third and fourth entries reach exp, atan2, sin, log
; and pow (sec. 8 item 14). In the O1.ll, atan2 is a libm call and exp, sin, log, pow are the llvm math intrinsics clang
; emits for them (llvm.exp/sin/log/pow.f64); by rule 18 an intrinsic is the call of the libm function of the same name. The
; compiler injects musl's exp.c, atan2.c, sin.c, log.c and pow.c from the source bundle and lifts them like every other
; callee with a quantum argument: the lowering shows the clone calls __cq_q_exp_1(x), __cq_q_sin_1(x), __cq_q_log_1(x)
; (mask 1) and __cq_q_atan2_10(x, y), __cq_q_pow_10(x, y) (mask 10, y a classical double), each returning a fresh result
; rail (copy-out, rule 18), and their _unc twins zero those rails after the last sum read them; the caller then frees them.
; THE CLONE BODIES ARE DECLARED ONLY: this example witnesses the call sites, the masks and the clone/twin signatures; 184
; shows one lifted libm body (musl atan) in full. For the trace, _tools/trace_stubs.c (exp, atan2) and
; _tools/stubs.d/175_libm_quantum.c (sin, log, pow) print the clone and twin calls so the trace links. Everything but the
; result rails is uncomputed LIFO before each measurement; in the fourth entry the partial sum %7 is uncomputed before the
; sin and log rails it reads (rule 5: an operand rail outlives every _unc that reads it).

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 20 (bool x[nq] is a runtime-sized slot array: one `alloca i32, nq` of i1 handles; every access has a
; classical index and loads the handle), 2 (each H-loop trip mints x[i] = alloc_i1(false) + Ry; cq_theta on a slot handle
; rotates that rail in place; the measure loop reads the slots), 14 (every loop has a classical runtime bound: the three Ry
; loops, the two value(x) loops and the measure loop run nq trips, the outer loop iters trips; all stay ROLLED classical
; loops; each value(x) trip pushes its three trip-local rails and a reverse loop of nq trips pops and uncomputes them),
; 4 (value(x) is zext_i1_to_i32 / shl_i32_hl / or_i32 into fresh rails; the oracle compare is icmp_eq_i32_hl against the
; runtime target), 8 (the compare rail is the branch flag: the oracle phase arm is rz_i1 on it; R0's phase arm sits on the
; FALSE edge of `v == 0`, so it is the X-bracketed kickback), 5 (LIFO: the flag, then the value chain newest trip first, all
; before the next A^dag / A layer rotates their sources), 7 (the |0> accumulator seed of each value(x) is freed directly),
; 12 (every cq_phi is under a quantum predicate: none is deleted).
; Checked: x[0..nq-1] (the nq measured rails; m = sum x[i] << i).
; Clean: every flag, every value-chain rail (zext, shl, or) and both accumulator seeds, in every iteration.
; Kept: the nq registers only (measured). No rail is left dirty.
; Rotations: Ry(pi/2) on x[0..nq-1] (A; control 1); then per iteration r = 0 .. iters-1:
;   P(pi)  on flag(v == target)       [O;  control predicate: value(x) == target, v = sum_i x[i] << i]
;   Ry(-pi/2) on x[0..nq-1]           [A^dag; control 1]
;   P(pi)  on NOT flag(v == 0)        [R0; control predicate: value(x) != 0, the X-bracketed flag]
;   Ry(pi/2) on x[0..nq-1]            [A; control 1]
; Expected: P(target) = sin^2((2 iters + 1) theta) with sin^2 theta = 2^-nq. Replayed on a state vector (scratch replayer,
; every free asserted |0>): grover_search(3, 5, 2): P(5) = 0.945312 (textbook 0.945312); grover_search(4, 11, 3):
; P(11) = 0.961319 (textbook 0.961319); every other outcome (1 - P) / (2^nq - 1), max deviation 5.6e-16.
; The source is Nielsen & Chuang's G = A R0 A^dag O with A = Ry(pi/2)^nq, written as plain C with the qubit count an
; input. -O1 inlines value(nq, x) twice as an nq-trip accumulator loop (zext nneg i8 -> i32 of the cell, shl by the trip
; index, or into the carried i32) whose carried value starts from the literal 0 (a |0> seed rail, minted before the
; nq > 0 guard so that the zero-trip path reads the seed too: the exit phis %42 / %59 are the seed or the last trip's
; or-rail). The H loop stores 0 and forwards it into `cq_theta_i1(false, pi/2)`: one minted register per trip, the dead
; `store i8 0` emits nothing. The quantum lowering of the accumulator is 117's: fresh rails per trip, handle-stack mirror
; right after the flag's kickback, before A^dag / A rotate the cells (the _unc of zext reads the cell, which must still
; hold the value it read). The mirror runs only when the forward loop ran (the same classical nq > 0 test); its last pop
; is the seed, which is then freed directly. `value(x) != 0` is spelled by -O1 as `icmp eq %59, 0` with the phase block
; on the false edge, so the kickback is bracketed by X on the flag; P(pi) under `v != 0` is R0 = 2|0><0| - I up to a
; global phase. No quantum data crosses the outer back edge except the nq registers (in place), so the handle stack is
; empty at every latch.

  call void @cqrt_ry_i1(i32 %20, double 0x3FF921FB54442D18)    ; IR: %20 = cq_theta_i1(false, pi/2)  [A: Ry(pi/2)]
  store i32 %20, ptr %19, align 4    ; IR: %21 = zext %20; store i8 %21, ptr %19  (slot i holds the handle of x[i])

25:; IR: block %26

  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %32)    ; IR: trip-local rails on the handle stack (rule 14): the previous accumulator
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %35)    ; IR: ... the zext rail
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %37)    ; IR: ... the shl rail
  %39 = add nuw nsw i64 %31, 1    ; IR: %39  (classical)

  %42 = phi i32 [ %29, %27 ], [ %38, %30 ]    ; IR: %42 = phi i32 [ 0, %28 ], [ %38, %30 ]  (v: the seed, or the last trip's rail)
  %43 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %42, i32 %1)    ; IR: %43 = icmp eq i32 %42, %1  [the oracle flag: v == target, target a runtime literal]
  call void @cqrt_rz_i1(i32 %43, double 0x400921FB54442D18)    ; IR: br i1 %43 -> block %44: cq_phi(pi)  [O: kickback on the flag]
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl_unc(i32 %43, i32 %42, i32 %1)    ; IR: uncompute %43 after its only controlled gate
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %43)    ; IR: release the flag (|0>)

; Kept: im (%6, the rotated register) and the measured result rail %31; nothing else.
; Rotations: (Ry, im, ti, 1); the clone holds none.
; float _Complex with the IMAGINARY part quantum: 171's shape at float width on the <2 x float> ABI (173). Taint flows
; through clang's Annex G expansion exactly as rule 3 says: z = re + im*I makes the real part `im * 0 + re` quantum as
; well (%7, %8), so z * w reaches __mulsc3 with mask 1100 (a = crealf(z) and b = im quantum, c, d classical), NOT the
; 0100 the .c comment guesses: the mask is taken from the SSA values at the call. One clone of the compiler-rt body,
; returning the <2 x float> as { i32, i32 } (two lane handles); the extractelements are lane moves and get no gate. The
; body has 173's -O1 shape (fcmp ord + or into the early exit, the %64 chain as `fcmp une` + and, block %95 under !%13 &
; !%94): with both a and b quantum every fabs/isinf/copysign of the body is a template, the only classical values are
; the c/d NaN fixes (%27-%32), which enter the merges as literal arms of select_f32_ll. The entry's two `fcmp uno`
; branches conjoin into the P20 predicate (rule 8) and the clone's lanes are merged with the fast-path values by two
; selects on it (rule 9). conjf(p) is representation only: -O1 folds `- cimagf(conj p)` into `+ cimagf(p)`, so the sum

; fmul_f32 into a fresh product rail, then an fadd_f32 of the product and the addend; the product is uncomputed right
; after the sum it fed (rule 5, LIFO), in the clone and again in its _unc twin's recomputation.

; both parts quantum (measured, %64 -> %65).
; Clean: every flag, select and arithmetic rail of both entries, all freed before the measurement.
; Kept: the registers (re %4; re %5 and im %6) and the two measured result rails (%62, %64).
; Rotations: (Ry, re, tr, 1) in cabs_complex_h_re; (Ry, re, tr, 1), (Ry, im, ti, 1) in cabs_complex_h_both.
; cabs through the complex.h entry point: the .c defines cabs(z) = hypot_musl(creal z, cimag z) with musl's hypot body.
; clang -O1 inlines the static hypot_musl into cabs and then inlines cabs (its `double complex` parameter already split
; into two scalar doubles by the SysV ABI) into both entries, so the O1.ll holds NO call: there is nothing to lift, no
; clone __cq_q_cabs_10/_11 or __cq_q_hypot_musl_10/_11 can appear (rule 18 lifts a CALL with a quantum argument), and
; every body is shown because it is in the entries. The exported `cabs` itself has no caller and no quantum value
; reaches it: it is a classical function and passes through unchanged (its instructions are annotated `(classical)`);
; nothing of it is quantum, so no rail, flag or gate belongs to it. What differs from 172 is the Annex G prelude of z =
; re + im*I (rule 26): the real part is `im * 0 + re`, a classical fmul and one fadd_f64_hl in the first entry, a
; quantum fmul_f64_hl and a two-handle fadd in the second; cimag(z) is the im value itself. From there the lowering is
; 172's: the union views are bitcast / lshr / trunc templates (rule 20), the swap is one icmp flag and two selects, the
; if-ladder returns are nested selects on the local flags (%18 / %22 / %25 in the first entry: y, x, x + y, innermost
; the sqrt path), the 2^+-700 scaling phis are two nested selects, the split through fptrunc / fpext and the two
; llvm.fmuladd sums (lx, ly) UNFUSED (§2, cf. 14): fmul into a product rail, then fadd, the product uncomputed after the
; sum. Everything but the result rail is uncomputed LIFO and freed before the measurement.

define double @cabs(double noundef %0, double noundef %1) {
  %3 = tail call double @llvm.fabs.f64(double %0)    ; IR: %3 = fabs(creal z)  (classical: no quantum value reaches cabs; the function passes through)
  %4 = bitcast double %3 to i64    ; IR: %4  (classical)
  %5 = tail call double @llvm.fabs.f64(double %1)    ; IR: %5  (classical)
  %6 = bitcast double %5 to i64    ; IR: %6  (classical)
  %7 = icmp ult i64 %4, %6    ; IR: %7  (classical)
  %8 = select i1 %7, double %3, double %5    ; IR: %8  (classical)
  %9 = select i1 %7, double %5, double %3    ; IR: %9  (classical)
  %10 = bitcast double %9 to i64    ; IR: %10  (classical)
  %11 = lshr i64 %10, 52    ; IR: %11  (classical)
  %12 = trunc nuw nsw i64 %11 to i32    ; IR: %12  (classical)
  %13 = bitcast double %8 to i64    ; IR: %13  (classical)
  %14 = lshr i64 %13, 52    ; IR: %14  (classical)
  %15 = trunc nuw nsw i64 %14 to i32    ; IR: %15  (classical)
  %16 = icmp eq i64 %14, 2047    ; IR: %16  (classical)
  br i1 %16, label %61, label %17    ; IR: br %16  (classical)

17:
  %18 = icmp eq i64 %11, 2047    ; IR: %18  (classical)
  %19 = icmp eq i64 %13, 0    ; IR: %19  (classical)
  %20 = or i1 %19, %18    ; IR: %20  (classical)
  br i1 %20, label %61, label %21    ; IR: br %20  (classical)

21:
  %22 = sub nsw i32 %12, %15    ; IR: %22  (classical)
  %23 = icmp sgt i32 %22, 64    ; IR: %23  (classical)
  br i1 %23, label %24, label %26    ; IR: br %23  (classical)

24:
  %25 = fadd double %3, %5    ; IR: %25  (classical)
  br label %61    ; IR: br  (classical)

26:
  %27 = icmp ugt i64 %10, 6908521828386340863    ; IR: %27  (classical)
  br i1 %27, label %28, label %31    ; IR: br %27  (classical)

28:
  %29 = fmul double %9, 0x1430000000000000    ; IR: %29  (classical)
  %30 = fmul double %8, 0x1430000000000000    ; IR: %30  (classical)
  br label %36    ; IR: br  (classical)

31:
  %32 = icmp ult i64 %13, 2580562586483294208    ; IR: %32  (classical)
  br i1 %32, label %33, label %36    ; IR: br %32  (classical)

33:
  %34 = fmul double %9, 0x6BB0000000000000    ; IR: %34  (classical)
  %35 = fmul double %8, 0x6BB0000000000000    ; IR: %35  (classical)
  br label %36    ; IR: br  (classical)

36:
  %37 = phi double [ %30, %28 ], [ %35, %33 ], [ %8, %31 ]    ; IR: %37  (classical)
  %38 = phi double [ %29, %28 ], [ %34, %33 ], [ %9, %31 ]    ; IR: %38  (classical)
  %39 = phi double [ 0x6BB0000000000000, %28 ], [ 0x1430000000000000, %33 ], [ 1.000000e+00, %31 ]    ; IR: %39  (classical)
  %40 = fptrunc double %38 to float    ; IR: %40  (classical)
  %41 = fpext float %40 to double    ; IR: %41  (classical)
  %42 = fsub double %38, %41    ; IR: %42  (classical)
  %43 = fmul double %41, %41    ; IR: %43  (classical)
  %44 = fadd double %38, %38    ; IR: %44  (classical)
  %45 = fsub double %44, %42    ; IR: %45  (classical)
  %46 = fmul double %42, %42    ; IR: %46  (classical)
  %47 = tail call double @llvm.fmuladd.f64(double %42, double %45, double %46)    ; IR: %47  (classical)
  %48 = fptrunc double %37 to float    ; IR: %48  (classical)
  %49 = fpext float %48 to double    ; IR: %49  (classical)
  %50 = fsub double %37, %49    ; IR: %50  (classical)
  %51 = fmul double %49, %49    ; IR: %51  (classical)
  %52 = fadd double %37, %37    ; IR: %52  (classical)
  %53 = fsub double %52, %50    ; IR: %53  (classical)
  %54 = fmul double %50, %50    ; IR: %54  (classical)
  %55 = tail call double @llvm.fmuladd.f64(double %50, double %53, double %54)    ; IR: %55  (classical)
  %56 = fadd double %55, %47    ; IR: %56  (classical)
  %57 = fadd double %51, %56    ; IR: %57  (classical)
  %58 = fadd double %43, %57    ; IR: %58  (classical)
  %59 = tail call double @llvm.sqrt.f64(double %58)    ; IR: %59  (classical)
  %60 = fmul double %39, %59    ; IR: %60  (classical)
  br label %61    ; IR: br  (classical)

61:
  %62 = phi double [ %25, %24 ], [ %60, %36 ], [ %8, %2 ], [ %9, %17 ]    ; IR: %62  (classical)
  ret double %62    ; IR: ret %62  (classical)
}

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 15, 8, 12, 2, 4, 5, 7, 14, 20, 22.
; Checked: out = sum_j c[j] << (t-1-j) | sum_i k[i] << (t+i): the t counting rails c[j] (behind the runtime-sized slot
; array %7; the first measure loop loads and measures each) and the nk eigenphase rails k[i] (behind %5; the second
; measure loop), all measured.
; Clean: the kv accumulator walk (its |0> seed and per trip the zext, shl, or rails, pushed and uncomputed by the mirror
; loop), its sitofp rail (or, for nk <= 0, the 0.0 seed rail of the phi), the angle base A = fl((2 pi / 2^nk) * (double)kv)
; (the program's fmul), the per-trip angle rail A_j = fl(A * 2^j) (one per trip of the phase loop) and the QFT^-1 Toffoli
; flags c[m] & c[j] (one per (m, j) pair), each |0> (or its seed value) at its free.
; Kept: the user registers k[i] and c[j] (measured; a measured rail stays allocated). No other rail survives.
; Rotations: (Ry, k[i], tk[i], 1) for i = 0..nk-1; (Ry, c[j], pi/2, 1) for j = 0..t-1; then for j = 0..t-1:
; (P, A_j, val(A_j), c[j]) with A_j = fl(fl((2 pi / 2^nk) * (double)kv) * 2^j), kv = sum_i k[i] << i [the controlled
; U^(2^j), U = diag(e^{i 2 pi kv / 2^nk}), applied by ONE primitive on the angle rail]; then the QFT^-1: for j = t-1..0:
; (P, flag, -pi / 2^(m-j), c[m] & c[j]) for m = t-1..j+1, (P, c[j], pi, c[j]) (rz_i1 on the bare rail), (Ry, c[j], pi/2, 1).
; Expected: for basis kv the counting field reads kv * 2^(t-nk) exactly when t >= nk (c[0] is its top bit); in
; superposition every kv branch reads its own estimate and k is left unchanged. Replayed on a state vector (the phase
; primitive modelled as e^{i val(A_j)} on the c[j] = 1 branch, val(A_j) the double the chain computes from the basis
; value of k; every free asserted at its seed value; only the registers stay allocated): call 1 (nk = 2, t = 2,
; tk = {pi, 0}: kv = 1) reads c = 01, k = (1, 0) with p = 1.0000; call 2 (nk = 3, t = 4, tk = {pi/2, pi/2, pi}: kv uniform
; on {4, 5, 6, 7}) reads c = 2 kv (1000, 1010, 1100, 1110) jointly with its own k, p = 0.25 each, nothing else.
; QPE whose phase comes from a QUANTUM angle register, general size: nk, t and the preparation angles tk[] are inputs, so
; both registers are runtime-sized slot arrays (rule 20: `bool k[nk], c[t]` are `alloca i32, n` of handle cells; the
; memset zero-fills are one seed rail alloc_i1(0) per cell, rules 20, 22) and every loop has a classical runtime bound
; (rule 14). kv = sum k[i] << i is the quantum accumulator of 28 (zext, shl, or into fresh rails, pushed per trip). -O1
; turns (double)kv into `sitofp` at the loop exit and merges it with the literal 0.0 of the nk <= 0 path; that incoming is a
; seed rail cqrt_alloc_f64(0.0), so the phi is a handle on both edges. The kv seed alloc_i32(0) is allocated before the
; guard and is also the kv rail of the nk <= 0 path. -O1 hoists 2 pi / 2^nk (classical) and its product with (double)kv out
; of the phase loop: cq_template_fmul_f64_hl gives the f64 REGISTER A holding the program's IEEE double, bit-exact (rule 15,
; as 79 and 143). Each trip multiplies A by the classical (double)(1 << j) into the trip rail A_j, computed UNGUARDED (pure
; arm code is hoisted, rule 9), and `if (c[j]) cq_phi(phi)` is ONE primitive cqrt_rz_qangle_controlled(c[j], A_j):
; e^{i val(A_j)} on the branch where the bare rail c[j] is 1 (rule 15; the backend supplies the N-bit ladder, the IR never
; spells it; the phase is RELATIVE in k, never a deletable global one, rule 12). A_j is only read, so it is uncomputed and
; freed right after the primitive; after the loop A, the sitofp rail and the kv walk are uncomputed in LIFO order before
; the QFT^-1 (no non-diagonal gate ever touches k). The QFT^-1 is 117's caller loop: the nested branches c[m], c[j] are one
; Toffoli flag with a kickback cqrt_rz_i1(flag, -pi / 2^(m-j)); `if (c[j]) cq_phi(pi)` on the bare rail is cqrt_rz_i1 on
; the rail itself; cq_theta(&c[j], pi/2) is cqrt_ry_i1 in place. The measure loops and the packing are classical (rule 2).

; pack | m << 8.

; every sort trip's flag a[i] > a[i+1] and its two select rails (popped and uncomputed by the reverse sort loop); every
; scan trip's umax rail (popped and uncomputed by the reverse scan loop); the three shl rails and the two inner ors of the
; pack.
; Kept: the user register x; the pack result rail and the copied-out maximum (both measured).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).

; scan counter, the fixed post-loop reads), so it is a SLOT ARRAY (rule 20): a classical `alloca [4 x i32]` of handles,

; Checked: histogram: h[0] | h[1] << 4 | h[2] << 8 | h[3] << 12 with h[b] = #{i < 4 : (x >> 2i) & 3 == b} (measured).

; out[3] << 24 after out[(x >> 2i) & 3] = v0 + i for i = 0..3 in order (measured); the classical result is their sum.
; Clean: histogram: every trip's shift rail, bucket index rail, loaded old count and incremented count (popped and
; uncomputed by the reverse loop, the trip's store popped first), the four fixed-index copy-outs, the three shl rails and
; two inner ors, the shared memset handle 0, every store's tape slot, and the QRAM h (every store popped, then
; cqrt_qram_free). gather_scatter: the same for out, plus every trip's two shift rails, table index rail, QROM read, the
; partial sums s_1..s_4 and the basis-state value handle v0 + i (rule 7), and the |0> seed of s (never written).
; Kept: histogram: the user register x and the pack result rail (measured). gather_scatter: x, the copied-out sum and the
; pack result rail (both measured).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1) in each entry.
; h is read AND written at the quantum bucket (x >> 2i) & 3, so it is a QRAM (rule 20: a quantum-offset store): ONE
; cqrt_qram_alloc_i32(4) at the alloca, the `= {0}` memset is one cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl per cell sharing one basis-state
; handle 0 (rule 22, as in 30), and `h[b]++` is a read-modify-write at the logical-i32 index rail (-O1's zext to i64 and
; the gep scaling are not emitted): cqrt_qram_load_i32(h, idx) -> old (copy-out), new = old + 1 into a fresh rail,
; cqrt_qram_store_i32(h, idx, new) (the store owns a tape slot; the displaced cell, old, goes into it). The loop bound is
; classical, so it stays a classical loop (rule 14): the shift amount 2i is classical (an _hl literal recomputed from the
; trip index by the mirror) and each trip pushes its four rails. The post-loop reads are fixed-index copy-outs
; cqrt_qram_load_i32_hl. The reverse loop runs after the pack's garbage is uncomputed and the copy-outs are un-copied:
; every bucket store may touch every cell, so the pops are strictly last-in-first-out; popping trip i's store puts old

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 14, 16, 20, 21.
; Checked: list_search: p ? i : -1, the index of the first node whose v equals key, else -1 (the copied-out result,
; measured). calloc_aligned: r = s[j & 1] + 1 (measured).
; Clean: list_search: every trip rail (the object flags tag == 1, tag == 2, the merged v and its inner select, the found
; flag, the body predicate, the merged next tag and its inner select, the null flag, the trip's exit value, the next
; tag and result selects, the predicates A[1]..A[K-1]) popped and uncomputed by the reverse loop, plus the three seeds
; (p = tag 1, the result 0, the |1> predicate) freed directly. calloc_aligned: the index rail k & 3, the copy-out a[1],
; the rail x + 1; the store a[k & 3] = x is popped and the QRAM released at free(a).
; Kept: list_search: x and y (rotated), the result (measured) and the output predicate A[K] (rule 14: LLVM knows no
; bound of the trip count, the loop ends on a NULL read from memory; A[K] is 0 on every branch here, since the list has
; three nodes, but the compiler cannot prove it). calloc_aligned: k and x (rotated) and r (measured).
; Rotations: list_search: (Ry, x, tx, 1); (Ry, y, ty, 1). calloc_aligned: (Ry, k, tk, 1); (Ry, x, tx, 1).
; list_search. HEAP RECORDS: the three malloc'd nodes are objects 1 = a (%8), 2 = b (%7), 3 = c (%6); no access to them
; has a quantum offset (p->v is cell 0, p->next the field at byte 8, both CLASSICAL offsets), so none is a QRAM. Each
; is a host record block of the same 16-byte layout {i32 v, ptr next}: the v field of a and b holds a HANDLE (a slot
; cell: the handle replaces the int, both 4 bytes), the v field of c only ever holds the classical 7 and stays a
; classical cell (rule 20, homogeneous per cell), and every next field holds a CLASSICAL host pointer, stored as written.
; LOOP: the exit p->v != key reads quantum data, so the loop is a K-loop (rule 14, cutoff K = 4: no range bound B
; exists). A trip is one execution of the header %14; trip j runs under A[j] (A[0] = |1> seed), the body %19 under
; B[j] = A[j] & NOT found[j], and the next header under A[j+1] = B[j] & NOT null[j]. The carried pointer p is a FAT
; POINTER (rule 21): its tag rail, idx always 0 (the record start); trip 0's p = a is the seed tag 1. A deref is one
; classical-offset access per object of the provenance {a, b, c} merged by select on the guards tag == 1, tag == 2,
; with c the complement innermost (rule 9); the NULL tag 0 also falls to c, which is never observable: a NULL p never
; runs a trip. The loads stay where -O1 has them, in every trip (%17 in the header, %22 in the body); the reverse loop
; reloads the v cells its uncomputes read (nothing in the function writes them after the loop starts).
; p->next is a POINTER LOADED THROUGH A FAT POINTER (rule 21): one unguarded host load of each object's next field, kept
; where -O1 has it (block %19, every trip). The loaded values are host pointers whose origin the compiler does not
; resolve from the stores: each is decoded AT RUN TIME to a tag by range tests over the function's object table
; (base[o] = the malloc'd host address, cell count 1 = one 16-byte record; base[o] <= addr <= base[o] + 16, one-past
; included; an address in no object, NULL among them, is tag 0), a classical select chain. The three decoded tags are
; merged by select on the same guards (run-time classical operands of select_ll/select_lh); they are pushed per trip
; and popped for the merges' _unc. idx is not carried: a pointer this loop dereferences has idx 0 in every defined
; execution (C never dereferences a one-past or misaligned node pointer), and the only other use, the NULL test, is
; tag == 0 (rule 21: distinct allocations of this function and NULL compare by tags; a one-past address is non-NULL
; and decodes to a nonzero tag). Here a->next decodes to 2, b->next to 3, c->next to 0. i is the
; induction variable %16 = j (SCEV), a classical trip index. The exit phi %25 is carried as the result rail r: trip j
; sets r = found[j] ? j : -1 under A[j] (an exit at %14 yields j, a continue sets the provisional -1 that the NULL exit
; at %19 keeps). After K trips r is copied out, and the reverse loop pops each trip; on reverse index 0 (trip K-1) it
; keeps A[K] (rule 14: the test that would admit a (K+1)-th trip). The blocks are never freed by the program (host
; memory, no rail).
; calloc_aligned. a: a[k & 3] = x is a QUANTUM-OFFSET store, so the calloc block is a QRAM (rule 20, rule 16): calloc(4,
; 4) is cqrt_qram_alloc_i32(4) and nothing else, because a fresh QRAM cell is |0>, exactly calloc's zero fill (no host
; block, no gate); calloc(n, size) maps to n cells of the accessed element type (here size = sizeof(int), one i32 cell
; per element; a quantum n allocates at its upper bound). s: aligned_alloc(16, 16) is accessed only at classical offsets
; (0, 1 and the runtime j & 1), so it is a SLOT ARRAY and stays a host call: 4 int cells = 4 handle slots of 4 bytes =
; the same 16 bytes at the same alignment. s[0] = a[1] stores the fixed-index copy-out of the QRAM cell 1 into slot 0;
; s[1] = x + 1 stores the fresh rail; s[j & 1] is a slot load (the handle, no gate). free(a) under no predicate is a
; lifetime end (rule 16): the copy-out a[1] is un-copied (cell 1 unchanged since the load), the store is popped (x and
; the index rail hold their forward values) and the QRAM is released. free(s) is the ordinary host call.

  %11 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %8, i64 8    ; IR: %11 = gep %8, 8

  %15 = ptrtoint ptr %7 to i64    ; IR: object table: base[2] = b

  %19 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 true)    ; IR: predicate of reaching the header in trip 0 (always 1)

  %28 = load i32, ptr %7, align 8    ; IR: %17: object 2's v cell (the handle of y)
  %29 = load i32, ptr %6, align 8    ; IR: %17: object 3's v cell (classical host load: 7)

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 4, 5, 7, 18, 20, 21, 22, §1.3 (QRAM contract), §1.4.
; Checked: alias_params: a[0] after addto (measured): 2 * a0 when x & 1 == 0 (q aliases p), a0 + a1 when x & 1 == 1.
; qram_2d: g[1][2] + g[r & 3][0] (measured): v * [r & 3 == 1 && c & 3 == 2] + v * [c & 3 == 0].
; Clean: alias_params: the clone's two load copy-outs and its sum (inside the clone), the stored value rail (popped, then
; cleared by the twin), the two initializer seeds a0, a1, the index rail x & 1, every tape slot, and the 2-cell QRAM a
; (qram_free). qram_2d: the two load copy-outs, the flattened index rail, the row-offset rail, r & 3, c & 3, the value
; seed v, the shared memset seed 0, every tape slot, and the 16-cell QRAM g (qram_free).
; Kept: alias_params: x (rotated register) and the measured result a[0]. qram_2d: r, c (rotated registers) and the
; measured result.
; Rotations: alias_params: (Ry, x, tx, 1). qram_2d: (Ry, r, tr, 1); (Ry, c, tc, 1).
; alias_params: a = {a0, a1} is read through q = a + (x & 1) inside addto, a QUANTUM-OFFSET load, and a[0] is later
; written with the quantum sum, so a may hold a handle: by rule 20 the whole object is a QRAM (qram_alloc_i32(2); the
; initializer is one store_hl per cell of a basis-state seed). Both pointer arguments cross the clone boundary as fat
; pointers (rule 21): (object, tag, i32 idx) with object = the QRAM bus handle of a (the object table; no mask digit), tag the
; classical 1 (single-object provenance {a}: no guard), idx the CELL index: p = (a, 1, 0) classical, q = (a, 1, x & 1)
; with a quantum idx. Mask per §1.4 over the fields tag_p, idx_p, tag_q, idx_q: 0001; the pointee cells add no digits,
; since a is a QRAM (§1.4: QRAM cells get no mask digits, a QRAM object is quantum by definition). In the clone *q is
; qram_load_i32 (quantum idx), *p is qram_load_i32_hl (classical idx), and *p = sum is qram_store_i32_hl. ALIASING:
; both loads are executed before the store (-O1's order), so when x & 1 == 0 both copy-outs read cell 0 = a0 and the
; store writes 2 * a0, exactly C's result; when x & 1 == 1 they read a1 and a0. Rule 18 copy-out: the sum is copied
; into a fresh rail v and the body (sum, both loads) is uncomputed BEFORE the store, while every cell still holds the
; value it had at the loads (a load's _unc requires that; after the store cell 0 has changed). The store keeps v as its
; value rail, and the pop precondition (§1.3) needs v at its forward value until the store is popped, so the clone
; RETURNS v as an extra i32 result (rule 18: a callee storing into a caller's QRAM returns each stored value rail)
; instead of freeing it. The caller copies
; out a[0], and at the lifetime end of a pops the clone's store first (it touched cell 0, after both initializer
; stores), then calls the twin __cq_q_addto_0001_unc(v, args...) (rule 18): with the store popped the cells are again a0, a1, so
; the twin recomputes both loads and the sum, XORs v to |0> with copy_i32 and uncomputes; the caller frees v. The
; initializer stores (distinct cells: they commute) are popped, their seeds freed, x & 1 uncomputed, the QRAM freed.
; The measured copy-out a[0] stands while the stores are popped (a pop permutes the cells only; 186).
; qram_2d: g is written at a QUANTUM offset, so it is a 16-cell QRAM. -O1's llvm.memset(g, 0, 64) is one store_hl per
; i32 cell of the shared seed 0 (rule 22, as in 30). The 2-D index is FLATTENED to the cell index (rule 20): the store's
; index rail is (r & 3) * 4 + (c & 3) (mul_i32_hl by the row length 4, then add_i32); -O1's gep %11 = &g[r & 3] is the
; row offset (r & 3) * 4, which is also the cell index of the load g[r & 3][0], so the two accesses share that rail.
; g[1][2] (-O1's byte offset 24) is cell 6: qram_load_i32_hl(g, 6). The zexts to i64 and the gep scaling are address
; arithmetic and are not emitted. At the lifetime end the copy-outs are un-copied, the quantum-index store (it may
; touch every cell) is popped before the 16 memset stores (distinct cells, written in reverse), and the QRAM is freed.

define i32 @alias_params(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2, i32 noundef %3) {
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_alloc_i32(i32 2)    ; IR: %5 = alloca [2 x i32]: a 2-cell QRAM a, cells |0> (a quantum-offset load reads it and it may hold a handle)
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %6, double %1)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %2)    ; IR: store i32 %2, ptr %5: a0 as a basis-state handle
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl(i32 %5, i32 0, i32 %7)    ; IR: store i32 %2, ptr %5: a[0] = a0
  %8 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %3)    ; IR: store i32 %3, ptr %7: a1 as a basis-state handle
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl(i32 %5, i32 1, i32 %8)    ; IR: store i32 %3, ptr %7: a[1] = a1
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_and_i32_hl(i32 %6, i32 1)    ; IR: %8 = and i32 %6, 1  [q's cell index rail; zext %9 and gep %10 not emitted]
  %10 = call fastcc i32 @__cq_q_addto_0001(i32 %5, i32 1, i32 0, i32 %5, i32 1, i32 %9)    ; IR: call fastcc void @addto(ptr %5, ptr %10): p = (a, tag 1, idx 0), q = (a, tag 1, idx x & 1); returns the stored value rail v
  %11 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i32_hl(i32 %5, i32 0)    ; IR: %11 = load i32, ptr %5: a[0]  (copy-out)  [result rail]
  ; IR: llvm.lifetime.end(%5): the lifetime of a ends; clean-up in reverse order of its accesses
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl_unc(i32 %5, i32 0, i32 %10)    ; IR: pop the clone's store *p = sum (last store to cell 0): cells a0, a1 again
  call fastcc void @__cq_q_addto_0001_unc(i32 %10, i32 %5, i32 1, i32 0, i32 %5, i32 1, i32 %9)    ; IR: twin: recompute the clone's loads and sum, XOR v to |0>
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %10)    ; IR: release v (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl_unc(i32 %5, i32 1, i32 %8)    ; IR: pop a[1] = a1
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %8)    ; IR: release the seed a1 (rule 7)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl_unc(i32 %5, i32 0, i32 %7)    ; IR: pop a[0] = a0
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release the seed a0 (rule 7)
  call void @cq_template_and_i32_hl_unc(i32 %9, i32 %6, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %8
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %9)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_qram_free(i32 %5)    ; IR: llvm.lifetime.end(%5): release the QRAM a (every store popped)
  %12 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %11)    ; IR: %12 = cq_measure_si32(%11)
  ret i32 %12    ; IR: ret i32 %12
}

  %8 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i32_hl(i32 %0, i32 %2)    ; IR: %4 = load i32, ptr %0: *p  (classical cell index)

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 16, 20, §0 (run-time circuit), §1.3 (QRAM contract, qram_realloc), §2, §6.
; Checked: realloc_shrink: r = a[k & 1] (measured): v iff k & 3 < 2, else 0 (the never-written cell, §6).
; realloc_qsize: r = a[k & 1] + a[1] (measured): v + 7 for k & 3 == 0, 2v for k & 3 odd, v for k & 3 == 2.
; vla_qram: a[0] (measured): y iff x % n == 0, else 0 (§6). guarded_global: table[i & 7] (measured): y if x > k, else
; the cell's previous value (0 on the first call); the global's cells after the call (table[i & 7] == y iff x > k).
; Clean: realloc_shrink: k & 1, k & 3, the seed v, the store's tape slot, the realloc (undone), the QRAM a.
; realloc_qsize: k & 1, k & 3, the size rail (k & 3) + 2, the cell index (k & 3) + 1, both copy-outs, the seeds v and 7,
; both tape slots, the realloc (undone), the QRAM a. vla_qram: x % n, the seed y, the tape slot, the n-cell QRAM a.
; guarded_global: the flag x > k, both i & 7 rails, the seed y.
; Kept: realloc_shrink, realloc_qsize: k and the measured result. vla_qram: x and the measured result. guarded_global:
; x, i, the measured result, and the global QRAM table WITH its controlled store (never popped: an output, 160; the
; store's tape slot stays allocated, |0> on the x <= k branch).
; Rotations: realloc_shrink, realloc_qsize: (Ry, k, tk, 1). vla_qram: (Ry, x, tx, 1). guarded_global: (Ry, x, tx, 1);
; (Ry, i, ti, 1).
; realloc_shrink: a[k & 3] = v makes the malloc/realloc block one QRAM (186). realloc(a, 2) SHRINKS it:
; cqrt_qram_realloc_i8(a, 2) changes the logical size only; no gate runs and no cell moves (§1.3). When k & 3 >= 2 the
; stored v sits in a cell >= 2 that stays PHYSICALLY present but is out of range for every later access through a'
; (§2: a load there reads 0, a store is a no-op); C's realloc discards that cell, and the program never reads it
; again, so the circuit agrees with C on every basis input. The hidden cells are never re-exposed to the program: a
; later realloc that GREW a' back to 4 or more would map the new logical indices 2, 3 to FRESH |0> cells, never to the
; cells this shrink hid (§1.3), so a v hidden in cell 2 or 3 could not reappear (C's grown part is indeterminate = 0,
; §6); the hidden cells stay allocated, out of the program's reach, until the _unc chain re-exposes them for the pop.
; The read a[k & 1] (index < 2, in range) is the measured result, so it is never un-copied and its index rail is
; uncomputed right after it. At free(a) (rule 16) the realloc is undone FIRST (no store was made through a'),
; restoring the logical size 4, and then the store a[k & 3] = v is popped: its cell is still physically present (a
; shrink never detaches), so the pop returns it to |0> on every branch. The QRAM is released.
; realloc_qsize: realloc(a, (k & 3) + 2) has a QUANTUM size. The size rail (k & 3) + 2 is computed like any tainted
; value (-O1's zext to i64 is the size argument's representation and is not emitted) and the QRAM is resized to the
; size's UPPER BOUND 5 from LLVM's range facts (k & 3 <= 3; §1.3: a quantum n allocates at its upper bound): the call
; reads no rail, so the size rail has no consumer and is uncomputed at once (computed, never removed). The cells 2..4
; are FRESH |0> cells (§1.3: growing never maps to cells a shrink hid; C's grown part is indeterminate = 0, §6). a[(k
; & 3) + 1] = 7 stores at cell index (k & 3) + 1 (-O1's two geps; byte = cell for i8), in range (<= 4 < 5) on every
; branch, and in range of C's block too ((k & 3) + 1 < (k & 3) + 2). At free(a): un-copy both loads, pop the store
; made through a' (cell index rail recomputed-free afterwards), undo the realloc to the old size 2 (§1.3: after every
; store made through a' was popped), pop a[k & 1] = v, release the QRAM.
; vla_qram: int a[n] is an alloca of RUN-TIME length n (classical); a[x % n] = y is a quantum-offset store, so a is a
; QRAM of n cells: cqrt_qram_alloc_i32(n) with the host value n. The lowered program is a host program that builds the
; circuit at run time (§0), so the QRAM's size is a run-time parameter of the circuit. The index rail is urem_i32_hl(x,
; n) with the classical n as the literal operand. a[0] is read with load_hl and measured. A VLA's lifetime ends at its
; scope's end (rule 20: llvm.stackrestore or the function return; -O1 emits no stackrestore here), so its clean-up (pop
; the store, free the seed y, uncompute x % n, qram_free) runs at the return, after the measurement, not after the
; last access.
; guarded_global: static int table[8] is a global QRAM (rule 20, 160): a module constructor allocates its 8 cells once with
; cqrt_qram_alloc_host_i32(@table, 8), seeded from the global's own storage (the zeroinitializer); the handle lives in @table.qram.
; The store sits in an arm under the quantum flag x > k (rule 8): its index chain i & 7 is pure and hoisted unguarded
; (rule 9), and the store is ONE cqrt_qram_store_i32_controlled(flag, table, idx, y): under flag = 0 nothing happens and
; its tape slot stays |0> (§1.3). The global persists, so the store is never popped (160); its value seed y, its index
; rail and the flag are functions of parameters and of the untouched registers x, i, and are uncomputed and freed (the
; precondition of a pop no longer matters: there is none). The read table[i & 7] after the merge is -O1's separate
; %15 = and i32 %8, 7 and a QRAM load whose copy-out is the measured result.
; Regenerated 2026-11-02 (the first version called cqrt_qram_alloc_i32(8) and kept the handle in @table itself).

@table = internal unnamed_addr global [8 x i32] zeroinitializer, align 16    ; IR: @table = internal global [8 x i32] zeroinitializer  (kept as it is: the host object the constructor seeds the bus from)
@table.qram = internal global i32 0, align 4    ; IR: (compiler-made: holds the QRAM handle of @table's 8 cells)
@llvm.global_ctors = appending global [1 x { i32, ptr, ptr }] [{ i32, ptr, ptr } { i32 65535, ptr @__cq_qram_init_table, ptr null }]    ; IR: program start: the global's storage exists before any entry runs

define internal void @__cq_qram_init_table() {
  %1 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_alloc_host_i32(ptr @table, i64 8)    ; IR: @table's storage: an 8-cell i32 QRAM whose cells start as the host object's contents (the zeroinitializer: all |0>)
  store i32 %1, ptr @table.qram, align 4    ; IR: the handle cell keeps the array handle (classical)
  ret void
}

define i32 @realloc_shrink(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i8 noundef zeroext %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [register k]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %4, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_alloc_i8(i32 4)    ; IR: %5 = call @malloc(4): the QRAM a, 4 byte cells |0>
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_and_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 3)    ; IR: %6 = and i32 %4, 3  [index rail; zext %7 and gep %8 not emitted]
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i8(i8 %2)    ; IR: store i8 %2, ptr %8: v as a basis-state handle
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i8(i32 %5, i32 %6, i32 %7)    ; IR: store i8 %2, ptr %8: a[k & 3] = v
  %8 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_realloc_i8(i32 %5, i32 2)    ; IR: %9 = call @realloc(%5, 2): SHRINK, logical size 2; cells 2, 3 stay physically present (out of range)
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_and_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 1)    ; IR: %10 = and i32 %4, 1  [index rail; zext %11 and gep %12 not emitted]
  %10 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i8(i32 %8, i32 %9)    ; IR: %13 = load i8, ptr %12: a[k & 1]  [result rail r]
  call void @cq_template_and_i32_hl_unc(i32 %9, i32 %4, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %10 (the load is a measured result, never un-copied)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %9)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  ; IR: call @free(%9): the lifetime of a ends
  call void @cqrt_qram_realloc_i8_unc(i32 %8, i32 4)    ; IR: undo the shrink (no store was made through a'): logical size 4
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i8_unc(i32 %5, i32 %6, i32 %7)    ; IR: pop a[k & 3] = v (its cell was never detached): every cell |0>
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release the seed v (rule 7)
  call void @cq_template_and_i32_hl_unc(i32 %6, i32 %4, i32 3)    ; IR: uncompute %6
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_qram_free(i32 %5)    ; IR: call @free(%9): release the QRAM a
  %11 = call i8 @cqrt_measure_i8(i32 %10)    ; IR: %14 = cq_measure_ui8(%13)
  %12 = zext i8 %11 to i32    ; IR: %15 = zext i8 %14 to i32  (classical)
  ret i32 %12    ; IR: ret i32 %15
}

define i32 @realloc_qsize(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i8 noundef zeroext %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [register k]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %4, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_alloc_i8(i32 2)    ; IR: %5 = call @malloc(2): the QRAM a, 2 byte cells |0>
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_and_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 1)    ; IR: %6 = and i32 %4, 1  [index rail; zext %7 and gep %8 not emitted]
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i8(i8 %2)    ; IR: store i8 %2, ptr %8: v as a basis-state handle
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i8(i32 %5, i32 %6, i32 %7)    ; IR: store i8 %2, ptr %8: a[k & 1] = v
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_and_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 3)    ; IR: %9 = and i32 %4, 3
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %8, i32 2)    ; IR: %10 = add nuw nsw i32 %9, 2  [the quantum size rail; zext %11 not emitted]
  %10 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_realloc_i8(i32 %5, i32 5)    ; IR: %12 = call @realloc(%5, %11): QUANTUM size in [2, 5], resized at its upper bound 5; cells 2..4 new |0>
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %9, i32 %8, i32 2)    ; IR: uncompute %10 (the realloc read only its bound)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %9)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  %11 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %8, i32 1)    ; IR: %13 = zext %9; %14 = gep %12, %13; %15 = gep %14, 1: cell index (k & 3) + 1
  %12 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i8(i8 7)    ; IR: store i8 7, ptr %15: 7 as a basis-state handle
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i8(i32 %10, i32 %11, i32 %12)    ; IR: store i8 7, ptr %15: a[(k & 3) + 1] = 7
  %13 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i8(i32 %10, i32 %6)    ; IR: %16 = gep %12, %7; %17 = load i8, ptr %16: a[k & 1]
  %14 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i8_hl(i32 %10, i32 1)    ; IR: %18 = gep %12, 1; %19 = load i8, ptr %18: a[1]
  %15 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i8(i32 %14, i32 %13)    ; IR: %20 = add i8 %19, %17  [result rail r]
  ; IR: call @free(%12): the lifetime of a ends; clean-up in reverse order of its accesses
  call void @cqrt_qram_load_i8_hl_unc(i32 %14, i32 %10, i32 1)    ; IR: un-copy %19
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %14)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_qram_load_i8_unc(i32 %13, i32 %10, i32 %6)    ; IR: un-copy %17
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %13)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i8_unc(i32 %10, i32 %11, i32 %12)    ; IR: pop a[(k & 3) + 1] = 7 (the store made through a')
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %12)    ; IR: release the seed 7 (rule 7)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %11, i32 %8, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute the cell index (k & 3) + 1
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %11)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_and_i32_hl_unc(i32 %8, i32 %4, i32 3)    ; IR: uncompute %9
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %8)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_qram_realloc_i8_unc(i32 %10, i32 2)    ; IR: undo the realloc: cells 2..4 are |0> and dropped
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i8_unc(i32 %5, i32 %6, i32 %7)    ; IR: pop a[k & 1] = v
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release the seed v (rule 7)
  call void @cq_template_and_i32_hl_unc(i32 %6, i32 %4, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %6
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_qram_free(i32 %5)    ; IR: call @free(%12): release the QRAM a
  %16 = call i8 @cqrt_measure_i8(i32 %15)    ; IR: %21 = cq_measure_ui8(%20)
  %17 = zext i8 %16 to i32    ; IR: %22 = zext i8 %21 to i32  (classical)
  ret i32 %17    ; IR: ret i32 %22
}

define i32 @vla_qram(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2, i32 noundef %3) {
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %5, double %1)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_alloc_i32(i32 %3)    ; IR: %6 = zext i32 %3 to i64; %7 = alloca i32, i64 %6: a QRAM of n cells, n known at run time
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_urem_i32_hl(i32 %5, i32 %3)    ; IR: %8 = urem i32 %5, %3  [index rail; zext %9 and gep %10 not emitted]
  %8 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %2)    ; IR: store i32 %2, ptr %10: y as a basis-state handle
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32(i32 %6, i32 %7, i32 %8)    ; IR: store i32 %2, ptr %10: a[x % n] = y
  %9 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i32_hl(i32 %6, i32 0)    ; IR: %11 = load i32, ptr %7: a[0]  [result rail]
  %10 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %9)    ; IR: %12 = cq_measure_si32(%11)
  ; IR: ret: the VLA's scope ends at the function return (rule 20); its clean-up runs here, after the measurement
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_unc(i32 %6, i32 %7, i32 %8)    ; IR: pop a[x % n] = y (the copy-out a[0] was measured: it stands)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %8)    ; IR: release the seed y (rule 7)
  call void @cq_template_urem_i32_hl_unc(i32 %7, i32 %5, i32 %3)    ; IR: uncompute %8
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_qram_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release the QRAM a
  ret i32 %10    ; IR: ret i32 %12
}

define i32 @guarded_global(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2, i32 noundef %3, double noundef %4, i32 noundef %5) {
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %7 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %7, double %1)    ; IR: %7 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %8 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %3)    ; IR: %8 = cq_theta_ui32(%3, %4)  [register i]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %8, double %4)    ; IR: %8 = cq_theta_ui32(%3, %4)  [Ry]
  %9 = load i32, ptr @table.qram, align 4    ; IR: @table  (the QRAM handle of the global, classical)
  %10 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_ugt_i32_hl(i32 %7, i32 %2)    ; IR: %9 = icmp ugt i32 %7, %2  [flag]
  %11 = call i32 @cq_template_and_i32_hl(i32 %8, i32 7)    ; IR: %11 = and i32 %8, 7  [block %10, pure: hoisted unguarded; zext %12 and gep %13 not emitted]
  %12 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %5)    ; IR: store i32 %5, ptr %13: y as a basis-state handle
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_controlled(i32 %10, i32 %9, i32 %11, i32 %12)    ; IR: store i32 %5, ptr %13 under %9: table[i & 7] = y iff x > k (never popped: the global persists)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %12)    ; IR: release the seed y (basis state; the store copied it)
  call void @cq_template_and_i32_hl_unc(i32 %11, i32 %8, i32 7)    ; IR: uncompute %11
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %11)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_ugt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %10, i32 %7, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %9 after its last controlled gate
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %10)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  %13 = call i32 @cq_template_and_i32_hl(i32 %8, i32 7)    ; IR: %15 = and i32 %8, 7  [block %14; zext %16 and gep %17 not emitted]
  %14 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i32(i32 %9, i32 %13)    ; IR: %18 = load i32, ptr %17: table[i & 7]  [result rail]
  call void @cq_template_and_i32_hl_unc(i32 %13, i32 %8, i32 7)    ; IR: uncompute %15 (the load is a measured result)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %13)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  %15 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %14)    ; IR: %19 = cq_measure_si32(%18)
  ret i32 %15    ; IR: ret i32 %19  (the QRAM table stays allocated: a global is an output)
}

;   measurements of the clone's result copies, classical sum).
; Clean: every rail but the registers (re; c and d) and the measured result rails: every flag, seed, product, select and
;   clone-internal rail, and (first entry) the __muldc3 result copies after the _unc twin, all freed.
; Kept: nothing beyond the registers and the measured rails: neither clone holds a loop (no a_K) or a rotation.
; Rotations: Ry(th) on re (first entry); Ry(tc) on c, Ry(td) on d (second entry). The clones hold no rotation.
; Rule 18 with the REAL builtin bodies. The .c defines neither __muldc3 nor __divdc3, so clang's calls reach compiler-rt's
; pinned 19.1.7 bodies in the injection bundle (cq_bundle_v1: @__muldc3 lines 7-139, @__divdc3 lines 140-547), and those are
; the bodies lifted here value for value: __compiler_rt_logb / __compiler_rt_scalbn / fmax are INLINE in them (bit tests
; on the i64 pattern, llvm.ctlz.i64 for the subnormal case, llvm.sadd.sat.i32 for the saturated exponent, llvm.smax.i32,
; llvm.copysign, llvm.fabs; no libm call and no nested clone), unlike 169-174, whose .c files define musl-shaped helpers
; and so witness the lifted-musl shape instead (§7: a reference that depicts another body pins nothing).
; Taint. First entry: z's real part re is the register, so `__muldc3(re, im, a, b)` is reached with mask 1000 (arg 0
; quantum; im, a and the real part a + b*0 of w are classical) -> __cq_q___muldc3_1000. clang -O1 emits Annex G's inline
; formula first (%11-%16: ac, ad quantum, bd, bc classical; the products are fmul_hl, the differences fsub_hl / fadd_hl
; with the classical factor as the literal, rule 4) and calls __muldc3 only on the NaN path `isnan(real) && isnan(imag)`
; (%17, %19: two fcmp uno flags, both quantum). The callee body has no non-pure gate (no rotation, phase, store or tape),
; so by rule 19 it is called UNGUARDED and its results are merged by select under the path predicate P20 = %17 & %19 (one
; and_i1 flag, rule 8): the two phis of %24 become one select_f64 each, the complement (the inline value) in the else arm.
; Second entry: c and d are the registers, b*0 + a is classical, so `__divdc3(a, b, c + d*0, d)` is reached with mask 0011
; -> __cq_q___divdc3_0011 (clang never inlines a complex divide). Nothing calls a twin of that clone, since both result
; copies are measured directly (as 169's c_qq), so none is defined (§1.4); __cq_q___muldc3_1000_unc is defined and called.
; Inside the clones every op with a handle operand is an out-of-place template into a fresh rail (rule 4; _hl/_lh with the
; classical value as the literal, a commutative op with the handle first, compares never _lh), every op on classical
; operands only stays classical IR, and a phi whose two arms are both classical values but whose edge is a quantum flag is
; a select_f64_ll into a fresh rail (rule 9: %32-%34 of __muldc3). llvm.fmuladd is UNFUSED (§2, cf. 14, 69, 169): an fmul
; into a fresh product rail, then an fadd of the product and the addend. The fcmp predicates (uno, ord-free here: uno,
; oeq, olt, ueq, une) are templates; `select i1 %a, i1 true, i1 %b` is the disjunction or_i1 and `select i1 %a, i1 %b,
; i1 false` / `and i1` the conjunction and_i1 into a fresh |0> flag (rule 8); a negated conjunct is an X bracket (not_i1)
; around the gate; a classical conjunct of a mixed condition is a seed rail (rule 7, as 169); the i1 phi %90 of __muldc3
; (`[false, %53], [false, %72], [true, %60]`) is the flag %59 & !%71. A flag read as data (%16, %38, %40 feed uitofp i1)
; is the compare's own rail. llvm.ctlz.i64 (zero-is-poison: the template is total, §2), llvm.sadd.sat.i32 and llvm.smax.i32
; on handles are the ctlz_i64, sadd_sat_i32 and smax_i32_hl templates. Merges follow the CFG: an if/else-if ladder into one
; exit nests its selects on the local flags, the deepest else innermost (rule 9: the %35 logb merge on %14/%16/%18, the
; four scalbn merges %88/%137/%192/%244 on their %47-shaped / %64 / %70 flags, the %135 merge on %37); the five-incoming
; phis of %302 (__divdc3) and %85/%99 (__muldc3) whose arms sit on disjoint path predicates (P254, P288, P270; P72; P91)
; are one select per distinct incoming on and_i1 chains of those predicates, the complement value (the plain quotient /
; product) innermost. Rule 6 does not fire: no rotated register is updated (re + im*0, c + d*0 are fadds, not bijections),
; and the clones' dead integer intermediates are rule-5 garbage uncomputed LIFO like every other rail (nothing is kept).
; Each clone copies its two results into fresh rails, uncomputes its whole chain LIFO (rule 5) and returns the copies; the
; first entry runs the twin (recompute, copy_f64 the results out, uncompute) and frees the copies before measuring the
; merged sum, the second measures the two copies after uncomputing its own garbage (%12, %11).

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
