define double @complex_mul_builtin(double noundef %0, double noundef %1, double noundef %2, double noundef %3, double noundef %4) {
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_f64(double %0)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_f64(%0, %1)  [register re]
  call void @cqrt_ry_f64(i32 %6, double %1)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_f64(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %7 = fmul double %2, 0.000000e+00    ; IR: %7 = fmul %2, 0.0  (im * I: real part im*0)  (classical)
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f64_hl(i32 %6, double %7)    ; IR: %8 = fadd %7, %6  (real part of z; commutative, handle first)
  %9 = fmul double %4, 0.000000e+00    ; IR: %9 = fmul %4, 0.0  (classical)
  %10 = fadd double %9, %3    ; IR: %10 = fadd %9, %3  (real part of w)  (classical)
  %11 = call i32 @cq_template_fmul_f64_hl(i32 %8, double %10)    ; IR: %11 = fmul %10, %8  (ac; commutative, handle first)
  %12 = fmul double %2, %4    ; IR: %12 = fmul %2, %4  (bd)  (classical)
  %13 = call i32 @cq_template_fmul_f64_hl(i32 %8, double %4)    ; IR: %13 = fmul %8, %4  (ad)
  %14 = fmul double %10, %2    ; IR: %14 = fmul %10, %2  (bc)  (classical)
  %15 = call i32 @cq_template_fsub_f64_hl(i32 %11, double %12)    ; IR: %15 = fsub %11, %12  (inline real part)
  %16 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f64_hl(i32 %13, double %14)    ; IR: %16 = fadd %14, %13  (inline imaginary part; commutative, handle first)
  %17 = call i32 @cq_template_fcmp_uno_f64_hl(i32 %15, double 0.000000e+00)    ; IR: %17 = fcmp uno %15, 0  [br %17 -> block %18, else exit %24]
  %18 = call i32 @cq_template_fcmp_uno_f64_hl(i32 %16, double 0.000000e+00)    ; IR: %19 = fcmp uno %16, 0  (block %18)  [br %19 -> block %20, else %24]
  %19 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: P20 = path predicate of block %20 (the __muldc3 call): %17 & %19  [fresh flag rail]
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %17, i32 %18, i32 %19)    ; IR: P20 = path predicate of block %20 (the __muldc3 call): %17 & %19
  %20 = call fastcc { i32, i32 } @__cq_q___muldc3_1000(i32 %8, double %2, double %10, double %4)    ; IR: %21 = call @__muldc3(%8, %2, %10, %4) in block %20: the pinned compiler-rt body, lifted with mask 1000 (arg 0 quantum); no non-pure gate in the body, so it runs unguarded (rule 19) and P20 steers the merge
  %21 = extractvalue { i32, i32 } %20, 0    ; IR: extractvalue %21, 0  (handle; classical)
  %22 = extractvalue { i32, i32 } %20, 1    ; IR: extractvalue %21, 1  (handle; classical)
  %23 = call i32 @cq_template_select_f64(i32 %19, i32 %21, i32 %15)    ; IR: %25 = phi [ %15, %5 ], [ %15, %18 ], [ %22, %20 ]  (real part of p)
  %24 = call i32 @cq_template_select_f64(i32 %19, i32 %22, i32 %16)    ; IR: %26 = phi [ %16, %5 ], [ %16, %18 ], [ %23, %20 ]  (imaginary part of p)
  %25 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f64(i32 %23, i32 %24)    ; IR: %27 = fadd %25, %26  [result rail]
  call void @cq_template_select_f64_unc(i32 %24, i32 %19, i32 %22, i32 %16)    ; IR: uncompute %26
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %24)    ; IR: release the %26 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_select_f64_unc(i32 %23, i32 %19, i32 %21, i32 %15)    ; IR: uncompute %25
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %23)    ; IR: release the %25 rail (|0>)
  call fastcc void @__cq_q___muldc3_1000_unc(i32 %21, i32 %22, i32 %8, double %2, double %10, double %4)    ; IR: uncompute the result rails of %21 (the _unc twin recomputes and XORs them out)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %21)    ; IR: release the %21 result copy (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %22)    ; IR: release the %21 result copy (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %17, i32 %18, i32 %19)    ; IR: uncompute P20  [self-inverse]
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %19)    ; IR: release the P20 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_fcmp_uno_f64_hl_unc(i32 %18, i32 %16, double 0.000000e+00)    ; IR: uncompute %19
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %18)    ; IR: release the %19 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_fcmp_uno_f64_hl_unc(i32 %17, i32 %15, double 0.000000e+00)    ; IR: uncompute %17
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %17)    ; IR: release the %17 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_fadd_f64_hl_unc(i32 %16, i32 %13, double %14)    ; IR: uncompute %16
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %16)    ; IR: release the %16 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_fsub_f64_hl_unc(i32 %15, i32 %11, double %12)    ; IR: uncompute %15
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %15)    ; IR: release the %15 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_fmul_f64_hl_unc(i32 %13, i32 %8, double %4)    ; IR: uncompute %13
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %13)    ; IR: release the %13 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_fmul_f64_hl_unc(i32 %11, i32 %8, double %10)    ; IR: uncompute %11
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %11)    ; IR: release the %11 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_fadd_f64_hl_unc(i32 %8, i32 %6, double %7)    ; IR: uncompute %8
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %8)    ; IR: release the %8 rail (|0>)
  %26 = call double @cqrt_measure_f64(i32 %25)    ; IR: %28 = cq_measure_f64(%27)
  ret double %26    ; IR: ret double %28
}

define double @complex_div_builtin(double noundef %0, double noundef %1, double noundef %2, double noundef %3, double noundef %4, double noundef %5) {
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_f64(double %2)    ; IR: %7 = cq_theta_f64(%2, %3)  [register c]
  call void @cqrt_ry_f64(i32 %7, double %3)    ; IR: %7 = cq_theta_f64(%2, %3)  [Ry]
  %8 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_f64(double %4)    ; IR: %8 = cq_theta_f64(%4, %5)  [register d]
  call void @cqrt_ry_f64(i32 %8, double %5)    ; IR: %8 = cq_theta_f64(%4, %5)  [Ry]
  %9 = fmul double %1, 0.000000e+00    ; IR: %9 = fmul %1, 0.0  (classical)
  %10 = fadd double %9, %0    ; IR: %10 = fadd %9, %0  (real part of z)  (classical)
  %11 = call i32 @cq_template_fmul_f64_hl(i32 %8, double 0.000000e+00)    ; IR: %11 = fmul %8, 0.0  (d * I: real part d*0)
  %12 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f64(i32 %7, i32 %11)    ; IR: %12 = fadd %7, %11  (real part of w)
  %13 = call fastcc { i32, i32 } @__cq_q___divdc3_0011(double %10, double %1, i32 %12, i32 %8)    ; IR: %13 = call @__divdc3(%10, %1, %12, %8): the pinned compiler-rt body, lifted with mask 0011 (args 2 and 3 quantum); both result rails are measured below, so the twin never runs
  %14 = extractvalue { i32, i32 } %13, 0    ; IR: extractvalue %13, 0  (handle; classical)
  %15 = extractvalue { i32, i32 } %13, 1    ; IR: extractvalue %13, 1  (handle; classical)
  call void @cq_template_fadd_f64_unc(i32 %12, i32 %7, i32 %11)    ; IR: uncompute %12
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %12)    ; IR: release the %12 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_fmul_f64_hl_unc(i32 %11, i32 %8, double 0.000000e+00)    ; IR: uncompute %11
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %11)    ; IR: release the %11 rail (|0>)
  %16 = call double @cqrt_measure_f64(i32 %14)    ; IR: %16 = cq_measure_f64(%14)
  %17 = call double @cqrt_measure_f64(i32 %15)    ; IR: %17 = cq_measure_f64(%15)
  %18 = fadd double %16, %17    ; IR: %18 = fadd %16, %17  (two outcomes)  (classical)
  ret double %18    ; IR: ret double %18
}

define internal fastcc { i32, i32 } @__cq_q___muldc3_1000(i32 %0, double %1, double %2, double %3) {
  %5 = call i32 @cq_template_fmul_f64_hl(i32 %0, double %2)    ; IR: %5 = fmul a, c  (ac)
  %6 = fmul double %1, %3    ; IR: %6 = fmul b, d  (bd)  (classical)
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_fmul_f64_hl(i32 %0, double %3)    ; IR: %7 = fmul a, d  (ad)

  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_fsub_f64_hl(i32 %5, double %6)    ; IR: %9 = fsub %5, %6  (ac - bd)
  %10 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f64_hl(i32 %7, double %8)    ; IR: %10 = fadd %8, %7  (ad + bc; commutative, handle first)

  %12 = call i32 @cq_template_fcmp_uno_f64_hl(i32 %10, double 0.000000e+00)    ; IR: %12 = fcmp uno %10, 0  (isnan(imag))
  %13 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: %13 = and i1 %11, %12  [br %13 -> block %14 (recover), else exit %99]  [fresh flag rail]
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %11, i32 %12, i32 %13)    ; IR: %13 = and i1 %11, %12  [br %13 -> block %14 (recover), else exit %99]
  %14 = call i32 @cq_template_fabs_f64(i32 %0)    ; IR: %15 = fabs(a)  (block %14)
  %15 = call i32 @cq_template_fcmp_oeq_f64_hl(i32 %14, double 0x7FF0000000000000)    ; IR: %16 = fcmp oeq %15, inf  (isinf(a); a flag read as data by %21 too)
  %16 = tail call double @llvm.fabs.f64(double %1)    ; IR: %17 = fabs(b)  (classical)
  %17 = fcmp oeq double %16, 0x7FF0000000000000    ; IR: %18 = fcmp oeq %17, inf  (isinf(b))  (classical)
  %18 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 %17)    ; IR: %19 = or i1 %16, %18: the classical disjunct %18  [the classical conjunct as a seed rail, rule 7]
  %19 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: %19 = or i1 %16, %18  [br %19 -> block %20, else %31]  [fresh flag rail]

  %20 = call i32 @cq_template_uitofp_i1_to_f64(i32 %15)    ; IR: %21 = uitofp i1 %16 to double  (block %20)
  %21 = call i32 @cq_template_copysign_f64(i32 %20, i32 %0)    ; IR: %22 = copysign(%21, a)
  %22 = uitofp i1 %17 to double    ; IR: %23 = uitofp i1 %18 to double  (classical)
  %23 = tail call double @llvm.copysign.f64(double %22, double %1)    ; IR: %24 = copysign(%23, b)  (classical)

  %26 = select i1 %24, double %25, double %2    ; IR: %27 = select %25, %26, c  (classical)
  %27 = fcmp uno double %3, 0.000000e+00    ; IR: %28 = fcmp uno d, 0  (classical)

  %29 = select i1 %27, double %28, double %3    ; IR: %30 = select %28, %29, d  (classical)
  %30 = call i32 @cq_template_select_f64_ll(i32 %19, double %29, double %3)    ; IR: %32 = phi [ %30, %20 ], [ %3, %14 ]  (d after step 1; two classical arms under a quantum flag)
  %31 = call i32 @cq_template_select_f64_ll(i32 %19, double %26, double %2)    ; IR: %33 = phi [ %27, %20 ], [ %2, %14 ]  (c after step 1)

  %35 = call i32 @cq_template_fabs_f64(i32 %31)    ; IR: %37 = fabs(%33)

  %37 = call i32 @cq_template_fabs_f64(i32 %30)    ; IR: %39 = fabs(%32)
  %38 = call i32 @cq_template_fcmp_oeq_f64_hl(i32 %37, double 0x7FF0000000000000)    ; IR: %40 = fcmp oeq %39, inf  (isinf(d))
  %39 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: %41 = or i1 %40, %38  [br %41 -> block %42, else %53]  [fresh flag rail]
  call void @cqrt_or_i1(i32 %38, i32 %36, i32 %39)    ; IR: %41 = or i1 %40, %38  [br %41 -> block %42, else %53]
  %40 = call i32 @cq_template_uitofp_i1_to_f64(i32 %36)    ; IR: %43 = uitofp i1 %38 to double  (block %42)
  %41 = call i32 @cq_template_copysign_f64(i32 %40, i32 %31)    ; IR: %44 = copysign(%43, %33)
  %42 = call i32 @cq_template_uitofp_i1_to_f64(i32 %38)    ; IR: %45 = uitofp i1 %40 to double

  %49 = call i32 @cq_template_select_f64(i32 %47, i32 %48, i32 %32)    ; IR: %52 = select %50, %51, %34
  %50 = call i32 @cq_template_select_f64(i32 %39, i32 %43, i32 %30)    ; IR: %54 = phi [ %46, %42 ], [ %32, %31 ]  (d after step 2)
  %51 = call i32 @cq_template_select_f64(i32 %39, i32 %41, i32 %31)    ; IR: %55 = phi [ %44, %42 ], [ %33, %31 ]  (c after step 2)
  %52 = call i32 @cq_template_select_f64(i32 %39, i32 %49, i32 %32)    ; IR: %56 = phi [ %52, %42 ], [ %34, %31 ]  (b after step 2)

  %54 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_lh(i32 %39, i32 1, i32 %34)    ; IR: %58 = phi i32 [ 1, %42 ], [ %36, %31 ]  (recalc)
  %55 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %54, i32 0)    ; IR: %59 = icmp eq %58, 0  (!recalc)  [br %59 -> block %60, else %85]
  %56 = call i32 @cq_template_fabs_f64(i32 %5)    ; IR: %61 = fabs(%5)  (block %60)
  %57 = call i32 @cq_template_fcmp_oeq_f64_hl(i32 %56, double 0x7FF0000000000000)    ; IR: %62 = fcmp oeq %61, inf  (isinf(ac))
  %58 = tail call double @llvm.fabs.f64(double %6)    ; IR: %63 = fabs(%6)  (classical)
  %59 = fcmp oeq double %58, 0x7FF0000000000000    ; IR: %64 = fcmp oeq %63, inf  (isinf(bd))  (classical)
  %60 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 %59)    ; IR: %65 = or i1 %62, %64: the classical disjunct %64  [the classical conjunct as a seed rail, rule 7]

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 1, 2, 4, 25.
; Checked: fadd_f32: x + c (measured, %5 -> %6); fadd_f80: x + c (measured, %5 -> %6); fmul_f80_qq: x * y (measured, %7 -> %8).
; Clean: none to free: each entry computes exactly one template into the rail it measures.
; Kept: the registers (x %4 in fadd_f32 and fadd_f80; x %5 and y %6 in fmul_f80_qq) and the three measured result rails.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1) in fadd_f32; (Ry, x, th, 1) in fadd_f80; (Ry, x, tx, 1), (Ry, y, ty, 1) in fmul_f80_qq.
; Floating-point widths are width variants of the same ABI (rule 25): cq_theta on a float mints alloc_f32 and rotates
; with cqrt_ry_f32, on a long double alloc_f80 / cqrt_ry_f80 (x86_fp80 literals and handles). The mixed Q+C adds are
; _hl fadd templates with the classical c as a literal; the quantum-quantum product is the two-handle fmul_f80 template.
source_filename = "fp_widths.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

; Function Attrs: nounwind ssp uwtable
define float @fadd_f32(float noundef %0, double noundef %1, float noundef %2) local_unnamed_addr #0 {
  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_f32(float %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_f32(%0, %1)  [register]
  call void @cqrt_ry_f32(i32 %4, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_f32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %5 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f32_hl(i32 %4, float %2)    ; IR: %5 = fadd float %4, %2
  %6 = call float @cqrt_measure_f32(i32 %5)    ; IR: %6 = cq_measure_f32(%5)
  ret float %6    ; IR: ret float %6
}

; Function Attrs: nounwind ssp uwtable
define x86_fp80 @fadd_f80(x86_fp80 noundef %0, double noundef %1, x86_fp80 noundef %2) local_unnamed_addr #0 {
  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_f80(x86_fp80 %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_f80(%0, %1)  [register]
  call void @cqrt_ry_f80(i32 %4, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_f80(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %5 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f80_hl(i32 %4, x86_fp80 %2)    ; IR: %5 = fadd x86_fp80 %4, %2
  %6 = call x86_fp80 @cqrt_measure_f80(i32 %5)    ; IR: %6 = cq_measure_f80(%5)
  ret x86_fp80 %6    ; IR: ret x86_fp80 %6
}

; Function Attrs: nounwind ssp uwtable

name: 28_horner_accumulator
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 14, 4, 5, 7, 2.
; Checked: s = Horner evaluation of coef[0..n-1] at x (measured).
; Clean: every trip's accumulator rail and product rail s * x (both popped and uncomputed by the mirror, the sum
; before the product it read) and the seed rail holding coef[0] (never written, freed directly, rule 7).
; Kept: the user register x; the copied-out result rail (measured).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x.
; coef is classical memory read with a classical index, so each coefficient is an ordinary load passed as a literal
; (the fadd's _hl shape, rule 4). clang contracts s * x + coef[i] into llvm.fmuladd.f64, which is UNFUSED (§2): each
; trip is an fmul into a fresh product rail and an fadd_hl of the product and coef[i] into a fresh accumulator rail.
; The accumulator chain is a classical loop with the handle stack (rule 14, classical bound): each trip pushes the old
; accumulator and its product rail, and the mirror (after the result is copied out) pops them and uncomputes the sum
; then the product (rule 5, dependency order). n <= 1 takes the classical edge and
; measures the seed rail itself.
source_filename = "horner_accumulator.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

  call void @cqrt_ry_f64(i32 %5, double %1)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_f64(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %6 = load double, ptr %2, align 8    ; IR: %6 = load double, ptr %2  (classical)
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_f64(double %6)    ; IR: incoming %6 of phi %15 / %11  [s before trip 1]
  %8 = icmp sgt i32 %3, 1    ; IR: %7 = icmp sgt i32 %3, 1
  br i1 %8, label %11, label %9    ; IR: br i1 %7, label %8, label %10

9:
  %10 = call double @cqrt_measure_f64(i32 %7)    ; IR: %12 = cq_measure_f64(%11), %11 = %6 from %4
  ret double %10    ; IR: ret double %12

11:
  %12 = zext nneg i32 %3 to i64    ; IR: %9 = zext nneg i32 %3 to i64
  br label %13

13:
  %14 = phi i64 [ 1, %11 ], [ %20, %13 ]    ; IR: %14 = phi i64 [ 1, %8 ], [ %19, %13 ]  (classical)
  %15 = phi i32 [ %7, %11 ], [ %19, %13 ]    ; IR: %15 = phi double [ %6, %8 ], [ %18, %13 ]
  %16 = getelementptr inbounds double, ptr %2, i64 %14    ; IR: %16 = getelementptr inbounds double, ptr %2, i64 %14
  %17 = load double, ptr %16, align 8    ; IR: %17 = load double, ptr %16  (classical)
  %18 = call i32 @cq_template_fmul_f64(i32 %15, i32 %5)    ; IR: %18 = llvm.fmuladd.f64(%15, %5, %17)  [product s * x]
  %19 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f64_hl(i32 %18, double %17)    ; IR: %18 = llvm.fmuladd.f64(%15, %5, %17)  [sum + coef[i]]
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %15)    ; IR: %15 [old accumulator, kept for the mirror]
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %18)    ; IR: %18 [product rail, kept for the mirror]
  %20 = add nuw nsw i64 %14, 1    ; IR: %19 = add nuw nsw i64 %14, 1
  %21 = icmp eq i64 %20, %12    ; IR: %20 = icmp eq i64 %19, %9
  br i1 %21, label %22, label %13    ; IR: br i1 %20, label %10, label %13

  call void @cqrt_copy_f64(i32 %19, i32 %23)    ; IR: %11
  br label %24

  %26 = phi i32 [ %19, %22 ], [ %30, %24 ]

  %28 = load double, ptr %27, align 8    ; IR: %17 of that trip (classical)
  %29 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: that trip's product rail
  %30 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: that trip's %15
  call void @cq_template_fadd_f64_hl_unc(i32 %26, i32 %29, double %28)    ; IR: uncompute %18 [sum]
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %26)    ; IR: release the %18 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_fmul_f64_unc(i32 %29, i32 %30, i32 %5)    ; IR: uncompute %18 [product]
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %29)    ; IR: release the product rail (|0>)

  %32 = icmp sgt i64 %31, 0
  br i1 %32, label %24, label %33

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %30)    ; IR: release the first s rail (never written, holds the classical %6)

  ret double %34    ; IR: ret double %12
}

; A constant table read with a quantum index is a QROM: the classical table is passed as a pointer literal and the
; quantum index selects the entry into a fresh rail. The index operand is the logical index rail at the width of the C

name: 30_local_array_quantum_index
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 4, 5, 7, 20, 22.
; Checked: local_array_quantum_index: v = arr[x & 3] (measured, %13 -> %14); local_array_quantum_write: arr[0] + arr[2]
; (measured, %11 -> %12).
; Clean: local_array_quantum_index: the index rail %12. local_array_quantum_write: the two fixed-index load rails %9, %10,
; the store's value handle %8 (basis state a, freed once its store is popped), the shared memset handle %5 (basis state
; 0, freed once its four stores are popped), the index rail %7, every store's tape slot (each pop returns it to |0>), and
; the 4-cell QRAM %4 (every cell back to |0> after every store is popped, then qram_free).
; Kept: x (%6 in each entry, the rotated register) and the two measured result rails; nothing else.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1) in each entry.
; A local array of classical values that is only READ at a quantum index stays classical memory and the read is a QROM
; over its contents at the load, not a QRAM, BECAUSE the array only ever holds classical values (rule 20: no store at a
; quantum index, no cell holding a quantum value, no quantum pointer into it; a, b, a + b, a * b are classical)
; (cq_template_qrom_load: table literal, length = the object's 4 cells, logical index rail x & 3 at the C expression's
; i32 width, fresh rail; -O1's zext to i64 and the gep scaling are address arithmetic and are not emitted, the same
; index form as the write). An array WRITTEN at a quantum index is a QRAM (address decoding is the backend's circuit;
; the ABI is the QRAM contract of §1.3): cqrt_qram_alloc_<W>(n) at the alloca (cells |0>). The initializer
; `= {0, 0, 0, 0}` is -O1's llvm.memset(arr, 0, 16): a memory intrinsic with a classical length over a QRAM is one
; cqrt_qram_store_<W>_hl(arr, j, val) per cell (rule 22; _hl = classical index), all four reading ONE basis-state
; handle cqrt_alloc_i32(0) (a store value is always a handle; a classical value is materialised once and shared, and
; freed after its last store is popped). The memset is emitted even though the cells already hold 0: every store owns
; a tape slot and the stores are part of the circuit the C program denotes. The quantum-index store is ONE
; cqrt_qram_store_<W>(arr, idx, val) with the logical-i32 index rail (x & 3) and the value a as a basis-state handle.
; Each store owns a fresh tape slot: the displaced cell is swapped into the slot, then the cell takes cell ^= val (a
; copy; val unchanged), so the store is a permutation of (cells, tape slots), not of the cells alone. A fixed-index read

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 18, 20, 5, §1.4.
; Checked: lo + hi (measured, %8 -> %9).
; Clean: the clone's result rail %6 (lo) and the hi rail %7 loaded from the slot, both zeroed by the clone's _unc twin and
; freed by the caller; inside the clone and its twin the shifted rail (%4) and the masked rail (%7) are uncomputed and
; freed.
; Kept: x (%5, the rotated register) and the sum rail %8 (measured); nothing else.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; The out-parameter is a non-escaping alloca: a classical slot, and because the
; callee stores a quantum value into it, the slot holds the HANDLE of that rail. The clone __cq_q_split_100 (mask left to
; right, §1.4: v quantum, k classical, the slot carries no quantum field on entry) writes the handle, the caller loads it.
; The body has two templates, so BOTH results are copied out (rule 18): v >> k into a fresh rail whose handle goes into
; the slot, and the masked value into the returned rail; the clone then uncomputes its ashr and and rails.
; Both results are garbage after the add, so the caller runs the clone's _unc twin, which takes (out, args, old slot
; handle): it zeroes the returned rail and the slot's rail by recomputation and restores the slot's content from before
; the call (hi was never written, so the caller passes poison). The caller then frees both rails.

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release the %6 rail (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release the hi rail (|0>)

  %7 = xor i32 %6, -1    ; IR: %6 = xor i32 %5, -1  (classical)

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 4, 6.
; Checked: second_rotation: x (%4, measured as %5); rotate_derived: y = x + c (%6, measured as %8); rotate_double: x (%4,
; measured as %5).
; Clean: rotate_derived: the old x rail (%5, rule 6: |0> after the copy) and the inverse t (%7), both freed. Nothing else
; to free in the other two: every rail is a user register.
; Kept: second_rotation: x (%4, measured); rotate_derived: y (%6, rotated then measured); rotate_double: x (%4, measured).
; Rotations: second_rotation: (Ry, x, t1, 1); (Ry, x, t2, 1). rotate_derived: (Ry, x, t1, 1); (Ry, y = x + c, t2, 1).
; rotate_double: (Ry_f64, x, t1, 1); (Ry_f64, x, t2, 1).
; A second cq_theta on a register that is already a handle is a second Ry on the same rail (rule 2: a rotation of an
; existing handle is in place). A cq_theta on a derived value (y = x + c, an out-of-place _hl add into a fresh rail by
; rule 4) rotates that fresh rail, which is a user register from then on. x is dead after the add and y = x + c is a
; bijection in x for fixed c, so rule 6 cleans the old x rail BEFORE the Ry on y: t = y - c recomputes x, copy_i32 zeroes
; x, t is uncomputed. Keeping x would leave a which-path record of y: the Ry(t2) would act on a dephased y (1-bit view,
; t1 = t2 = pi/2, c = 1: cleaned, y = X Ry(pi/2)|0> and Ry(pi/2) gives |1> with probability 1; kept, 1/2).

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"

  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %4, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %4, double %2)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_si32(%4, %2)  [second Ry on the same rail]
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %4)    ; IR: %6 = cq_measure_si32(%5)
  ret i32 %5    ; IR: ret i32 %6
}

; Function Attrs: nounwind ssp uwtable

  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %7, i32 %5)    ; IR: rule 6: x ^= t: the dead x rail is now |0>

; Ry(ta) on r under (x > k); Ry(tb) on r under NOT (x > k).
; A rotation under a quantum condition is a controlled Ry on the single target rail seeded with r0 (rule 10); the else
; arm is the same gate under the negated flag (an X bracket on the flag, rule 8). One rail for r in both arms, no

  call void @cqrt_ry_i32_controlled(i32 %7, i32 %8, double %4)    ; IR: block %8: %9 = cq_theta_si32(%3, %4)  [Ry under the predicate]
  call void @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %7, i32 %6, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %7

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 3, 4, 5, 20.
; Checked: r = x * c + HALF[sb] (%9, measured as %10).
; Clean: the bitcast of x (%5), the sign-bit index lshr (%6), the QROM load (%7) and the product rail x * c (%8), all
; uncomputed and freed.
; Kept: x (%4, the rotated register, a source of r) and r (%9, measured).
; Rotations: (Ry_f64, x, th, 1).
; A constant table of doubles read with a quantum index is a QROM over the classical table, the f64 width of 29's
; cq_template_qrom_load_<W>(ptr table, i64 n, idx). The index operand is the logical index rail (rule 20): the C index
; expression is sb = (unsigned)(bits >> 63); -O1 folds its trunc/zext pair into the i64 shift itself, so the rail is the
; lshr result and no cast and no gep scaling is emitted. The fmuladd that consumes the loaded entry is UNFUSED (§2, cf.
; 14): fmul_f64_hl of x and the literal c into a fresh product rail, then fadd_f64 of the product and the loaded entry
; (its quantum addend) into the result rail; the product rail is uncomputed by its fmul _unc and freed (rule 5).
source_filename = "table_f64.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_fmul_f64_hl(i32 %4, double %2)    ; IR: %9 = llvm.fmuladd.f64(%4, %2, %8)  [product x * c]
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f64(i32 %8, i32 %7)    ; IR: %9 = llvm.fmuladd.f64(%4, %2, %8)  [sum + HALF[sb], result rail]

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release the %8 rail (|0>)

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release the %6 rail (|0>)

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 14, 8, 7, 5, 2.
; Checked: y = x_K * c (the copied-out product of the carried x after K trips, %29, measured as %63).
; Clean: every trip rail except a_K: the path flags, products, the second compare, cont, the two candidate updates,
; the inner and carried selects, the chain predicates a_0..a_{K-1} (trips K..1 popped and uncomputed by the reverse
; loop; trip 0's test and a_0 uncomputed after it), and the |1> seed (%7) freed directly.
; Kept: x (%6, the rotated register); y (%29, measured); a_K (%27 of the K-th trip, %38 of the first reverse trip), the
; output rail of rule 14: the continue test evaluated after the K-th body, 1 iff the retry loop would run a (K+1)-th trip.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; Both gotos reach the header through one latch block (%12) that merges the two continue paths, so this is one rolled
; K-bounded loop (as example 05) whose CONTINUE predicate is the disjunction of the two path conditions:
; cont = (x > k) | (x*c > m), one or_i1 into a fresh |0> flag (rule 8; the second goto's own path predicate
; !(x > k) & (x*c > m) is not materialised, the OR absorbs it). -O1 tests at the header with no pre-header guard, so the
; loop is re-rolled to body-then-test (rule 14): the FIRST header evaluation (x_0 > k, x_0 * c, x_0 * c > m, cont_0) is
; computed before the loop as trip 0 of the chain, a_0 = seed & cont_0 from the |1> seed; trip j (j = 1..K) runs the
; body under a_{j-1} (the latch value x' = p1 ? x-k : x>>1 on the path flag of the CURRENT x, selected into the carried
; x only where a_{j-1} = 1) and then the NEXT header evaluation on the new x, a_j = a_{j-1} & cont_j. The path flag and
; the product of each test are carried into the next trip (the body's inner select reads the flag; the product of the
; last test is y). K = 4 (the literal 4 below).
; Output rail (rule 14): after the K-th body the chain ends in cont_K, the test admitting trip K + 1; a_K = a_{K-1} &
; cont_K is kept allocated, neither uncomputed nor freed: a_K = 1 means the retry loop would still continue after K
; trips; a loop that exits after exactly K trips reads 0. y is the value of x*c at the exit: the carried x stops
; changing once the loop has exited, so y = x_K * c, the product of the K-th test, copied out (alloc + copy) and
; measured. The reverse loop pops trips K..1 and skips the predicate uncompute on its first iteration (reverse index 0)
; by a classical branch; trip 0's test and a_0 are uncomputed after it and the |1> seed is freed directly (rule 7).

  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %6, double %1)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 true)    ; IR: predicate of reaching recompute the first time (always 1)
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %6, i32 %2)    ; IR: %9 = icmp sgt i32 %8, %2 at recompute the first time: trip 0 of the chain  [path 1 predicate, block %10]
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i32_hl(i32 %6, i32 %3)    ; IR: %15 = mul nsw i32 %8, %3  (block %14, pure, hoisted)
  %10 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %9, i32 %4)    ; IR: %16 = icmp sgt i32 %15, %4
  %11 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: block %12 is reached = path 1 OR path 2: cont = %9 | %16 (rule 8)
  call void @cqrt_or_i1(i32 %8, i32 %10, i32 %11)    ; IR: cont ^= %9 | %16
  %12 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: a_0 = predicate of the first back edge
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %7, i32 %11, i32 %12)    ; IR: br label %7 from %12 taken the first time
  br label %13

13:

  %15 = phi i32 [ %6, %5 ], [ %22, %13 ]    ; IR: %8 = phi i32 [ %6, %5 ], [ %13, %12 ]
  %16 = phi i32 [ %12, %5 ], [ %27, %13 ]    ; IR: a_{j-1}: predicate of this trip's body (the back edge that reaches it)
  %17 = phi i32 [ %8, %5 ], [ %23, %13 ]    ; IR: %9 of the current x (path 1 flag, computed by the previous test)
  %18 = phi i32 [ %9, %5 ], [ %24, %13 ]    ; IR: %15 of the current x (computed by the previous test)
  %19 = call i32 @cq_template_sub_i32_hl(i32 %15, i32 %2)    ; IR: %11 = sub nsw i32 %8, %2
  %20 = call i32 @cq_template_ashr_i32_hl(i32 %15, i32 1)    ; IR: %18 = ashr i32 %8, 1

  %22 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %16, i32 %21, i32 %15)    ; IR: next %8 = a ? %13 : %8
  %23 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %22, i32 %2)    ; IR: %9 = icmp sgt i32 %8, %2 at the next recompute: the test after this body
  %24 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i32_hl(i32 %22, i32 %3)    ; IR: %15 = mul nsw i32 %8, %3 of the next header
  %25 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %24, i32 %4)    ; IR: %16 = icmp sgt i32 %15, %4
  %26 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: cont of the next header = %9 | %16 (rule 8)
  call void @cqrt_or_i1(i32 %23, i32 %25, i32 %26)    ; IR: cont ^= %9 | %16
  %27 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: a_j = predicate of the next back edge (after trip K: a_K, the output rail)
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %16, i32 %26, i32 %27)    ; IR: br label %7 from %12 taken once more
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %15)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %16)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %17)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %18)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %19)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %20)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %21)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %25)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %26)
  %28 = add nuw nsw i32 %14, 1
  %29 = icmp ult i32 %28, 4    ; IR: K-bounded br label %7  [K]
  br i1 %29, label %13, label %30

30:
  %31 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: %15 = mul nsw i32 %8, %3 of the exiting trip  [copied-out result rail]
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %24, i32 %31)    ; IR: %15: y = x_K * c, the product of the K-th test
  br label %32

32:
  %33 = phi i32 [ 0, %30 ], [ %50, %49 ]    ; IR: reverse trip index
  %34 = phi i32 [ %22, %30 ], [ %46, %49 ]    ; IR: %8 written by this trip
  %35 = phi i32 [ %27, %30 ], [ %45, %49 ]    ; IR: a_j, the predicate computed by this trip's test
  %36 = phi i32 [ %23, %30 ], [ %44, %49 ]    ; IR: %9 computed by this trip's test
  %37 = phi i32 [ %24, %30 ], [ %43, %49 ]    ; IR: %15 computed by this trip's test
  %38 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %39 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %40 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %41 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %42 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %43 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %44 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %45 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %46 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %47 = icmp eq i32 %33, 0    ; IR: reverse index 0 is trip K: its a_j is a_K, the output rail (rule 14)
  br i1 %47, label %49, label %48

48:

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %35)    ; IR: release it (|0>)

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %38)    ; IR: release cont (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %39, i32 %37, i32 %4)    ; IR: uncompute %16
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %39)    ; IR: release %16 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_mul_i32_hl_unc(i32 %37, i32 %34, i32 %3)    ; IR: uncompute %15
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %37)    ; IR: release %15 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %36, i32 %34, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %9
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %36)    ; IR: release %9 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %34, i32 %45, i32 %40, i32 %46)    ; IR: uncompute next %8
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %34)    ; IR: release next %8 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %40, i32 %44, i32 %42, i32 %41)    ; IR: uncompute %13
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %40)    ; IR: release %13 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_ashr_i32_hl_unc(i32 %41, i32 %46, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %18
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %41)    ; IR: release %18 (|0>)

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %42)    ; IR: release %11 (|0>)

  %51 = icmp ult i32 %50, 4    ; IR: K  [K]

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %12)    ; IR: release a_0 (|0>)

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %11)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %10, i32 %9, i32 %4)    ; IR: uncompute the first %16
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %10)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_mul_i32_hl_unc(i32 %9, i32 %6, i32 %3)    ; IR: uncompute the first %15
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %9)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %8, i32 %6, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute the first %9

name: 55_array_in_quantum_loop
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 20, 22, 14 (a_K kept), 8, 4, 5, 7, 2.
; Checked: a[m - 1] after the K-bounded loop a[i] = i * c, i = 0..m (measured).
; Clean: the guard flag m < 0, the hoisted bound m + 1 and its zext, the index rail m - 1, every trip's latch flag and
; basis-state store value (rule 7), the shared memset handle 0 (rule 7), the next-trip predicates a_1..a_{K-1}, every
; store's tape slot (each pop returns it to |0>), and the QRAM a (every store popped, then cqrt_qram_free).
; Kept: the user register m; the loaded result rail (measured); the LAST trip predicate a_K (rule 14: a_K = 1 means the
; loop had not exited after K trips, which is observable; the trip count m + 1 has no range bound, so B is unknown and
; a_K is kept). a_K is the predicate computed by the last forward trip, the first popped in the reverse loop (reverse
; index K - 1); the reverse loop skips its and_i1 uncompute and its free by a classical branch and leaves it allocated.
; Rotations: Ry(th) on m.
; The array's cells become quantum (written under the trip predicate of a quantum-bounded loop, then read at a quantum
; index), so the array is a QRAM (rule 20; address decoding is the backend's circuit; ABI = the QRAM contract of §1.3,
; reference conversions 30 and 84): cqrt_qram_alloc_<W>(4) at the alloca (cells |0>) and every access ONE call. The
; initializer `= {0, 0, 0, 0}` is -O1's llvm.memset(a, 0, 16), a memory intrinsic with a classical length: one
; cqrt_qram_store_<W>_hl(arr, j, val) per cell (rule 22), all four reading ONE basis-state handle cqrt_alloc_i32(0)
; (shared; freed after its last store is popped). The loop's bound is quantum (m + 1 trips), so it is the rolled
; K-bounded loop of example 05 (rule 14), unchanged: its first predicate is NOT (m < 0) (an X bracket on the guard
; flag) and the next predicate is a_j & NOT (j + 1 == m + 1). Inside a trip the store index i = j is the CLASSICAL trip
; counter and the stored value i*c is classical, so the store is one cqrt_qram_store_<W>_hl_controlled(a_j, arr, j,
; val) (_hl = classical INDEX) under the trip predicate, with the value materialised as a basis-state handle by
; cqrt_alloc_<W> (a store value is ALWAYS a handle; the handle is pushed with the trip's flags for the mirror and freed
; once its store is popped). Each store owns a fresh tape slot (the displaced cell is swapped into it, then cell ^= val;
; under a_j = 0 nothing happens and the slot stays |0>). The read a[m - 1] has a QUANTUM index over QUANTUM cells, so it
; is one cqrt_qram_load_<W>(arr, idx) -> fresh rail (the result; not a QROM, which reads classical cells: 29/30) with the
; logical-i32 index rail m - 1 (-O1's sext to i64 and the gep scaling are not emitted; an index outside 0..3 reads 0,
; §2). Pops (_unc, same arguments) need the value, index and control at their forward values, which they hold (the
; predicates and value handles are popped from the stack unchanged), and are ordered last-in-first-out only among
; stores that may touch the same cell: the reverse loop pops trip j's store (cell j) before cell j's memset store, the
; memset stores (distinct cells, commuting) follow, then cqrt_qram_free releases the all-|0> array before the
; measurement. This is the k_rem_pio2 shape (iq[], f[], q[] written at the loop index, read at jz-relative indices).
; K = 4 (the literal 4 below, tagged [K]) also bounds the cell index.
source_filename = "array_in_quantum_loop.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

define i32 @array_in_quantum_loop(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_alloc_i32(i32 4)    ; IR: %4 = alloca [4 x i32]: a 4-cell QRAM, cells |0>
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register m]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %5, double %1)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: call @llvm.memset(%4, 0, 16): the classical value 0 as ONE basis-state handle, shared by the four cell stores (rule 22)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 0, i32 %6)    ; IR: memset: a[0] = 0  (fixed-index store; its tape slot takes the displaced |0> cell)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 1, i32 %6)    ; IR: memset: a[1] = 0
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 2, i32 %6)    ; IR: memset: a[2] = 0
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 3, i32 %6)    ; IR: memset: a[3] = 0
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_slt_i32_hl(i32 %5, i32 0)    ; IR: %6 = icmp slt i32 %5, 0  [guard]
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %7)    ; IR: bracket: the loop is entered under NOT %6 (used as trip 0's predicate)
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %5, i32 1)    ; IR: %8 = add nuw i32 %5, 1  (pure, hoisted out of block %7)
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_zext_i32_to_i64(i32 %8)    ; IR: %9 = zext i32 %8 to i64
  br label %10

10:
  %11 = phi i64 [ 0, %3 ], [ %16, %10 ]    ; IR: %17 = phi i64 [ 0, %7 ], [ %21, %16 ]  (classical trip index, bounded by K)  [K]
  %12 = phi i32 [ %7, %3 ], [ %18, %10 ]    ; IR: predicate of this trip (trip 0: NOT %6)
  %13 = trunc i64 %11 to i32    ; IR: %19 = trunc i64 %17 to i32  (classical)
  %14 = mul i32 %13, %2    ; IR: %20 = mul i32 %19, %2  (classical)
  %15 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %14)    ; IR: store i32 %20, ptr %18: the classical value i*c of this trip as a basis-state handle
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl_controlled(i32 %12, i32 %4, i32 %13, i32 %15)    ; IR: store i32 %20, ptr %18: a[i] = i*c under this trip's predicate (fixed index i = the classical trip counter; the %18 gep is not emitted; the displaced cell goes onto the backend's tape)
  %16 = add nuw nsw i64 %11, 1    ; IR: %21 = add nuw nsw i64 %17, 1  (classical)
  %17 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i64_hl(i32 %9, i64 %16)    ; IR: %22 = icmp eq i64 %21, %9
  %18 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: predicate of the next trip = a & NOT %22
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %17)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %12, i32 %17, i32 %18)    ; IR: br i1 %22 not taken
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %17)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %15)    ; IR: the value handle of this trip's store, for the mirror
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %12)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %17)
  %19 = icmp ult i64 %16, 4    ; IR: K-bounded br i1 %22, label %10, label %16  [K]
  br i1 %19, label %10, label %20

20:
  %21 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %5, i32 -1)    ; IR: %11 = add nsw i32 %5, -1  [the index rail; the %12 sext and the %13 gep are not emitted]
  %22 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i32(i32 %4, i32 %21)    ; IR: %14 = load i32, ptr %13: a[m - 1]  (one access: quantum index over quantum cells, copy-out into a fresh rail)  [result rail]
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %21, i32 %5, i32 -1)    ; IR: uncompute %11
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %21)    ; IR: release the %11 rail (|0>)
  br label %23

23:
  %24 = phi i64 [ 3, %20 ], [ %34, %33 ]    ; IR: reverse trip index (K - 1 down to 0)  [K]
  %25 = phi i32 [ %18, %20 ], [ %27, %33 ]    ; IR: predicate computed by this trip (on the first reverse trip: a_K, kept)
  %26 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: %22 of that trip
  %27 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: the predicate of that trip
  %28 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: the value handle of that trip's store
  %29 = trunc i64 %24 to i32    ; IR: %19 of that trip (classical)
  %30 = add nuw nsw i64 %24, 1
  %31 = icmp eq i64 %24, 3    ; IR: reverse index K - 1 is the last forward trip: the predicate it computed is a_K, the output rail (rule 14)  [K]
  br i1 %31, label %33, label %32

32:
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %26)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %27, i32 %26, i32 %25)    ; IR: uncompute the next-trip predicate (a_1..a_{K-1})
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %26)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %25)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  br label %33

33:
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i64_hl_unc(i32 %26, i32 %9, i64 %30)    ; IR: uncompute %22
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %26)    ; IR: release %22 (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl_controlled_unc(i32 %27, i32 %4, i32 %29, i32 %28)    ; IR: pop store i32 %20, ptr %18 of that trip (before the memset store of the same cell): a[i] holds its memset 0 again, the slot is |0> and released
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %28)    ; IR: release the value handle (basis state i*c)
  %34 = add nsw i64 %24, -1
  %35 = icmp sgt i64 %34, -1    ; IR: K  [K]
  br i1 %35, label %23, label %36

36:
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %7)    ; IR: bracket: %6 back
  call void @cq_template_icmp_slt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %7, i32 %5, i32 0)    ; IR: uncompute %6
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release %6 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_zext_i32_to_i64_unc(i32 %9, i32 %8)    ; IR: uncompute %9
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %9)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %8, i32 %5, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %8
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %8)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl_unc(i32 %4, i32 3, i32 %6)    ; IR: pop the memset stores (after the trip stores to the same cells; distinct cells commute, written in reverse): a[3] back to |0>
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl_unc(i32 %4, i32 2, i32 %6)    ; IR: a[2]
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl_unc(i32 %4, i32 1, i32 %6)    ; IR: a[1]
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl_unc(i32 %4, i32 0, i32 %6)    ; IR: a[0]
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release the basis-state handle 0 (its last store was popped)
  call void @cqrt_qram_free(i32 %4)    ; IR: llvm.lifetime.end: release the array (every store popped, all cells |0>)
  %37 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %22)    ; IR: %15 = cq_measure_si32(%14)
  ret i32 %37    ; IR: ret i32 %15
}

name: 56_int_intrinsics
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 4, 3, 5, 2, 25.
; Checked: each function's measured result: fshl_qq %7 -> %8; rotl_qc %8 -> %9; clz_q %4 -> %5; popcount_q %6 -> %7;
; smax_qc %5 -> %6; umax_qq %7 -> %8; abs_q %4 -> %5; fptoui_q %4 -> %5; same_operand_twice %8 -> %9 (the fptrunc of the
; measured x86_fp80 is classical).
; Clean: rotl_qc's two shift rails (%5, %7); popcount_q's mask rail x & c (%5); same_operand_twice's fpext (%5) and
; product (%7), all uncomputed and freed.
; Kept: every rotated register (a, b, x, y of each function) and each function's measured result rail.
; Rotations: fshl_qq: (Ry, a, ta, 1); (Ry, b, tb, 1). rotl_qc, clz_q, popcount_q, smax_qc, abs_q: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; umax_qq: (Ry, x, tx, 1); (Ry, y, ty, 1). fptoui_q, same_operand_twice: (Ry_f64, x, th, 1).
; Each intrinsic on quantum data is one template (fshl: a three-operand template, _qql = two quantum operands and a

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 20 (runtime-sized slot array), 7, 2, 1.
; Checked: e = sum of cq_measure(q[i]) over i < n: each measured q[i] (handle loaded from slot i, IR %33 -> %35).
; Clean: nothing to free: no garbage rail is ever minted (slot loads and the i8<->i1 casts emit no gate).
; Kept: the n cells q[0..n-1]: user registers seeded |0>, rotated in place and measured, they stay allocated.
; Rotations: (Ry, q[i], theta[i], 1) for i = 0..n-1 in loop order, each in place on its own rail.
; `bool q[n]` is a runtime-sized register: n i1 rails held in a classical array of SLOTS of runtime length (rule 20: the
; `alloca i8, n` becomes one `alloca i32, n`, one handle per 4-byte cell; -O1's byte GEPs over i8 cells are cell indices).
; The zero-init loop is folded by -O1 into `llvm.memset(q, 0, n)` under `n > 0`: a classical store into every cell, so each
; cell is a seed rail (rule 7) and the memset becomes a classical loop over the n cells minting one |0> rail per cell. A
; classical-index access `q[i]` is a load of the HANDLE from slot i (the i8<->i1 zext/trunc are representation changes,
; no gate); cq_theta rotates that rail in place, the store of its result changes nothing; the measure loop reads the
; slots. The n cells are user registers and stay allocated. This is the register-array shape of VQE/QPE (examples 59,
; 60, 114 build on it); the register size is a function input, never a compile-time constant.

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 10, 8, 20, 7, 2, 5.
; Checked: controlled_ry_chain: q[0] + q[n-1]; controlled_ry_two: q0 + q1 + q2 (measured).
; Clean: controlled_ry_two's conjunction flag q0 & q1.
; Kept: the i1 registers (q[0..n-1] behind the runtime-sized slot array; q0, q1, q2), rotated in place and measured.
; Rotations: controlled_ry_chain: Ry(theta[i]) on q[i] for i = 0..n-1; then Ry(c) on q[i+1] under q[i] for
; i = 0..n-2 (classical n). controlled_ry_two: Ry(t0) on q0; Ry(t1) on q1; Ry(c) on q2 under q0 & q1.
; `bool q[n]` is a runtime-sized register (rule 20): one `alloca i32, n` of handle cells, as in example 58; -O1 folds the
; zero-init loop into `llvm.memset(q, 0, n)` under `n > 0`, which becomes a classical loop minting one |0> seed rail per
; cell (rule 7). -O1's byte GEPs over i8 cells are cell indices; q[n-1] is `q + sext(n) - 1`, re-emitted over i32 cells.
; A bare _Bool rail read from a register-array slot is a condition by itself (no compare, rule 8):
; `if (q[i]) cq_theta(&q[i+1], c)` is one `cqrt_ry_i1_controlled(q[i], q[i+1], c)` with the control rail as the flag
; (rule 10), inside the classical loop (no predicate chain, no stack: nothing is computed into fresh rails). Two
; controls (`q0 && q1`, which -O1 spells `select i1 %4, i1 %5, i1 false`) become a Toffoli into a fresh |0> flag, the
; controlled Ry on that flag, the Toffoli again to return the flag to |0>, and one free.

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"

define i32 @controlled_ry_chain(ptr nocapture noundef readonly %0, i32 noundef %1, double noundef %2) {
  %4 = zext i32 %1 to i64    ; IR: %4  (classical n)
  %5 = alloca i32, i64 %4, align 16    ; IR: %5 = alloca i8, i64 %4  (runtime-sized classical slots: one handle per cell)
  %6 = icmp sgt i32 %1, 0    ; IR: %6  (classical)
  br i1 %6, label %7, label %15    ; IR: br i1 %6

7:
  %8 = zext nneg i32 %1 to i64    ; IR: %8  (classical memset length n)
  br label %9    ; IR: block %7: llvm.memset(%5, 0, %8) becomes a loop over the n cells

9:
  %10 = phi i64 [ 0, %7 ], [ %13, %9 ]    ; IR: memset cell index (classical)
  %11 = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %5, i64 %10    ; IR: memset byte %z = cell q[z]  (slot of q[z])
  %12 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: llvm.memset(%5, 0, %8): cell q[z] = 0  [register q[z], a |0> seed rail]
  store i32 %12, ptr %11, align 4    ; IR: llvm.memset(%5, 0, %8)  (slot z holds the handle of q[z])
  %13 = add nuw nsw i64 %10, 1    ; IR: memset cell index + 1 (classical)
  %14 = icmp eq i64 %13, %8    ; IR: all n cells written (classical)
  br i1 %14, label %15, label %9    ; IR: br label %9

15:
  %16 = icmp sgt i32 %1, 0    ; IR: %10  (classical)
  br i1 %16, label %17, label %19    ; IR: br i1 %10

17:
  %18 = zext nneg i32 %1 to i64    ; IR: %12  (classical)
  br label %24    ; IR: br label %18

19:
  %20 = icmp sgt i32 %1, 1    ; IR: %14  (classical)
  br i1 %20, label %21, label %32    ; IR: br i1 %14

21:
  %22 = add nsw i32 %1, -1    ; IR: %16  (classical)
  %23 = zext i32 %22 to i64    ; IR: %17  (classical)
  br label %43    ; IR: br label %42

24:
  %25 = phi i64 [ 0, %17 ], [ %30, %24 ]    ; IR: %19  (classical trip counter i)
  %26 = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %5, i64 %25    ; IR: %20 = getelementptr i8, ptr %5, %19  (slot of q[i])
  %27 = load i32, ptr %26, align 4    ; IR: %21 = load i8; %22 = trunc to i1  (handle of q[i]; no gate)
  %28 = getelementptr inbounds double, ptr %0, i64 %25    ; IR: %23  (classical)
  %29 = load double, ptr %28, align 8    ; IR: %24 = load double  (classical angle theta[i])
  call void @cqrt_ry_i1(i32 %27, double %29)    ; IR: %25 = cq_theta_i1(%22, %24)  [Ry in place on q[i]]; %26/store: handle unchanged
  %30 = add nuw nsw i64 %25, 1    ; IR: %27  (classical)
  %31 = icmp eq i64 %30, %18    ; IR: %28  (classical)
  br i1 %31, label %19, label %24    ; IR: br i1 %28

32:
  %33 = load i32, ptr %5, align 4    ; IR: %30 = load i8, ptr %5; %31 = trunc to i1  (handle of q[0])
  %34 = call i1 @cqrt_measure_i1(i32 %33)    ; IR: %32 = cq_measure_i1(%31)
  %35 = zext i1 %34 to i32    ; IR: %33  (classical)
  %36 = sext i32 %1 to i64    ; IR: %34  (classical)
  %37 = getelementptr i32, ptr %5, i64 %36    ; IR: %35 = getelementptr i8, ptr %5, i64 %34  (cell index n)
  %38 = getelementptr i32, ptr %37, i64 -1    ; IR: %36 = getelementptr i8, ptr %35, i64 -1  (slot of q[n-1])
  %39 = load i32, ptr %38, align 4    ; IR: %37 = load i8; %38 = trunc to i1  (handle of q[n-1])
  %40 = call i1 @cqrt_measure_i1(i32 %39)    ; IR: %39 = cq_measure_i1(%38)
  %41 = zext i1 %40 to i32    ; IR: %40  (classical)
  %42 = add nuw nsw i32 %41, %35    ; IR: %41  (classical)
  ret i32 %42    ; IR: ret i32 %41

43:
  %44 = phi i64 [ 0, %21 ], [ %52, %50 ]    ; IR: %43  (classical i)
  %45 = phi i64 [ 1, %21 ], [ %51, %50 ]    ; IR: %44  (classical i+1)
  %46 = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %5, i64 %44    ; IR: %45  (slot of q[i])
  %47 = load i32, ptr %46, align 4    ; IR: %46 = load i8; %47 = trunc to i1  (handle of q[i]: the control rail)
  %48 = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %5, i64 %45    ; IR: %49  (slot of q[i+1], hoisted from block %48: pure)
  %49 = load i32, ptr %48, align 4    ; IR: %50 = load i8; %51 = trunc to i1  (handle of q[i+1]: the target)
  call void @cqrt_ry_i1_controlled(i32 %47, i32 %49, double %2)    ; IR: br i1 %47 -> block %48: %52 = cq_theta_i1(%51, %2)  [Ry on q[i+1] controlled by the bare rail q[i]]; %53/store: handle unchanged
  br label %50    ; IR: br label %54

50:
  %51 = add nuw nsw i64 %45, 1    ; IR: %55  (classical)
  %52 = add nuw nsw i64 %44, 1    ; IR: %56  (classical)
  %53 = icmp eq i64 %52, %23    ; IR: %57  (classical)
  br i1 %53, label %32, label %43    ; IR: br i1 %57

define i32 @controlled_ry_two(double noundef %0, double noundef %1, double noundef %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_i1(false, %0)  [register q0]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i1(i32 %4, double %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_i1(false, %0)  [Ry]
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_i1(false, %1)  [register q1]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i1(i32 %5, double %1)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_i1(false, %1)  [Ry]
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: %6 = select i1 %4, i1 %5, i1 false  [flag rail for q0 && q1]
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %4, i32 %5, i32 %6)    ; IR: %6 = q0 & q1  (Toffoli into the |0> flag)
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: %10 = phi i1 [ %8, %7 ], [ false, %3 ]  [register q2, starts as false]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i1_controlled(i32 %6, i32 %7, double %2)    ; IR: br i1 %6 -> block %7: %8 = cq_theta_i1(false, %2)  [Ry on q2 under the flag]
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %4, i32 %5, i32 %6)    ; IR: uncompute %6 (q0, q1 unchanged)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release the flag (|0>)
  %8 = call i1 @cqrt_measure_i1(i32 %4)    ; IR: %11 = cq_measure_i1(%4)
  %9 = zext i1 %8 to i32    ; IR: %12  (classical)
  %10 = call i1 @cqrt_measure_i1(i32 %5)    ; IR: %13 = cq_measure_i1(%5)
  %11 = zext i1 %10 to i32    ; IR: %14  (classical)
  %12 = add nuw nsw i32 %11, %9    ; IR: %15  (classical)
  %13 = call i1 @cqrt_measure_i1(i32 %7)    ; IR: %16 = cq_measure_i1(%10)
  %14 = zext i1 %13 to i32    ; IR: %17  (classical)
  %15 = add nuw nsw i32 %12, %14    ; IR: %18  (classical)
  ret i32 %15    ; IR: ret i32 %18
}

name: 60_qft
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 20, 8, 2, 5.
; Checked: nothing is measured here; the caller's registers q[0..n-1] hold the result.
; Clean: every per-trip Toffoli flag q[j] & q[i].
; Kept: the caller's n i1 registers behind the slot array q (never freed; they belong to the caller).
; Rotations: for i = 0..n-1: Ry(base) on q[i]; then for j = i+1..n-1: P(base / 2^(j-i)) on (q[j] & q[i]).
; Expected: the QFT ladder on n qubits with base as the opening rotation and the controlled phases base/2^(j-i)
; between q[i] and every later q[j], without the final bit-reversal swaps.
; A `bool *` parameter that points at quantum registers arrives as a pointer to i32 HANDLE SLOTS (the caller's register
; array, example 58, rule 20), so `q[i]` is a classical-index load of a handle. The outer loop rotates q[i] in place;
; the inner loop's `if (q[j] && q[i])` is two nested branches on bare rails (-O1 keeps the short-circuit as nested br),
; folded into ONE Toffoli flag (rule 8); the cq_phi with its classically computed angle is an uncontrolled kickback on
; that flag; the flag is un-Toffoli'd and freed every trip. Both loops are classical-bound: no predicate chain, no
; stack. Nothing but the caller's registers survives.
source_filename = "qft.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

define void @qft(ptr nocapture noundef %0, i32 noundef %1, double noundef %2) {
  %4 = icmp sgt i32 %1, 0    ; IR: %4  (classical)
  br i1 %4, label %5, label %12    ; IR: br i1 %4

5:; preds = %3
  %6 = zext nneg i32 %1 to i64    ; IR: %6  (classical)
  %7 = zext nneg i32 %1 to i64    ; IR: %7  (classical)
  %8 = zext nneg i32 %1 to i64    ; IR: %8  (classical)
  br label %13

9:; preds = %37, %13
  %10 = add nuw nsw i64 %15, 1    ; IR: %10  (classical)
  %11 = icmp eq i64 %18, %7    ; IR: %11  (classical)
  br i1 %11, label %12, label %13    ; IR: br i1 %11

12:; preds = %9, %3
  ret void    ; IR: ret void

13:; preds = %5, %9
  %14 = phi i64 [ 0, %5 ], [ %18, %9 ]    ; IR: %14  (classical i)
  %15 = phi i64 [ 1, %5 ], [ %10, %9 ]    ; IR: %15  (classical i+1)
  %16 = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %0, i64 %14    ; IR: %16 = getelementptr i8, ptr %0, %14  (slot of q[i]; slots are i32 handles)
  %17 = load i32, ptr %16, align 4    ; IR: %17 = load i8, ptr %16; %18 = trunc to i1  (handle of q[i]; no gate)
  call void @cqrt_ry_i1(i32 %17, double %2)    ; IR: %19 = cq_theta_i1(%18, %2)  [Ry in place on q[i]]; %20/store: handle unchanged
  %18 = add nuw nsw i64 %14, 1    ; IR: %21  (classical)
  %19 = icmp ult i64 %18, %6    ; IR: %22  (classical)
  br i1 %19, label %20, label %9    ; IR: br i1 %22

20:; preds = %13, %37
  %21 = phi i64 [ %31, %30 ], [ %15, %13 ]    ; IR: %24  (classical j)
  %22 = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %0, i64 %21    ; IR: %25 = getelementptr i8, ptr %0, %24  (slot of q[j])
  %23 = load i32, ptr %22, align 4    ; IR: %26 = load i8, ptr %25; %27 = trunc to i1  (handle of q[j]; no gate)
  %24 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: predicate of block %31 = %27 & %30  (%29 = load i8, ptr %16 reloads q[i]: same handle %hi)
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %23, i32 %17, i32 %24)    ; IR: br i1 %27 -> block %28, br i1 %30 -> block %31: one Toffoli flag
  %25 = sub nuw nsw i64 %21, %14    ; IR: %32  (classical j - i)
  %26 = trunc nsw i64 %25 to i32    ; IR: %33  (classical)
  %27 = shl nuw i32 1, %26    ; IR: %34  (classical 1 << (j - i))
  %28 = sitofp i32 %27 to double    ; IR: %35  (classical)
  %29 = fdiv double %2, %28    ; IR: %36  (classical angle)
  call void @cqrt_rz_i1(i32 %24, double %29)    ; IR: block %31: cq_phi(%36)  [kickback on the flag]
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %23, i32 %17, i32 %24)    ; IR: uncompute the %31 predicate
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %24)    ; IR: release the flag (|0>)
  br label %30    ; IR: br label %37

30:; preds = %23
  %31 = add nuw nsw i64 %21, 1    ; IR: %38  (classical)
  %32 = icmp eq i64 %31, %8    ; IR: %39  (classical)
  br i1 %32, label %9, label %20    ; IR: br i1 %39

name: 61_invert_theta_and_call
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 17, 2, 18, 10, 20, 8, §1.3.
; Checked: invert_theta: x (%4 -> %5). invert_call: x (the slot pointee, %10 -> %11) and y (%9 -> %12), summed classically.
; Clean: the flag f = (y > k) of the clone (%7 of __cq_q_prep_11000), uncomputed and freed after its controlled rotation
;        (in the bracketed activation the backend recomputes and uncomputes it as the reversed list runs, rule 17).
; Kept: the user registers x and y in both functions (rotated, measured).
; Rotations: invert_theta: (Ry, x, th, 1); then the region as the backend emits it: (Ry, x, -t2, 1).
; invert_call: (Ry, y, ty, 1); (Ry, x, t1, 1); (Ry, x, t2, y > k); then the region: (Ry, x, -t2, y > k); (Ry, x, -t1, 1).
; cq_invert is the run-time pair cqrt_invert_begin()/cqrt_invert_end() (rule 17, §1.3): the code between the markers is
; lowered as anywhere else, and the backend emits the gates recorded between the two calls reversed with each gate
; inverted. invert_theta: the recorded list is [Ry(x, t2)], emitted as Ry(x, -t2). invert_call: `prep(&x, ...)` takes
; the register's ADDRESS, so x lives in a classical slot holding its handle (31) and the clone rotates that handle in
; place with no result rail; the conditional rotation is controlled by a flag computed from the OTHER register y. The
; clone __cq_q_prep_11000 (mask over all five args, §1.4: a pointer-to-slot field's digit is 1 iff the cell holds a
; handle AT THE CALL; x's cell does: it holds a handle after the clone's rotation, so it is a handle on every path (rule
; 20's homogeneous cell) and the caller's classical x = x0 is the seed rail alloc_i32(x0) stored before the call; y is a
; quantum scalar; k and the angles are classical) is [Ry(x, t1); f = (y > k); cRy(f, x, t2); unc f; free f]. The
; bracketed call is the SAME clone (no `_adj` kind exists, §1.4): the backend's reversal of the gates it records is
; [unc f (= compute f); cRy(f, x, -t2); f's uncompute; Ry(x, -t1); free f], the compare/uncompute pair reversing into
; itself. Had the condition read x itself (`if (*x > k) cq_theta(x, t2)`), the flag could not be uncomputed after the
; rotation changed x; that shape is example 66, where the flag stays allocated. Regenerated 2026-11-02 (the first version

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 18, 26, 1, 5.
; Checked: r.hi + r.lo (the fadd rail %8 -> %9).
; Clean: the clone's chain (hi = x * c, lo = x - hi: %3, %4 of __cq_q_split_10, uncomputed and freed inside the clone) and
; the two copied-out result rails (%6, %7 in the caller), zeroed by the _unc twin and freed by the caller.
; Kept: x (%4, the rotated register) and the sum (%8, measured).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; An aggregate return is a call with TWO results: the clone __cq_q_split_10 (mask left to right, §1.4) returns { i32, i32 },
; the handles of two fresh result rails (hi, lo), each copied out of the callee's chain before the chain is uncomputed (the
; one-result form is 34); the _unc twin takes both result handles first and zeroes both by recomputing the chain. The caller
; extracts the two handles (extractvalue on handles, classical) and continues out of place; when the sum is formed both
; results are garbage and the twin runs, then the caller frees both result rails.
source_filename = "aggregate_return.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

define double @aggregate_return(double noundef %0, double noundef %1, double noundef %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_f64(double %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_f64(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_f64(i32 %4, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_f64(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %5 = call fastcc { i32, i32 } @__cq_q_split_10(i32 %4, double %2)    ; IR: %5 = call @split(%4, %2), clone for mask (quantum, classical): two result handles
  %6 = extractvalue { i32, i32 } %5, 0    ; IR: %6 = extractvalue %5, 0  (handle of the hi rail; classical)
  %7 = extractvalue { i32, i32 } %5, 1    ; IR: %7 = extractvalue %5, 1  (handle of the lo rail; classical)
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f64(i32 %6, i32 %7)    ; IR: %8 = fadd double %6, %7  [result rail]
  call fastcc void @__cq_q_split_10_unc(i32 %6, i32 %7, i32 %4, double %2)    ; IR: uncompute %6 and %7 (both results of the call)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release the %6 rail (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release the %7 rail (|0>)
  %9 = call double @cqrt_measure_f64(i32 %8)    ; IR: %9 = cq_measure_f64(%8)
  ret double %9    ; IR: ret double %9
}

  %4 = call i32 @cq_template_fsub_f64(i32 %0, i32 %3)    ; IR: %4 = fsub double %0, %3
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_f64(double 0.000000e+00)    ; IR: insertvalue ..., %3, 0  [result rail hi]
  call void @cqrt_copy_f64(i32 %3, i32 %5)    ; IR: copy r.hi out

  call void @cqrt_copy_f64(i32 %4, i32 %6)    ; IR: copy r.lo out
  call void @cq_template_fsub_f64_unc(i32 %4, i32 %0, i32 %3)    ; IR: uncompute %4

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %3)    ; IR: release the %3 rail (|0>)

  %8 = insertvalue { i32, i32 } %7, i32 %6, 1    ; IR: %6 = insertvalue %5, %4, 1

define internal fastcc void @__cq_q_split_10_unc(i32 %0, i32 %1, i32 %2, double %3) {

  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_fsub_f64(i32 %2, i32 %5)    ; IR: recompute %4

name: 65_fenv_bracket
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 23, 8, 4, 5, 2.
; Checked: fenv_bracket: y = x * c; fenv_tested: y + (double)f, f = fetestexcept(FE_INEXACT) (y measured; f is classical
; by rule 2 and is a classical read).
; Clean: the compare flag y > k of each function; the flags rail select(y > k, 32, 0) of each function; fenv_tested's
; flags & 32 and host | quantum rails. All of them collapse after the measurement of y (rule 2).
; Kept: the user register x of each function; the result rail y (measured).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x (each function).
; Classical reads (rule 2): 1 (fenv_tested's cq_measure(f): f is classical after y's measurement, no gate).
; This is the DEFAULT-ENVIRONMENT case of rule 23: without `#pragma STDC FENV_ACCESS ON` clang emits plain
; fadd/fmul/fcmp, which assume round-to-nearest and raise no flags, so every FP op lowers to its ordinary template;
; examples 80-82 are the full model (constrained ops). The fenv calls are classical calls on thread-global state and
; are kept exactly as clang emitted them (host calls on the real fenv_t slot); classical code is never deleted. The
; flags are split as in 81: the host register holds what classical code raises, the quantum FLAGS RAIL what quantum
; code raises. Plain ops raise nothing, so the only quantum write is an explicit feraiseexcept under a quantum
; predicate: flags' = flags | select(pred, m, 0), no host call (while the rail is empty, the select rail is the flags
; rail). fetestexcept(m) = host call | (flags & m). fenv_bracket: the feholdexcept/feupdateenv pair brackets no
; quantum flags (the rail is empty throughout), so it is host calls only. fenv_tested: fesetround(FE_UPWARD) is a host
; call but does not reach the plain fmul, which clang compiled for the default environment, so the template rounds to
; nearest exactly as the IR says.
; CLASSICAL COLLAPSE (rule 2, ruling 2026-10-29): both functions measure y, and every rail computed from y alone (the
; compare, the flags rail, fenv_tested's f chain) is a function of the outcome and classical values. Rule 2 is a
; data-flow condition, not a program-order one: those rails were computed BEFORE the measurement, and "while its
; sources still hold the outcome" is exactly that case (the _unc reads the measured rail, which still holds m). So each
; such rail is uncomputed right after the measurement (convention: as early as the invariant allows) and its value is
; recomputed by ordinary classical instructions from m. The flags rail is fenv state: its classical value is written to
; the HOST environment by feraiseexcept(v) at the collapse point (v = 0 raises nothing), so rule 23's "final flags rail
; is an output" has nothing left to keep. fenv_tested's cq_measure(f) measures a value rule 2 made classical: it is a
; classical read and emits no measurement (one measurement per call, y's). f's host part (%11) was read at its program
; point, before the write-back, exactly as the C program read it.
source_filename = "fenv_bracket.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

  call void @cqrt_ry_f64(i32 %6, double %1)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_f64(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %7 = call i32 @fegetround()    ; IR: %7 = fegetround()  (host call)
  %8 = call i32 @fesetround(i32 0)    ; IR: %8 = fesetround(0)  (host call)
  %9 = call i32 @feholdexcept(ptr %5)    ; IR: %9 = feholdexcept(%5)  (host call; the quantum flags rail is empty)
  %10 = call i32 @cq_template_fmul_f64_hl(i32 %6, double %2)    ; IR: %10 = fmul double %6, %2  [result rail y]  (plain op: raises nothing)
  %11 = call i32 @feupdateenv(ptr %5)    ; IR: %11 = feupdateenv(%5)  (host call; empty | empty)
  %12 = call i32 @cq_template_fcmp_ogt_f64_hl(i32 %10, double %3)    ; IR: %12 = fcmp ogt double %10, %3  [predicate of block %13]
  %13 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_ll(i32 %12, i32 32, i32 0)    ; IR: br i1 %12 -> block %13: %14 = feraiseexcept(32) under the predicate  [flags rail]
  %14 = call i32 @fesetround(i32 %7)    ; IR: %16 = fesetround(%7)  (host call)
  %15 = call double @cqrt_measure_f64(i32 %10)    ; IR: %17 = cq_measure_f64(%10)  [outcome m; %10 holds it from here on]
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_ll_unc(i32 %13, i32 %12, i32 32, i32 0)    ; IR: rule 2 collapse: the flags rail is a function of y alone; uncompute it while %12 still holds its value

  %7 = call i32 @feclearexcept(i32 32)    ; IR: %7 = feclearexcept(32)  (host call; the quantum flags rail is still empty)
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_fmul_f64_hl(i32 %5, double %2)    ; IR: %8 = fmul double %5, %2  [result rail y]
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_fcmp_ogt_f64_hl(i32 %8, double %3)    ; IR: %9 = fcmp ogt double %8, %3  [predicate of block %10]
  %10 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_ll(i32 %9, i32 32, i32 0)    ; IR: br i1 %9 -> block %10: %11 = feraiseexcept(32) under the predicate  [flags rail]
  %11 = call i32 @fetestexcept(i32 32)    ; IR: %13 = fetestexcept(32): the host part, read at its program point
  %12 = call i32 @cq_template_and_i32_hl(i32 %10, i32 32)    ; IR: %13: the quantum part, flags & 32
  %13 = call i32 @cq_template_or_i32_hl(i32 %12, i32 %11)    ; IR: %13 = host | quantum  [f]
  %14 = call double @cqrt_measure_f64(i32 %8)    ; IR: %14 = cq_measure_f64(%8)  [outcome m; %8 holds it from here on]
  call void @cq_template_or_i32_hl_unc(i32 %13, i32 %12, i32 %11)    ; IR: rule 2 collapse: f is a function of y alone; uncompute %13
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %13)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_and_i32_hl_unc(i32 %12, i32 %10, i32 32)    ; IR: uncompute %13's quantum part
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %12)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_ll_unc(i32 %10, i32 %9, i32 32, i32 0)    ; IR: uncompute the flags rail (a function of y alone)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %10)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_fcmp_ogt_f64_hl_unc(i32 %9, i32 %8, double %3)    ; IR: uncompute %9 while %8 holds the outcome
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %9)    ; IR: release the %9 rail (|0>)
  %15 = fcmp ogt double %14, %3    ; IR: %9 recomputed classically from the outcome (rule 2)
  %16 = select i1 %15, i32 32, i32 0    ; IR: the flags rail's classical value: select(y > k, 32, 0)
  %17 = and i32 %16, 32    ; IR: %13's quantum part, classical
  %18 = or i32 %17, %11    ; IR: %13 = host | quantum, classical  [f]
  %19 = call i32 @feraiseexcept(i32 %16)    ; IR: the collapsed flags written to the host environment (rule 23)
  %20 = sitofp i32 %18 to double    ; IR: %16 = sitofp i32 %15 to double  (%15 = cq_measure_si32(%13) is a classical read of f: no measurement)
  %21 = fadd double %14, %20    ; IR: %17 = fadd double %14, %16  (classical)

name: 66_self_conditioned_rotation
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 10 (a flag that read the rotated register stays allocated), 8, 2.
; Checked: x (%5 -> %7).
; Clean: none: nothing is freed.
; Kept: x (%5, the rotated register) and the flag f = (x > k) (%6): it was computed from x before the controlled rotation
; changed x, so it can no longer be uncomputed and stays allocated, entangled with x.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, t1, 1); (Ry, x, t2, x > k) with the predicate read from x before this rotation.
; The condition reads the register the arm rotates: the flag f = (x > k) is computed from x BEFORE the rotation, and after
; cRy(f, x, t2) it can no longer be uncomputed from x, because x has changed. We never decline: the flag is emitted, the
; rotation is controlled by it, and the flag simply STAYS ALLOCATED, entangled with x, like a user register (its which-branch
; record dephases later interference between the two arms: that is what the program says). C principle: the compiler does
; not stop the user shooting their own foot; it emits the program as written. Compare 39, where the condition reads a
; different register and the flag is uncomputed.
source_filename = "self_conditioned_rotation.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

define i32 @self_conditioned_rotation(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2, double noundef %3) {
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %5, double %1)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %5, i32 %2)    ; IR: %6 = icmp sgt i32 %5, %2  [path predicate of block %7, read from x before the rotation]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32_controlled(i32 %6, i32 %5, double %3)    ; IR: block %7: %8 = cq_theta_si32(%5, %3); %10 = phi [ %8, %7 ], [ %5, %4 ]  [Ry under the predicate, in place]
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %5)    ; IR: %11 = cq_measure_si32(%10)  (%f is NOT uncomputed: x changed under it; the flag rail stays allocated)
  ret i32 %7    ; IR: ret i32 %11
}

name: 67_static_global_slot
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 20, 18, 16, 4, 5, 2.
; Checked: y + saved, saved = x * c, y = bump(saved) (measured).
; Clean: the product x * c (the slot's rail), the clone's result rail (zeroed by the twin, then freed), and every rail
; inside the clone and its twin.
; Kept: the user register x; the result rail (measured); the clone's tape rail (never freed).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x.
; A function-local `static` is a global with internal linkage whose address never escapes (the casin shape: openlibm
; keeps `static double complex ca, ct, zz, z2;` and stores quantum values into them between calls to csqrt/clog,
; which is what stops -O1 from localizing them). Such a global is a classical SLOT exactly like the non-escaping
; alloca of example 31 (rule 20): it keeps its i32 type and holds the HANDLE of the rail stored into it; the load after
; the call yields that handle. The callee is cloned for its quantum argument (rule 18); its printf is the output tape
; of example 47 (rule 16: one tape per function, the entry appended once). The clone's _unc twin recomputes the pure
; chain only: tape operations are write-once and are never replayed, so the twin has no tape. Both the stored product
; and the call result are uncomputed after the final add.
source_filename = "static_global_slot.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

@static_global_slot.saved = internal unnamed_addr global i32 0, align 4    ; IR: @static_global_slot.saved  (classical slot: holds a handle)
@.str = private unnamed_addr constant [4 x i8] c"%d\0A\00", align 1    ; IR: @.str  (format string of the tape entry)

define i32 @static_global_slot(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %4, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %5 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 %2)    ; IR: %5 = mul nsw i32 %4, %2
  store i32 %5, ptr @static_global_slot.saved, align 4    ; IR: store i32 %5, ptr @static_global_slot.saved  (the slot takes the handle)
  %6 = call fastcc i32 @__cq_q_bump_1(i32 %5)    ; IR: %6 = call @bump(%5), quantum clone (arg 0 quantum)
  %7 = load i32, ptr @static_global_slot.saved, align 4    ; IR: %7 = load i32, ptr @static_global_slot.saved  (the handle of %5)
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32(i32 %7, i32 %6)    ; IR: %8 = add nsw i32 %7, %6  [result rail]
  call fastcc void @__cq_q_bump_1_unc(i32 %6, i32 %5)    ; IR: uncompute %6
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release the %6 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_mul_i32_hl_unc(i32 %5, i32 %4, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %5 (the slot's rail)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %5)    ; IR: release the %5 rail (|0>); the slot's handle is dead
  %9 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %8)    ; IR: %9 = cq_measure_si32(%8)
  ret i32 %9    ; IR: ret i32 %9
}

define internal fastcc i32 @__cq_q_bump_1(i32 %0) {
  %2 = call i32 @cqrt_tape_alloc()    ; IR: the clone's output tape
  call void @cqrt_tape_fmt(i32 %2, ptr @.str)    ; IR: %2 = printf(@.str, %0): open the entry with its format string
  %3 = call i32 @cqrt_tape_write_i32(i32 %2, i32 %0)    ; IR: %2 = printf(..., %0): field 0, a quantum value copied onto a fresh tape rail
  %4 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %0, i32 1)    ; IR: %3 = add nsw i32 %0, 1
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: ret i32 %3  [result rail of the call]
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %4, i32 %5)    ; IR: copy the result out
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %4, i32 %0, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %3
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %4)    ; IR: release the %3 rail (|0>)
  ret i32 %5    ; IR: ret i32 %3
}

define internal fastcc void @__cq_q_bump_1_unc(i32 %0, i32 %1) {
  %3 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %1, i32 1)    ; IR: recompute %3 (no tape: the entry was appended once by the forward clone)
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %3, i32 %0)    ; IR: xor the result out of %out
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %3, i32 %1, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %3
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %3)    ; IR: release the %3 rail (|0>)
  ret void
}
