name: 68_nested_quantum_loops
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 14 (nested K-loops), 8, 7, 5.
; Checked: acc (the copied-out result %32 -> %66).
; Clean: every rail except a_K and the K rails b_K: every trip's values and intermediate predicates, popped and uncomputed
; by the mirror loops; a_0 through the guard compare; the |0> seed of acc (%62); the guard compare itself (%6).
; Kept: x (%4, the rotated register); the outer chain's last predicate a_K (%28 of outer trip K-1, popped as %36 on the first
; outer reverse trip); the K inner last predicates b_K (%22 of inner trip K-1 of each outer trip, popped as %38); the result
; %32 (measured).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; A quantum-bounded loop nested inside a quantum-bounded loop, the k_rem_pio2 shape: this is example 05 composed with
; itself. -O1 made both loops bottom-tested (do-while) behind one guard x == 0. The outer loop runs K trips under the chain
; a_k (a_0 = NOT(x == 0), a_{k+1} = a_k & NOT(i - 1 == 0)); each outer trip runs an inner rolled loop of K trips under its
; own chain seeded from the outer predicate (b_0 = a_k, b_{m+1} = b_m & NOT(j + 1 == i)); the inner j is the classical trip
; index (it equals m whenever the trip is live), the outer i is quantum (it starts at x). Stack discipline: every inner trip
; pushes its handles, then the outer trip pushes its own (i, a_k, i - 1, the exit flag, the inner chain's final predicate).
; The reverse pops in stack order: an outer reverse trip pops its own handles, uncomputes them, then runs the inner reverse
; loop (popping the inner trips in reverse order); the pops match the pushes because the inner pushes of outer trip k sit
; above outer trip k's own pushes. This is not the exact gate mirror (forward ran the inner trips before the outer
; trip's i - 1, select, compare and a_{k+1}), and it need not be: rule 5 asks for dependency order, and those outer rails
; read only i and a_k, which the inner trips also only read, while no inner rail reads them; both groups' sources
; (i, a_k) stay live until the next reverse trip, so the two groups commute. K = 4 here; every literal K is tagged [K].
; Output rails (rule 14): the outer chain's last predicate a_K (a_K = 1 means the outer loop would have run past K trips) is
; kept allocated, neither uncomputed nor freed; the outer reverse loop skips its uncompute on reverse index 0 by a classical
; branch. Likewise each outer trip's inner chain keeps ITS last predicate b_K (pushed by the outer trip): K inner output
; rails in all, one per outer trip (b_K of a dead outer trip is |0>); the inner reverse loop skips the uncompute on reverse
; inner index K-1. Every other predicate is uncomputed as before; a_0 is uncomputed through the guard compare.
source_filename = "nested_quantum_loops.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

define i32 @nested_quantum_loops(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %4, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: incoming 0 of phi %8 / %10
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 0)    ; IR: %5 = icmp eq i32 %4, 0  [guard]
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: predicate of entering the outer loop = NOT %5
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %6)    ; IR: bracket: NOT %5
  call void @cqrt_xor_i1(i32 %6, i32 %7)    ; IR: a_0 = NOT %5  (CNOT into the |0> rail)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %6)    ; IR: bracket
  br label %8

  %9 = phi i32 [ 0, %3 ], [ %29, %24 ]    ; IR: outer trip index, bounded by K
  %10 = phi i32 [ %4, %3 ], [ %26, %24 ]    ; IR: %7 = phi i32 [ %13, %12 ], [ %4, %3 ]
  %11 = phi i32 [ %5, %3 ], [ %19, %24 ]    ; IR: %8 = phi i32 [ %19, %12 ], [ 0, %3 ]
  %12 = phi i32 [ %7, %3 ], [ %28, %24 ]    ; IR: predicate of this outer trip (a_k)
  br label %13    ; IR: br label %15

  %14 = phi i32 [ 0, %8 ], [ %20, %13 ]    ; IR: %16 = phi i32 [ 0, %6 ], [ %20, %15 ]  (j: classical trip index)
  %15 = phi i32 [ %11, %8 ], [ %19, %13 ]    ; IR: %17 = phi i32 [ %8, %6 ], [ %19, %15 ]
  %16 = phi i32 [ %12, %8 ], [ %22, %13 ]    ; IR: predicate of this inner trip (b_m; b_0 = a_k)
  %17 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i32_hl(i32 %15, i32 %2)    ; IR: %18 = mul i32 %17, %2
  %18 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %17, i32 %14)    ; IR: %19 = add i32 %18, %16
  %19 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %16, i32 %18, i32 %15)    ; IR: next %17 / %8 = b_m ? %19 : %17
  %20 = add nuw i32 %14, 1    ; IR: %20 = add nuw i32 %16, 1  (classical)
  %21 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %10, i32 %20)    ; IR: %21 = icmp eq i32 %20, %7  (commutative: quantum %7 in the _hl slot)

  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %16, i32 %21, i32 %22)    ; IR: br i1 %21 not taken: b_{m+1} = b_m & NOT %21
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %21)    ; IR: bracket

  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %17)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %18)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %16)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %21)

  %26 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %12, i32 %25, i32 %10)    ; IR: next %7 = a_k ? %13 : %7
  %27 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %25, i32 0)    ; IR: %14 = icmp eq i32 %13, 0
  %28 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: predicate of the next outer trip
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %27)    ; IR: bracket: NOT %14
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %12, i32 %27, i32 %28)    ; IR: br i1 %14 not taken: a_{k+1} = a_k & NOT %14
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %27)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %10)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %12)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %25)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %27)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %22)    ; IR: the inner chain's final predicate b_K of this outer trip
  %29 = add nuw nsw i32 %9, 1
  %30 = icmp ult i32 %29, 4    ; IR: K-bounded br i1 %14, label %9, label %6  [K]
  br i1 %30, label %8, label %31

  %32 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: %10 = phi i32 [ 0, %3 ], [ %19, %12 ]  [copied-out result]

  br label %33

  %35 = phi i32 [ %26, %31 ], [ %42, %61 ]    ; IR: %7 written by this outer trip
  %36 = phi i32 [ %28, %31 ], [ %41, %61 ]    ; IR: predicate of the next outer trip (a_{k+1})
  %37 = phi i32 [ %19, %31 ], [ %62, %61 ]    ; IR: acc after this outer trip
  %38 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %39 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %40 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %41 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %42 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()

  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl_unc(i32 %39, i32 %40, i32 0)    ; IR: uncompute %14
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %39)    ; IR: release %14 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %40, i32 %42, i32 -1)    ; IR: uncompute %13
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %40)    ; IR: release %13 (|0>)

  %47 = phi i32 [ 3, %45 ], [ %59, %58 ]    ; IR: reverse inner trip index (K - 1 down to 0)  [K]
  %48 = phi i32 [ %38, %45 ], [ %51, %58 ]    ; IR: b_{m+1} of this inner trip
  %49 = phi i32 [ %37, %45 ], [ %54, %58 ]    ; IR: %17 / %8 written by this inner trip
  %50 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %51 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %52 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %53 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %54 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %55 = add nuw i32 %47, 1    ; IR: %20 of this trip (classical)
  %56 = icmp eq i32 %47, 3    ; IR: reverse inner index K-1 is inner trip K-1: its b_{m+1} = b_K is an output rail (rule 14)  [K]
  br i1 %56, label %58, label %57

  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %51, i32 %50, i32 %48)    ; IR: uncompute b_{m+1} (inner trips 0..K-2)

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 26, 18, 8, 9, 4, 5.
; Checked: creal(q) + cimag(q), the returned double (the fadd rail %28 -> %29).
; Clean: every rail but the register re: the inline product chain (%8, %11, %13, %15, %16), the two fcmp uno flags (%17, %18)
; and their conjunction (%19), the __muldc3 clone's two result rails (%21, %22) and the two merge selects (%23, %24), the
; twice clone's two result rails (%26, %27); inside each clone its whole chain, every block flag and every seed rail.
; Kept: re (%6, the rotated register) and the sum (%28, measured).
; Rotations: (Ry, re, th, 1); nothing else (the clones have no rotation; every branch is a value arm).
; A `double complex` is two doubles: the parameters arrive as separate scalars, locals are two SSA values, and a complex
; return is the aggregate { double, double } of example 64. `z * w` is inlined by clang as four products and two sums; only
; when BOTH parts are NaN (a quantum condition: the two `fcmp uno` flags) does it call __muldc3, the compiler-rt body
; reproduced in the .c file. That call becomes a quantum clone (mask 1000: the real part of z is the only quantum argument)
; called unconditionally; its two result handles are merged with the fast-path values by two selects on the conjunction
; flag (06 + 04). Inside the clone every branch on a quantum condition is flattened: block merges become selects on the
; local branch flag, the three-way phis in %85/%99 select on the conjunction of the flags along the one differing path,
; and the `!recalc` edge needs a NOT bracket. Every block predicate is a branch flag (rule 8): a conjunction is
; cqrt_and_i1 and a disjunction cqrt_or_i1 into a fresh |0> rail, re-applied to uncompute; a classical disjunct (isinf(b),
; isinf(bd), isinf(bc), classical because b, c, d are classical) is lifted to a seed rail cqrt_alloc_i1(c) (rule 7)
; that is freed after the flag. The `select` templates read those flags as their condition handle (rule 9). Conditions that
; depend only on b, c, d stay classical IR. The clone copies both parts out, uncomputes its whole chain, and its _unc twin
; recomputes it to zero the two result rails (64). Also shown: `twice`, a clone taking two quantum scalars and returning an
; aggregate.
; The recalculation's two llvm.fmuladd.f64 calls (%94, %97) are UNFUSED (§2, cf. 14): an fmul into a fresh product rail,
; then an fadd of the product and the addend; the product is uncomputed right after the sum it fed (rule 5).

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 26, 20, 18, 25, 4, 5, 2.
; Checked: creall(q) + cimagl(q), q = scale2(re + im*I) (measured).
; Clean: the real part of z (the slot's rail), the clone's result rail (zeroed by the twin, then freed), and every
; rail inside the clone and its twin.
; Kept: the user register re; the result rail (measured).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on re.
; On x86-64 a `long double complex` does not travel in registers: the caller builds it in an
; `alloca { x86_fp80, x86_fp80 }` and passes the pointer `byval`; the return comes back as the aggregate
; { x86_fp80, x86_fp80 } (rule 26). The alloca is a non-escaping slot pair (31, 52, rule 20): a field that holds a
; quantum value holds its HANDLE (type i32), a classical field stays a classical x86_fp80, so the slot type is the
; clone's mask applied field-wise, { i32, x86_fp80 } here (mask 10: real part quantum, imaginary part classical), and
; the GEP by byte offset becomes a field GEP. The clone reads the handle from the slot, computes out of place, copies
; its quantum result out, and returns a mask-typed aggregate { i32, x86_fp80 }: a handle for the quantum field, the
; classical value for the other (64 is the all-quantum case). The _unc twin takes the result handle and the slot
; pointer. Everything the caller allocated is uncomputed except the user register and the measured sum.
source_filename = "complex_long_double.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"

  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_f80(x86_fp80 %0)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_f80(%0, %1)  [register re]
  call void @cqrt_ry_f80(i32 %5, double %1)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_f80(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %6 = fmul x86_fp80 %2, 0xK00000000000000000000    ; IR: %6 = fmul x86_fp80 %2, 0  (classical)
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f80_hl(i32 %5, x86_fp80 %6)    ; IR: %7 = fadd x86_fp80 %6, %5  (real part of z; commutative, quantum operand first)
  %8 = getelementptr inbounds { i32, x86_fp80 }, ptr %4, i32 0, i32 1    ; IR: %8 = getelementptr i8, ptr %4, i64 16  (field 1)
  store i32 %7, ptr %4, align 16    ; IR: store x86_fp80 %7, ptr %4  (the slot takes the handle of the real part)
  store x86_fp80 %2, ptr %8, align 16    ; IR: store x86_fp80 %2, ptr %8  (classical imaginary part)
  %9 = call fastcc { i32, x86_fp80 } @__cq_q_scale2_10(ptr %4)    ; IR: %9 = call @scale2(byval %4), quantum clone (field 0 of the pointee quantum)
  %10 = extractvalue { i32, x86_fp80 } %9, 0    ; IR: %10 = extractvalue %9, 0  (handle of the real result; classical)
  %11 = extractvalue { i32, x86_fp80 } %9, 1    ; IR: %11 = extractvalue %9, 1  (classical imaginary result)
  %12 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f80_hl(i32 %10, x86_fp80 %11)    ; IR: %12 = fadd x86_fp80 %10, %11  [result rail]
  call fastcc void @__cq_q_scale2_10_unc(i32 %10, ptr %4)    ; IR: uncompute %10 (the call's quantum result)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %10)    ; IR: release the %10 rail (|0>)

name: 72_memset_array
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 22, 20, 14, 4, 5, 7, 2.
; Checked: memset_over_quantum: before + a[1], before = a[k & 3] read before the memset; memset_quantum_byte:
; b[0] + b[3] (measured).
; Clean: memset_over_quantum: the four fill-value rails x + i, both fixed-index copy-outs, the index rail x & 3, the
; basis-state handles 0 and c (rule 7), and the QRAM a (every store popped, then cqrt_qram_free); memset_quantum_byte:
; the fill byte (char)x, the index rail y & 3, both copy-outs and their zexts, the basis-state handle 7, and the QRAM b.
; In both, every store's tape slot (each pop returns it to |0>).
; Kept: the user registers (x; x and y); the result rail (measured).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x (memset_over_quantum); Ry(tx) on x and Ry(ty) on y (memset_quantum_byte).
; Both arrays are written at a QUANTUM index (a[x & 3] = c, b[y & 3] = 7: a quantum-offset store), so each is a QRAM
; for its whole lifetime (rule 20; holding quantum values alone would only make a slot array; the per-cell circuit is
; the backend's; ABI = the QRAM contract of §1.3): cqrt_qram_alloc_<W>(n) at the alloca (cells |0>) and every access ONE
; call, the classical-offset accesses in their _hl form. The quantum-index store is what keeps this the QRAM memset
; witness. llvm.memset over such an array is a
; fixed-size intrinsic, not a loop (rule 22): its lowering is one fixed-index store cqrt_qram_store_<W>_hl(arr, j, val)
; per cell (_hl = classical INDEX), not an unrolled ladder. memset_over_quantum: the fill loop writes the quantum value
; x + i into cell i by store_hl at the classical loop index (the value rail stays live and is uncomputed by its
; producer in the reverse loop, after its store is popped); before = a[k & 3] is a fixed-index copy-out
; cqrt_qram_load_<W>_hl(arr, j) -> fresh rail (cell preserved; its _unc un-copies once the cell holds that value
; again); memset(a, 0) is four store_hl of ONE basis-state handle cqrt_alloc_i32(0) (a store value is ALWAYS a handle;
; a classical value is materialised once, shared by every store that reads it, and freed after its last store is
; popped); the quantum-index write a[x & 3] = c is one cqrt_qram_store_<W>(arr, idx, val) with the logical-i32 index
; rail (x & 3; -O1's zext to i64 and the gep scaling are not emitted) and c as a handle. memset_quantum_byte: the fill
; byte is a quantum rail (trunc of x) and every i8 cell takes it by store_hl (one rail may feed many stores; it is
; uncomputed once, by its trunc, after the four stores are popped); the fixed-index reads b[0], b[3] are copy-outs.
; Each store owns a fresh tape slot: the displaced cell is swapped into the slot, then cell ^= val (a copy; val
; unchanged), so a store is a permutation of (cells, tape slots), not of the cells alone. Pops (_unc, same arguments)
; need the value, index and cells at their forward values (every value rail here is unrotated and live until after
; its pop) and are ordered last-in-first-out only among stores that may touch the same cell: the quantum-index store
; may touch every cell and is popped first, then the memset stores (distinct cells: they commute; written in reverse),
; then the fill stores in the reverse loop (each after the memset store of its cell); a copy-out is un-copied while its
; cell holds the value it had at the load (before = a[k & 3] after the memset stores are popped). Each pop returns its
; slot to |0>; then cqrt_qram_free releases the all-|0> array. The backend chooses the circuit.
source_filename = "memset_array.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %6, double %1)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [Ry]

  %18 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %2)    ; IR: store i32 %2, ptr %14: the classical value c as a basis-state handle
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32(i32 %5, i32 %17, i32 %18)    ; IR: store i32 %2, ptr %14: a[x & 3] = c  (one access; the backend fans out over the cells)

  call void @cqrt_qram_load_i32_hl_unc(i32 %19, i32 %5, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %16 (un-copy; the cell is unchanged since the copy-out)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %19)    ; IR: release it (|0>)

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %18)    ; IR: release the value handle (basis state c)

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %17)    ; IR: release the %12 rail (|0>)

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 22, 20, 14, 4, 5, 7, 2.
; Checked: memcpy_classical: a[0] + a[3] after a[x & 3] += 1 over the memcpy'd src; memcpy_quantum: a[1] + b[1] with
; b a copy of a = {x + i} and b[y & 3] = c (measured).
; Clean: memcpy_classical: the four basis-state source handles (rule 7), the index rail x & 3, the read-modify-write
; load and its increment, both fixed-index copy-outs, and the QRAM a; memcpy_quantum: the four fill rails x + i (the
; cells of the slot array a, uncomputed by the reverse fill loop once no store on b reads them), the index rail y & 3,
; the basis-state handle c, the copy-out b[1], and the QRAM b (every store popped, then cqrt_qram_free).
; Kept: the user registers (x; x and y); the result rail (measured).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x (memcpy_classical); Ry(tx) on x and Ry(ty) on y (memcpy_quantum).
; Rule 20 classifies each object by its accesses' offsets. An object with a quantum-offset store (or a quantum-offset
; load while it may hold a handle) is a QRAM for its whole lifetime (ABI = the QRAM contract of §1.3): cqrt_qram_alloc_<W>(n)
; at the alloca (cells |0>), every access ONE call, the classical-offset accesses in their _hl form (_hl = classical
; INDEX). An object with only classical offsets that may hold a handle is a SLOT ARRAY: a classical array of handles,
; loads and stores move handles and emit no gate. llvm.memcpy with a classical length works per cell (rule 22).
; memcpy_classical: a[x & 3] += 1 is a quantum-offset read-modify-write, so a is a QRAM from its alloca, and the memcpy
; from the classical source is, per cell, a classical load of src[j] materialised as a basis-state handle by
; cqrt_alloc_<W> (a QRAM store value is ALWAYS a handle) and one store_hl; the read is one cqrt_qram_load_<W>(arr, idx)
; -> fresh rail (cell preserved) with the logical-i32 index rail (x & 3; -O1's zext to i64 and the gep scaling are not
; emitted), the write-back one cqrt_qram_store_<W>(arr, idx, val) of the incremented rail; a[0], a[3] are fixed-index
; copy-outs cqrt_qram_load_<W>_hl. memcpy_quantum: a is only accessed at classical offsets (the fill a[i], the memcpy
; source cells, a[1]), so a is a slot array (alloca [4 x i32] of handles): the fill loop stores the rail x + i into slot
; i. b is written at the quantum index y & 3, so b is a QRAM, and memcpy(b, a) is a QRAM memcpy: per cell one slot load
; of a[j] (a handle, no gate) and one cqrt_qram_store_<W>_hl(b, j, handle); the quantum-index write b[y & 3] = c is one
; cqrt_qram_store_<W> of c as a handle; a[1] is a slot load (the rail x + 1 itself), b[1] a fixed-index copy-out. The
; backend keeps each displaced cell on its own tape; the stores are popped LIFO per array by their _unc (same args),
; copy-outs are un-copied, the fill rails are uncomputed by the reverse fill loop (reading each handle back from its
; slot) after b's stores that read them are popped, then cqrt_qram_free releases each all-|0> QRAM.

; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).

; loop and every classical value stay exactly as clang wrote them. The quantum-index read is the QROM of 29 and 30 with the
; runtime element count %6 as its length operand and the logical index rail x % n (i32) as its index; -O1's zext to i64
; and the gep scaling are address arithmetic and are not emitted (rule 20). The index is x % n, which lies in [0, n) for
; n > 0, so the QROM never reads past the array. n == 0 needs no guard: the urem template is total (§2: urem(x, 0) = x)
; and the QROM reads 0 at an index >= its length 0 (§2: out-of-range qrom_load), so the same calls cover it. At -O1 a
; VLA at function scope needs no llvm.stacksave/stackrestore (none is emitted here); inside a loop or a block they appear
; and stay classical calls around the classical alloca. The read value is the measured result, so only the index chain

; and free stay the classical calls clang wrote (rule 16: an allocation with a classical size whose block never
; becomes a QRAM is classical), and each cell stores the handle of its rail. Here the element type is i32, so a handle
; slot and an element have the same size and the allocation size and every GEP stand as written. For any other element
; type the block holds one i32 handle per element: the size n * sizeof(T) becomes n * 4 and every GEP stride and byte
; offset is rescaled from sizeof(T) to 4. The cells are uncomputed by a reverse loop that reads their handles back from
; the block, and it runs before free(a), while the block still holds them; only the result r is left for the
; measurement. Reading a[k] with k outside [0, n) is the program's own undefined behaviour and is emitted as written.

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 20, 4, 5, 2.
; Checked: a[0] ^ a[1] ^ a[2] ^ a[3] after a[x & 3] += y over a = {y, y+1, y+2, y+3} (measured).
; Clean: the three initializer rails y+1, y+2, y+3, the index rail x & 3, the old-value copy-out and the sum, the four
; fixed-index copy-outs and the two inner xors, every store's tape slot (each pop returns it to |0>), and the QRAM a
; (every store popped, then cqrt_qram_free).
; Kept: the user registers x and y (y is also cell 0's value; never freed); the result rail (measured).
; Rotations: Ry(tx) on x; Ry(ty) on y.
; The four cells hold QUANTUM values from the start (a[0] is the register y itself, a[1..3] fresh rails y+1..y+3) and
; the array is read AND written at a quantum index, so the whole local array is a QRAM (rule 20; address decoding
; is the backend's circuit; ABI = the QRAM contract of §1.3, reference conversions 30 and 84):
; cqrt_qram_alloc_i32(4) at the alloca (cells |0>), and each initializer cell is one cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl(arr, j,
; rail) with the classical index (_hl = classical INDEX) and the VALUE always a handle (the rail stays live and is
; uncomputed later by its own producer; y is the user register and is never freed). `a[x & 3] += y` with quantum x is
; a read-modify-write at the quantum index rail idx = x & 3 (the logical-i32 index: -O1's zext to i64 and the gep
; scaling are not emitted): ONE cqrt_qram_load_i32(arr, idx) -> old (copy-out, cells preserved), sum = add(old, y) into
; a fresh rail, ONE cqrt_qram_store_i32(arr, idx, sum) (the store owns a fresh tape slot: the displaced cell[idx] is swapped
; into it, then cell[idx] ^= sum, a copy; sum unchanged). The
; fixed-index loads after it are cqrt_qram_load_i32_hl(arr, j) copy-outs, and the xors go into fresh rails.
; Uncomputation runs in reverse order before the measurement: the xors, the four fixed-index copy-outs, then the
; stores are popped (_unc, same arguments: the value, index and cells hold their forward values; y, a store value, is
; not rotated again), last-in-first-out among stores that may touch the same cell: the quantum-index store, which may
; touch every cell, first; then the initializer stores of cells 3, 2, 1, 0 (distinct cells: they commute), sum and
; old between them (old is un-copied after the store it preceded is popped, when cell[idx] holds the old value again),
; each initializer rail by its own producer, and cqrt_qram_free once every cell and every tape slot is |0> again. The
; contract fixes the unitary (a permutation of (cells, tape slots): slot <-> cell[idx], then cell[idx] ^= sum); the
; backend chooses the circuit (fan-out per cell as in
; Bennett.jl memory.jl, bucket brigade).

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %2)  [register x]

; Checked: theta_quantum_angle: r + x; phi_quantum_angle: x (measured).

; Kept: the user register x of each function; theta_quantum_angle's r (rotated by the angle rail, frozen, measured).
; Rotations: theta_quantum_angle: Ry(tx) on x; Ry(tr) on r; Ry(A) on r with A the angle rail holding (double)x * c.
; phi_quantum_angle: Ry(tx) on x; phase(A) on the angle rail A = (double)x * c, uncontrolled; phase(A) under (x > k).
; A QUANTUM ANGLE (rule 15): the angle a = x * c is computed by the ordinary opcode lowering into an f64 REGISTER (the
; program's IEEE double, bit-exact, on a rail: sitofp then fmul_hl, rule 4). The rotation is then ONE gate primitive
; that reads that register: cqrt_ry_i32_qangle(r, A) applies Ry(val(A)) to r controlled by A's bits; the backend
; supplies the circuit (reduce val(A) exactly mod 4π, round it to nearest-even onto the grid 4π·k/2^N, one controlled
; Ry per ladder bit i with the weight 4π·2^(i-N), CONSTRUCTION_RULES §1.3; rotations about one axis add, so the product
; is Ry(val(A)) on every branch up to that rounding; no emitted angle comes out of floating-point arithmetic). The IR never spells the ladder. The angle register is only
; read, so it is uncomputed afterwards by the LIFO spine. cq_phi(a): e^(i a(x)) depends on the register, so it is a
; RELATIVE phase, never a deletable global one (rule 12): uncontrolled it is cqrt_rz_qangle(A), a phase on the angle
; register that A's uncompute kicks back onto x. Under the quantum condition x > k it is
; cqrt_rz_qangle_controlled(flag, A). No NOT-rail identity (rz(-theta) + global phase) may be used here: with a quantum
; theta the "global" leftover e^(i theta(A)) is relative. A fixed-point ladder spelled in the IR would bake the
; ladder's precision into the compiled program; the primitive leaves N to the backend (§0).

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 23, 4, 9, 5, 2.
; Checked: fenv_rounding: w + (double)m, w = ((x * c) + c) * c under the three modes, m the quantum mode;
; quantum_mode_classical_op: s = a + b rounded under the quantum mode (measured).
; Clean: fenv_rounding: the product y, the compare flag, the sum z; quantum_mode_classical_op: the compare flag and
; the mode rail.
; Kept: the user register x of each function; fenv_rounding's mode rail (measured as m) and result rail w;
; quantum_mode_classical_op's result rail s.
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x (each function).
; Full floating-point environment, part 1 of 3: the ROUNDING MODE (rule 23). Under `#pragma STDC FENV_ACCESS ON`
; clang -O1 emits llvm.experimental.constrained.* with round.dynamic: every such op reads the current mode. The fenv
; is program state (as the escaping global of 71), split in two: the HOST part, kept exactly by the real fenv calls
; for classical ops, and the QUANTUM part, the mode and flags as rails. The mode is classical (an i32 value the
; compiler tracks: the last classical fesetround argument, or fegetround() at entry) until a quantum value is written
; into it; then it is a handle and no host call is made. Template grammar (§1.2), one rule for all three fenv
; examples: cq_template_<op>[_<pred>]_<W>[_hl|_lh|_ll][_rm|_rmq][_exc][_unc]
;   _rm  = the mode is a classical i32 operand, last; _rmq = the mode is a handle, last; _exc = see example 81.
; A constrained op whose operands are all classical but whose mode is quantum is QUANTUM (its result depends on the
; mode): quantum_mode_classical_op shows it, `a + b` becomes cq_template_fadd_f64_ll_rmq. fegetround() under a quantum
; mode returns the mode handle itself. fpexcept.ignore here (`#pragma clang fp exceptions(ignore)`): no exception
; bits; 81 has them. Mode constants are the x86-64 host's: FE_TONEAREST 0, FE_DOWNWARD 1024, FE_UPWARD 2048,
; FE_TOWARDZERO 3072.

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"

  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_fmul_f64_hl_rm(i32 %5, double %2, i32 2048)    ; IR: %7 = constrained.fmul(%5, %2, round.dynamic)  [mode = classical 2048]

  %11 = call i32 @fesetround(i32 0)    ; IR: %13 = fesetround(0)  (classical again: host call, mode operand 0)
  %12 = call i32 @cq_template_fmul_f64_hl_rm(i32 %10, double %2, i32 0)    ; IR: %14 = constrained.fmul(%11, %2, round.dynamic)  [mode = classical 0]

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %10)    ; IR: release the %11 rail (|0>)

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release the %7 rail (|0>)

  %15 = call double @llvm.experimental.constrained.sitofp.f64.i32(i32 %14, metadata !"round.dynamic", metadata !"fpexcept.ignore")    ; IR: %17  (classical, host mode 0)
  %16 = call double @llvm.experimental.constrained.fadd.f64(double %13, double %15, metadata !"round.dynamic", metadata !"fpexcept.ignore")    ; IR: %18  (classical, host mode 0)

  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f64_ll_rmq(double %3, double %4, i32 %8)    ; IR: %10 = constrained.fadd(%3, %4, round.dynamic)  [both operands classical, the mode a handle: s is QUANTUM]
  %10 = call i32 @fesetround(i32 0)    ; IR: %11 = fesetround(0)  (classical again: host call; the quantum mode is no longer state)

; (measured).

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 23, 18, 26, 5.
; Checked: inexact (%17 -> %31) and w (%27 -> %32), summed classically.
; Clean: every dropped flags rail (the held flags %14 after feupdateenv, scale's returned flags %23 after fesetexceptflag,
; the FE_UPWARD flags %29 after fesetenv), the exception-bit rails %11 and %28, the quantum part of inexact's test (%16),
; p (%10), y (%13), scale's result rail %22, and inside the clone its whole chain.
; Kept: x (%8, the rotated register); the final flags rail %19 (restored | held, an output of rule 23, never freed);
; inexact (%17) and w (%27), measured.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; Full floating-point environment, part 3 of 3: SAVED ENVIRONMENTS and CALLS. Mode and flags are split into a host part
; and a quantum part as in 80 and 81. A fenv_t or fexcept_t object keeps its host part through the real calls on the real
; alloca; its quantum part (the flags rail, and the mode when it is a handle) is known statically at every fenv call, so it
; is carried as SSA values exactly as -O1 carries a promoted slot (an object that escapes or is written in a loop is a
; classical slot of handles, as 31/70). feholdexcept(&env): save {mode, flags}, clear the flags (the rail becomes empty).
; feupdateenv: restore the saved part, then OR the current flags in. fegetexceptflag/fesetexceptflag(FE_ALL_EXCEPT): save /
; reinstate the flags handle itself (a narrower mask would and/or it). fegetenv/fesetenv: save / reinstate both. A flags
; rail that stops being current state (dropped by fesetexceptflag or fesetenv) is uncomputed; the final one is an output
; and stays. CALLS: a clone of a function that does constrained FP work takes the caller's mode (literal or handle) and
; quantum flags handle as two trailing parameters and returns { result, flags' } (the aggregate ABI of 64), BOTH copied
; into fresh rails before the body is uncomputed (rule 18); its _unc twin takes both returned handles first, then the same
; operands, and zeroes both; the caller frees both after the twin. scale's v * c + c is a constrained llvm.fmuladd, which is
; UNFUSED (§2, cf. 14): a constrained fmul then fadd, each with its _rm value template and _exc exception-bit template;
; flags' ORs both exception rails into the caller's flags, and every partial rail is uncomputed in dependency order.

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 4, 2, 25.
; Checked: fmod_qc: fmod(x, c) (%5 -> %6). fmod_cq: fmod(c, x) (%5 -> %6). fmodf_qq: fmodf(x, y) (%7 -> %8).
; fmodl_qc: fmodl(x, c) (%5 -> %6).
; Clean: nothing to free: each function is one template from its register(s) to the measured rail.
; Kept: the rotated register(s) of each function (%4; %4; %5 and %6; %4) and each measured result rail.
; Rotations: fmod_qc: (Ry, x, th, 1). fmod_cq: (Ry, x, th, 1). fmodf_qq: (Ry, x, tx, 1); (Ry, y, ty, 1).
; fmodl_qc: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; fmod/fmodf/fmodl with builtins on reach -O1 IR as the frem instruction, not a call, so they lower like fdiv (13, 19):
; cq_template_frem_<W>[_hl|_lh] out of place into a fresh rail. Backend coverage: frem is exact (the IEEE remainder of a

; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).

; (rule 8). A QUANTUM POINTER IS A FAT POINTER (tag, idx) (rule 21): tag is an i32 rail naming the OBJECT (0 = NULL,

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 21, 4, 5, 2.
; Checked: ptrdiff_q: q - p in elements (%11 -> %12). ptr_less: p < q (%24 -> %25). ptr_eq_two_objects: p == q (%16 -> %17).
; Clean: every rail but the registers and the result rails: the byte-offset chains of ptrdiff_q (%5..%10), the tag and
; cell-index chains of ptr_less (%6..%12), its base select (%15, %16), its two address chains (%17..%22) and its
; compare %23, the tag and index chains of ptr_eq_two_objects (%6..%12), its two compares and their conjunction
; (%13..%15), all uncomputed in LIFO order and freed. The arrays a, b of ptr_eq_two_objects are classical memory and
; are never touched.
; Kept: the register x of each function (%4 / %5 / %5, rotated) and each result rail (measured).
; Rotations: ptrdiff_q: (Ry, x, th, 1). ptr_less: (Ry, x, th, 1). ptr_eq_two_objects: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; Pointer arithmetic and comparison on fat pointers (tag, idx; example 84), idx a CELL index (rule 21). Three shapes.
; ptrdiff_q: -O1 already folds p = a + i, q = a + j, q - p into integer IR (p's byte offset (x & 3) * 4 = %6, q's byte
; offset ((x >> 2) & 3) * 4 = %8, sub, ashr exact by the stride); no pointer survives, so that IR is lowered as the
; integer ops it is. ptr_less: p is a select of two objects (tag rail) plus the cell index (x >> 1) & 3, q is
; a + ((x >> 3) & 3) (classical tag 1, cell-index rail); the GEPs add the C index expression to the base's idx 0 (the
; zext to i64 and the scaling by sizeof(int) are address arithmetic, never emitted for an access). a and b are
; PARAMETERS, so they may alias (b may point into a's array): the compare is over ADDRESSES (rule 21),
; base[tag] + 4 * idx, the classical bases being the parameter values themselves. p's base is a select_i64_ll on the
; tag (tag == 2 ? b : a, the complement a innermost), q's base the classical a (an _hl literal); the byte offset 4 * idx
; (zext, shl by 2) is emitted here only as part of the address; icmp ult on pointers is the unsigned i64 compare of the
; two addresses. ptr_eq_two_objects: a and b are two distinct local allocations of the function, so icmp eq on pointers
; reduces to tag == tag' AND idx == idx'; pointers into different objects are never equal, which the tag test decides.
; The conjunction is DATA (it is zext'ed into the result), so it is the cq_template_and_i1 form of rule 8, not a flag.
; Object tables: ptr_less: 1 = a (param %2), 2 = b (param %3); ptr_eq_two_objects: 1 = a (%3), 2 = b (%4). No deref

name: 87_pointer_induction
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 21, 20, 14 (re-rolled; a_K kept), 8, 9, 4, 5, 7, 2.
; Checked: n = the number of leading nonzero bytes of s = {c, c + 1, c ^ 3, 0}, over at most K = 4 trips (measured).
; Clean: the initializer rails c + 1 and c ^ 3, every trip's load *p, its flag, n + 1, idx + 1, both select merges and
; its predicate a_0..a_{K-1} (popped and uncomputed by the mirror, the K-th included), the after-trip-K exit test (its
; load and flag, uncomputed at once), the |1> seed and the |0> seeds of p.idx and n (rule 7), and the QRAM s (every
; store popped, then cqrt_qram_free).
; Kept: the user register c (also cell 0's value); the copied-out result rail (measured); a_K (%27: the exit test
; *p != 0 evaluated after the K-th body, ANDed with trip K's predicate; rule 14: a_K = 1 iff the loop would run a
; (K+1)-th trip, which is observable; a loop that exits after exactly K trips reads 0). No range fact bounds the trip
; count (it depends on memory contents), so the cutoff is K and a_K is kept.
; Rotations: Ry(th) on c.
; A POINTER AS THE LOOP-CARRIED VARIABLE of a rolled loop whose exit depends on quantum data (rules 21, 14). The
; buffer s is object 1; its cells hold QUANTUM values from the start (s[0] is the register c, s[1], s[2] fresh rails,
; s[3] the classical 0), and the loop reads it through p at a QUANTUM offset (p's idx is a loop-carried rail), so by
; rule 20 (a quantum-offset load of an object that may hold a handle) the whole array is a QRAM for its lifetime (the
; address decoding is the backend's circuit; ABI = the QRAM contract of §1.3, reference conversions 30 and 84):
; cqrt_qram_alloc_i8(4) at the alloca (cells |0>), each initializer cell one cqrt_qram_store_i8_hl(s, j, rail) with
; the classical index and the value always a handle (the rail stays live and is uncomputed by its own producer; c is the
; user register and is never freed); s[3] = 0 writes the all-|0> cell's own value and needs nothing (30's memset-0
; rule). p is a fat pointer (84) with the classical tag 1 and a loop-carried idx rail seeded |0>, like n; idx is the
; logical-i32 CELL index (p++ is idx + 1; -O1's i64 byte offset is not emitted, the cells are bytes).
; Re-rolled (rule 14): -O1's pre-header test *s != 0 is the latch test *(p + 1) != 0 one trip earlier (SCEV: p starts
; at s), so it is trip 0 of the loop: trip j loads *p at the carried idx (ONE cqrt_qram_load_i8 per trip, copy-out,
; cells preserved), tests it and forms a_j = a_{j-1} & NOT(*p == 0) from the |1> seed; n++ and p++ are select-merged
; on a_j (rule 9; the arm's pure ops run unguarded as in 84). The literal 4 is K [K]. After trip K the exit test is
; evaluated once more on the carried idx and a_K = a_{K-1} & NOT(*p == 0) is kept; that load and flag are uncomputed at
; once. idx only grows under a_j, so it never passes 3 (s[3] = 0 stops the chain); a read at 4 would be the program's
; own read of s[4] and reads 0 by §2. After n is copied out the reverse loop pops each trip and uncomputes it (the
; load's _unc un-copies against the preserved cell), every trip predicate included. Then the initializer stores are
; popped (cells 2, 1, 0), each rail by its producer, and cqrt_qram_free.
source_filename = "pointer_induction.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

define i32 @count_nonzero(i8 noundef zeroext %0, double noundef %1) {
  %3 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_alloc_i8(i32 4)    ; IR: %3 = alloca [4 x i8]: object 1, a 4-cell QRAM of bytes, cells |0> (read at a quantum offset while it holds handles)
  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i8(i8 %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_ui8(%0, %1)  [register c]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i8(i32 %4, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_ui8(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i8_hl(i32 %3, i32 0, i32 %4)    ; IR: store i8 %4, ptr %3: s[0] = c  (fixed index, the value a handle: the register c itself)
  %5 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i8_hl(i32 %4, i8 1)    ; IR: %5 = add i8 %4, 1
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i8_hl(i32 %3, i32 1, i32 %5)    ; IR: store i8 %5, ptr %6: s[1] = c + 1  (%6 = gep 1 is cell 1)
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_xor_i8_hl(i32 %4, i8 3)    ; IR: %7 = xor i8 %4, 3
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i8_hl(i32 %3, i32 2, i32 %6)    ; IR: store i8 %7, ptr %8: s[2] = c ^ 3  (%8 = gep 2 is cell 2); store i8 0, ptr %9: s[3] = 0 writes the |0> cell's own value, nothing emitted
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: incoming %3 of phi %16: p = s, p.idx = cell 0 (p.tag is the classical 1)
  %8 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: incoming 0 of phi %17 / %13
  %9 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 true)    ; IR: predicate of reaching the loop guard in %2 (always 1)
  br label %10

10:
  %11 = phi i32 [ 0, %2 ], [ %22, %10 ]    ; IR: trip index, bounded by K  [K]
  %12 = phi i32 [ %7, %2 ], [ %21, %10 ]    ; IR: %16 = phi ptr [ %19, %15 ], [ %3, %2 ]: p.idx
  %13 = phi i32 [ %8, %2 ], [ %19, %10 ]    ; IR: %17 = phi i32 [ %18, %15 ], [ 0, %2 ]
  %14 = phi i32 [ %9, %2 ], [ %17, %10 ]    ; IR: predicate of reaching this trip's test
  %15 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i8(i32 %3, i32 %12)    ; IR: %10 = load i8, ptr %3 (trip 0) / %20 = load i8, ptr %19: *p, ONE access at the index rail (copy-out, cells preserved)
  %16 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i8_hl(i32 %15, i8 0)    ; IR: %11 = icmp eq i8 %10, 0 (trip 0) / %21 = icmp eq i8 %20, 0
  %17 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: predicate of this trip
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %16)    ; IR: bracket: the loop body runs when the test is false
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %14, i32 %16, i32 %17)    ; IR: br i1 %11 (trip 0) / br i1 %21 not taken: a_j = a_{j-1} & NOT test
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %16)    ; IR: bracket
  %18 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %13, i32 1)    ; IR: %18 = add nuw nsw i32 %17, 1
  %19 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %17, i32 %18, i32 %13)    ; IR: next %17 / %13 = a ? %18 : %17
  %20 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %12, i32 1)    ; IR: %19 = getelementptr i8, ptr %16, i64 1: p.idx + 1 (the logical-i32 cell index)
  %21 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %17, i32 %20, i32 %12)    ; IR: next %16 = a ? %19 : %16
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %12)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %13)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %14)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %15)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %16)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %18)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %20)
  %22 = add nuw nsw i32 %11, 1
  %23 = icmp ult i32 %22, 4    ; IR: K-bounded br i1 %21, label %12, label %15  [K]
  br i1 %23, label %10, label %24

24:
  %25 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i8(i32 %3, i32 %21)    ; IR: %20 = load i8, ptr %19 after trip K: *p for the exit test that would admit a (K+1)-th trip
  %26 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i8_hl(i32 %25, i8 0)    ; IR: %21 = icmp eq i8 %20, 0 after trip K
  %27 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: a_K = predicate of trip K & NOT that test  [output rail, kept]
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %26)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %17, i32 %26, i32 %27)    ; IR: br i1 %21 not taken once more (rule 14)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %26)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i8_hl_unc(i32 %26, i32 %25, i8 0)    ; IR: uncompute that test
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %26)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_qram_load_i8_unc(i32 %25, i32 %3, i32 %21)    ; IR: un-copy that load against the preserved cell
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %25)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  %28 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: %13 = phi i32 [ 0, %2 ], [ %18, %15 ]  [copied-out result]
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %19, i32 %28)    ; IR: %13
  br label %29

29:
  %30 = phi i32 [ 0, %24 ], [ %41, %29 ]    ; IR: reverse trip index
  %31 = phi i32 [ %21, %24 ], [ %40, %29 ]    ; IR: %16 written by this trip
  %32 = phi i32 [ %19, %24 ], [ %39, %29 ]    ; IR: %17 written by this trip
  %33 = phi i32 [ %17, %24 ], [ %38, %29 ]    ; IR: predicate of this trip
  %34 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: %19 (p.idx + 1) of this trip
  %35 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: %18 (n + 1)
  %36 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: the test flag %11 / %21
  %37 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: the load %10 / %20
  %38 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: predicate of the previous trip (trip 0: the |1> seed)
  %39 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: %17 incoming
  %40 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: %16 incoming
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %32, i32 %33, i32 %35, i32 %39)    ; IR: uncompute next %17
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %32)    ; IR: release next %17 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %35, i32 %39, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %18
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %35)    ; IR: release %18 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %31, i32 %33, i32 %34, i32 %40)    ; IR: uncompute next %16
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %31)    ; IR: release next %16 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %34, i32 %40, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %19
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %34)    ; IR: release %19 (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %36)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %38, i32 %36, i32 %33)    ; IR: uncompute the predicate of this trip (every trip 1..K; a_K is a separate rail)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %36)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %33)    ; IR: release the predicate (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i8_hl_unc(i32 %36, i32 %37, i8 0)    ; IR: uncompute %11 / %21
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %36)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_qram_load_i8_unc(i32 %37, i32 %3, i32 %40)    ; IR: un-copy %10 / %20 against the preserved cell
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %37)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  %41 = add nuw nsw i32 %30, 1
  %42 = icmp ult i32 %41, 4    ; IR: K  [K]
  br i1 %42, label %29, label %43

43:
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %38)    ; IR: release the |1> seed directly (rule 7: known basis state)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %39)    ; IR: release incoming 0 of phi %17 (never written, |0>)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %40)    ; IR: release incoming %3 of phi %16 (p.idx seed, never written, |0>)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i8_hl_unc(i32 %3, i32 2, i32 %6)    ; IR: pop the initializer of s[2]
  call void @cq_template_xor_i8_hl_unc(i32 %6, i32 %4, i8 3)    ; IR: uncompute %7 by its producer
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i8_hl_unc(i32 %3, i32 1, i32 %5)    ; IR: pop the initializer of s[1]
  call void @cq_template_add_i8_hl_unc(i32 %5, i32 %4, i8 1)    ; IR: uncompute %5 by its producer
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %5)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i8_hl_unc(i32 %3, i32 0, i32 %4)    ; IR: pop the initializer of s[0] (the register c stays allocated: a user register)
  call void @cqrt_qram_free(i32 %3)    ; IR: llvm.lifetime.end: release the array (all cells |0>)
  %44 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %28)    ; IR: %14 = cq_measure_si32(%13)
  ret i32 %44    ; IR: ret i32 %14
}

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 21, 20, 9, 4, 5, 7, 2.
; Checked: a[0] + b[1] + *q after p[(x >> 1) & 1] = v through p = tab[x & 1] and tab[(x >> 2) & 1] = &s.g,
; q = tab[1] (measured).
; Clean: every index rail (x & 1, (x >> 1) & 1, (x >> 2) & 1 and their shifts), p's tag and idx copy-outs, p's cell
; idx, the object guards of the store and of *q, the QRAM load of b, the QROM load of s and their merge select, q's two
; halves, the a[0] and b[1] copy-outs and their sum, every basis-state handle (initializers, v, the fat constant (3, 1);
; rule 7), and the four QRAMs a, b, tab.tag, tab.idx (every store popped, then cqrt_qram_free).
; Kept: the user register x; the result rail (measured).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x.
; NESTED POINTERS (rule 21): a cell that holds a pointer holds a fat pointer (84), i.e. two values, tag and idx, each
; classical or a handle. Object table: 1 = a (%4), 2 = b (%5), 3 = s (%6, fields f = cell 0 and g = cell 1), 4 = tab
; (%7, two pointer cells). Classification per object (rule 20, over every access): tab is written at the QUANTUM cell
; index k = (x >> 2) & 1, so it is a QRAM; a and b are written through p + j, whose idx (tab's idx half + (x >> 1) & 1)
; is QUANTUM, so both are QRAMs (a quantum-offset store); s is only READ, at q's idx, a handle loaded from tab, i.e. at a
; quantum offset, and only ever holds the classical 5, 6, so it is classical memory read by a QROM
; (cq_template_qrom_load_i32, length 2), never a QRAM. A QRAM's classical initializer is one
; cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl(arr, j, cqrt_alloc_i32(v)) per nonzero cell. tab, whose cells hold TWO values, is modelled as
; TWO i32 QRAMs over the same cell index, one for the tags and one for the idxs (a pointer cell is written and read as
; the pair; a single wider QRAM would pack two logical values into one bit pattern and need shifts on every access). Its
; initializer stores the tags (1, 2); the idx halves are 0, and a |0> cell needs no store. Every idx is a CELL index:
; -O1's zext to i64 and the gep scaling (8 bytes into tab, 4 bytes into a/b) are not emitted, so &s.g is the classical
; fat constant (3, 1) (byte 4 = cell 1 of s). pp = tab + i is the fat pointer (4, i) with a classical tag, so p = *pp is
; an UNGUARDED one-call load of each half: cqrt_qram_load_i32(tab_tag, i), cqrt_qram_load_i32(tab_idx, i) -> the p.tag
; and p.idx rails. The store through p + j reaches p's provenance, every pointer tab held when it was loaded, objects a
; and b: ONE cqrt_qram_store_i32_controlled(g_o, arr_o, idx, v) per object under g_o = tag == o (block predicate:
; none), v a basis-state handle shared by both origins. Storing &s.g at tab + k is one unconditional cqrt_qram_store_i32
; per half (tag 3, idx 1 as handles). q = tab[1] is a fixed-index copy-out of both halves (cqrt_qram_load_i32_hl). *q
; is a deref over cell 1's provenance, the union of what was stored into it, b (the initial constant) and s: one pure,
; unguarded quantum-offset read per object (cqrt_qram_load_i32(b, q.idx) for the QRAM b, the QROM of s), merged by ONE
; select on g_b = q.tag == 2 with the complement s innermost (rule 9; the provenance {b, s} is exhaustive). The address
; decoding is the backend's circuit. Everything is uncomputed in reverse, each array's stores popped LIFO (tab_tag: the
; k store, then the initializer), then cqrt_qram_free releases the arrays.

  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_controlled(i32 %23, i32 %4, i32 %21, i32 %22)    ; IR: store into a: a[idx] = v under g_a (one access; the backend fans out over the cells)
  %24 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %17, i32 2)    ; IR: guard g_b = tag == 2 (object b)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_controlled(i32 %24, i32 %5, i32 %21, i32 %22)    ; IR: store into b: b[idx] = v under g_b
  %25 = call i32 @cq_template_lshr_i32_hl(i32 %9, i32 2)    ; IR: %19 = lshr i32 %8, 2  (%18 = &s.g is the classical fat constant (3, 1): object 3, cell 1)
  %26 = call i32 @cq_template_and_i32_hl(i32 %25, i32 1)    ; IR: %20 = and i32 %19, 1  [k, the cell index into tab; %21 zext and the gep %22's 8-byte scaling are not emitted]
  %27 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 3)    ; IR: store ptr %18, ptr %22: the tag 3 (s) as a basis-state handle
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32(i32 %7, i32 %26, i32 %27)    ; IR: store ptr %18, ptr %22: tab[k].tag = 3 (one access; the displaced cell goes on the backend's tape)
  %28 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 1)    ; IR: store ptr %18, ptr %22: the idx 1 (cell of s.g; was byte 4) as a basis-state handle
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32(i32 %8, i32 %26, i32 %28)    ; IR: store ptr %18, ptr %22: tab[k].idx = 1
  %29 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i32_hl(i32 %7, i32 1)    ; IR: %23 = load ptr, ptr %9: q.tag = tab[1].tag  (fixed index: copy-out)
  %30 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i32_hl(i32 %8, i32 1)    ; IR: %23: q.idx = tab[1].idx

; Checked: *q + v, q = (int *)((uintptr_t)((x & 1) ? a : b) ^ (x & 4)) (measured): (x & 1 ? a : b)[(x & 4) >> 2] + v.
; Clean: every pointer-arithmetic rail (the tag select, both object flags, the base select, the flat address, the
; rebuilt byte offset and cell index), both QROM loads and their merge select.
; Kept: the user register x; the result rail (measured).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x.
; A quantum pointer is a fat pointer (tag, idx) (84, rule 21): p = (x & 1) ? a : b has the quantum tag select(x & 1 == 0,
; 2, 1) over the object table (object 1 = a (%4), object 2 = b (%5); 8 bytes, 2 i32 cells each) and the classical cell idx
; 0. ptrtoint and inttoptr are the two crossings between the fat form and the flat host address:
;   ptrtoint  u = base[tag] + 4 * idx  a select on the object flag over the classical bases (provenance {a, b}: b is the
;                                      complement, no NULL arm), plus the byte offset of idx (nothing here: idx = 0);
;   inttoptr  of an integer DERIVED FROM ptrtoint(p) keeps p's provenance (rule 21, LLVM's rule): tag = p's tag (the

;             and trunc to the logical i32 index rail. No range test: the result never depends on where the host placed
;             a and b (only an integer of unknown origin is decoded by range tests over the candidate objects).
; The integer arithmetic in between (`or disjoint` = the xor of the C source) is the ordinary i64 template (rule 4). The
; host addresses are classical runtime operands of the templates (the trace prints them as P<n>+<off>); a and b are

; cell index is QUANTUM, so the deref is a quantum-offset access of each object in the provenance {a, b} (rule 21); a and

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 22, 20, 21, 9, 7, 4, 5.
; Checked: memcpy_quantum_len: d[0] + d[3] (the result rail, measured). memcpy_quantum_src: d[0] + d[1] (the result
; rail, measured).
; Clean: every rail but the register and the result: the length rails n, m (and x >> 2), the per-cell guards, every
; per-cell select rail (the slot gets the handle it held before back), the source-object flag and the merged source byte,
; the tag and length selects, the two zexts of the reads, and the per-cell initializer seeds 9 (never written: freed
; directly, rule 7).
; Kept: the register x of each function (rotated) and each result rail (measured).
; Rotations: memcpy_quantum_len: (Ry, x, th, 1). memcpy_quantum_src: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; Rule 20: d is never accessed at a QUANTUM OFFSET (the intrinsics write fixed cells j, the reads are d[0], d[3] / d[0],
; d[1]), so it is not a QRAM; it may hold a handle (the quantum-length intrinsics make its cells quantum), so it is a SLOT
; ARRAY: a classical array of handles, one 4-byte slot per CELL. The cell is the element type, unsigned char, so -O1's
; punned initializer store (i32 151587081 / i16 2313) is one store per byte cell and its byte-offset GEPs are cell
; indices (size 1). Slot cells are homogeneous (rule 20): each cell holds a handle from the start, the classical 9 as a
; basis-state seed alloc_i8(9) per cell (rule 7; no cell is ever written in place, rule 4).
; Rule 22: llvm.memcpy / llvm.memset with a QUANTUM LENGTH n (bytes) guard cell j (size 1) by n >= j + 1, i.e. the flag
; n >u j; the guarded cell is select(flag_j, new, old) into a fresh rail (rule 9) and the slot takes the new handle. Only
; cells some execution can touch exist: cell j iff j < the length's upper bound. memcpy_quantum_len: n = x & 3 <= 3 and
; m = (x >> 2) & 3 <= 3 (known bits), so both intrinsics cover cells 0..2, src[3] is never loaded and d[3] keeps its seed.
; A classical source byte is a host load (the select's literal arm, select_i8_lh); the memset fill is the literal 0.
; The length is compared as the logical i32 (-O1's zext to i64 is not emitted, like an index).
; memcpy_quantum_src: the source is a quantum fat pointer (rule 21; object table 1 = d, 2 = s1, 3 = s2; tag rail =
; select(x & 1 == 0, 3, 2), idx the CLASSICAL 0 + j). A quantum tag with a classical idx is a guarded classical-offset
; access of each object in the provenance: s1, s2 are classical memory, so the source byte j is two classical host loads

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 14, 16, 20, 21.
; Checked: heap_quantum_size: r = a[1] + a[5] (measured). heap_in_loop: last ? last[0] : 7 (measured).
; Clean: heap_quantum_size: the quantum size n & 3 and its zext, the index rail k & 3, the value handles v and 1, the
; copy-out a[1] and the free predicate k > 100, all freed; both stores are popped (their tape slots back to |0>), the
; realloc undone and the QRAM a released. heap_in_loop: the trip count x & 3, the NULL tag seed, the |1> seed predicate,
; every trip's rails (exit compare, trip predicate, x + i and its trunc, which is the trip object's cell, the tag
; select) popped and uncomputed, the object flags, the select chain of the read and its zext, the null test.
; Kept: heap_quantum_size: n and k, the rotated registers, and r (measured). heap_in_loop: x (the rotated register) and
; the result (measured). No trip predicate is kept: the loop's exit is quantum (i == x & 3) and its cutoff is
; min(K, B) with B = 3, the upper bound of the trip count x & 3 from LLVM's range facts (rule 14); B <= K, so a_K is
; not kept and every predicate, the last included, is uncomputed by the mirror.
; Rotations: heap_quantum_size: (Ry, n, tn, 1); (Ry, k, tk, 1). heap_in_loop: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; HEAP OBJECTS are objects of the table like an alloca and are classified by rule 20 over all their accesses.
; heap_quantum_size: a[k & 3] = v is a QUANTUM-OFFSET store, so the block (malloc site and its realloc: the same object)
; is a QRAM for its whole lifetime and every other access is the _hl form: cqrt_qram_alloc_i8 at the malloc site with
; the upper bound of its quantum size, 3 byte cells (n & 3 lies in [0, 3]; a cell past the real size n & 3 is the
; program's own undefined behaviour, read as the cell's content), and realloc(a, 6) is cqrt_qram_realloc_i8(a, 6) -> a'
; (§1.3: a logical resize to 6 cells, no gate, no cell moves; cells 3..5 are new |0> cells), undone by
; cqrt_qram_realloc_i8_unc(a', 3) after every store made through a' is popped. No host block is kept: every cell is a
; QRAM cell, so malloc and realloc emit no host call. The store is ONE cqrt_qram_store_i8(a, idx, v) with the
; logical-i32 index rail k & 3 (-O1's zext to i64 and the gep are not emitted) and v materialised as a basis-state
; handle. It runs at the logical size 3: on the branch k & 3 == 3 its index is out of range and the store is a no-op
; whose tape slot stays |0> (§2); the realloc does not retroactively make it land in cell 3. a[5] = 1 is
; cqrt_qram_store_i8_hl(a', 5, 1) of a basis-state handle (-O1 folded the later read of a[5] to 1); the read a[1] is a
; fixed-index copy-out cqrt_qram_load_i8_hl(a', 1). Each store owns a fresh tape slot (the displaced cell is swapped in,
; then cell ^= v). FREE under a quantum predicate emits nothing (rule 16): deallocation is a lifetime end, a reset
; cannot be conditioned on quantum data, so the block lives to the end of the scope. There the copy-out is un-copied
; (cell 1 holds the value it had at the load), the store a[5] = 1 is popped (made through a', so before the realloc is
; undone), the realloc is undone, and the quantum-index store is popped at the same logical size 3 as its forward
; (stores to cells {0, 1, 2} and {5} are disjoint and commute; pop preconditions hold: v, 1 and k & 3 are unchanged),
; then the QRAM is released. The predicate is computed and uncomputed as any flag.
; heap_in_loop: the loop exit i == x & 3 is quantum and the trip count has the range bound B = 3, so the loop is rolled
; for min(K, B) = 3 trips (tagged [B]: independent of K for K >= 3) under the predicate chain seeded |1> (rule 14). A
; malloc site inside the loop is one object per (site, trip): tags 1..3 for trips 0..2, three host mallocs. Each object
; is written only at the classical offset 0 (p[0] = x + i), and the deref last[0] after the loop has a QUANTUM TAG but
; the CLASSICAL idx 0 (rule 21: a guarded classical-offset access per object, merged by select), so no object is a QRAM:
; each may hold a handle and is a SLOT ARRAY of one cell, a heap block of handle cells (malloc(1): one byte cell = one
; 4-byte handle slot, host malloc(4)). The block pointers sit in a classical table filled by the rolled loop. The store
; is a slot store of the rail trunc(x + i) (no gate); it runs unguarded under the trip predicate because the object is
; fresh in its trip and a trip that did not run never has its object addressed (the select of rule 20 would differ only
; on branches where the cell is unobservable). The read is one slot load per object (the handle, no gate) merged by
; cq_template_select_i8 on the object flags tag == o, chained with object 3 (the complement) innermost (rule 9); the
; NULL test then selects 7. Everything is uncomputed in reverse order before the measurement: the read's chain, then per
; trip (last first) its tag select, its cell rail by its producers, its predicate. The heap blocks are never freed by the
; program and stay allocated (classical host memory). Object tables: heap_quantum_size: 1 = a (QRAM of 3, then 6 byte
; cells). heap_in_loop: j+1 = the block of trip j (a 1-cell slot block).
source_filename = "heap_quantum.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"


define i32 @heap_quantum_size(i8 noundef zeroext %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2, double noundef %3, i8 noundef zeroext %4) {
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i8(i8 %0)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_ui8(%0, %1)  [register n]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i8(i32 %6, double %1)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_ui8(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %2)    ; IR: %7 = cq_theta_ui32(%2, %3)  [register k]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %7, double %3)    ; IR: %7 = cq_theta_ui32(%2, %3)  [Ry]
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_and_i8_hl(i32 %6, i8 3)    ; IR: %8 = and i8 %6, 3  [the quantum size, range [0, 4)]
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_zext_i8_to_i64(i32 %8)    ; IR: %9 = zext nneg i8 %8 to i64
  %10 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_alloc_i8(i32 3)    ; IR: %10 = call @malloc(%9): object 1, a QRAM at the upper bound 3 of its quantum size n & 3: 3 byte cells |0> (no host block)
  %11 = call i32 @cq_template_and_i32_hl(i32 %7, i32 3)    ; IR: %11 = and i32 %7, 3  [the index rail; %12 = zext to i64 and the gep %13 are not emitted]
  %12 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i8(i8 %4)    ; IR: store i8 %4, ptr %13: the classical value v as a basis-state handle (a QRAM store value is always a handle)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i8(i32 %10, i32 %11, i32 %12)    ; IR: store i8 %4, ptr %13: a[k & 3] = v  (one access at size 3; the displaced cell goes into this store's tape slot; on the branch k & 3 == 3 the index is out of range: no-op, the slot stays |0> (§2))
  %13 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_realloc_i8(i32 %10, i32 6)    ; IR: %14 = call @realloc(%10, 6): the same object resized to 6 cells (logical resize: cells 0..2 keep their state, cells 3..5 are new |0> cells; no gate); the result is the bus from here on
  %14 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i8(i8 1)    ; IR: store i8 1, ptr %15: the classical 1 as a basis-state handle
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i8_hl(i32 %13, i32 5, i32 %14)    ; IR: %15 = gep %14, 5; store i8 1, ptr %15: a[5] = 1  (fixed index 5 of the same QRAM)
  %15 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i8_hl(i32 %13, i32 1)    ; IR: %16 = getelementptr i8, ptr %14, 1; %17 = load i8, ptr %16: a[1]  (fixed-index copy-out)
  %16 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_ugt_i32_hl(i32 %7, i32 100)    ; IR: %18 = icmp ugt i32 %7, 100  [predicate of block %19]
  ; IR: br i1 %18 -> block %19: free(%15) under a quantum predicate emits nothing (rule 16); the block lives to the end of the scope
  %17 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i8_hl(i32 %15, i8 1)    ; IR: %21 = add i8 %17, 1  (a[5] folded to 1)  [result rail]
  call void @cq_template_icmp_ugt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %16, i32 %7, i32 100)    ; IR: uncompute %18
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %16)    ; IR: release the %18 rail (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_qram_load_i8_hl_unc(i32 %15, i32 %13, i32 1)    ; IR: un-copy %17 (a[1]): the cell is unchanged since the copy-out
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %15)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i8_hl_unc(i32 %13, i32 5, i32 %14)    ; IR: pop the store a[5] = 1 (made through a': popped before the realloc is undone; no other store touches cell 5)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %14)    ; IR: release the value handle (basis state 1)
  call void @cqrt_qram_realloc_i8_unc(i32 %13, i32 3)    ; IR: undo the realloc: the logical size is 3 again (cells 3..5 are |0>); %10 is the bus again
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i8_unc(i32 %10, i32 %11, i32 %12)    ; IR: pop the store a[k & 3] = v at the same logical size 3 as the forward store (k & 3 == 3 stays a no-op): every cell and its slot back to |0>
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %12)    ; IR: release the value handle (basis state v)
  call void @cq_template_and_i32_hl_unc(i32 %11, i32 %7, i32 3)    ; IR: uncompute %11
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %11)    ; IR: release the %11 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_zext_i8_to_i64_unc(i32 %9, i32 %8)    ; IR: uncompute %9
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %9)    ; IR: release the %9 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_and_i8_hl_unc(i32 %8, i32 %6, i8 3)    ; IR: uncompute %8
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %8)    ; IR: release the %8 rail (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_qram_free(i32 %10)    ; IR: scope end: release object 1's QRAM (every store popped, all cells |0>)
  %18 = call i8 @cqrt_measure_i8(i32 %17)    ; IR: %22 = cq_measure_ui8(%21)
  %19 = zext i8 %18 to i32    ; IR: %23 = zext i8 %22 to i32  (classical)
  ret i32 %19    ; IR: ret i32 %23
}

define i32 @heap_in_loop(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1) {
  %3 = alloca [3 x ptr], align 16    ; IR: the object table: the slot blocks of the trip objects 1..3 (filled by the loop)
  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %3 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %4, double %1)    ; IR: %3 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %5 = call i32 @cq_template_and_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 3)    ; IR: %4 = and i32 %3, 3  [the trip count, range [0, 3]: B = 3]
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: incoming null of phi %7: last's tag before trip 0 (NULL = 0)
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 true)    ; IR: predicate of reaching the first test (always 1)
  br label %8
8:
  %9 = phi i64 [ 0, %2 ], [ %21, %8 ]    ; IR: trip index, bounded by min(K, B) = 3  [B]
  %10 = phi i32 [ %6, %2 ], [ %20, %8 ]    ; IR: %7 = phi ptr [ null, %2 ], [ %11, %9 ]: last's tag so far
  %11 = phi i32 [ %7, %2 ], [ %14, %8 ]    ; IR: predicate of reaching this trip's test
  %12 = trunc nuw nsw i64 %9 to i32    ; IR: %10 = phi i32 (i, classical)
  %13 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %5, i32 %12)    ; IR: %5 = icmp eq i32 %4, 0 (trip 0) / %15 = icmp eq i32 %14, %4: the loop is over when i == %4
  %14 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: predicate of block %9 at this trip
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %13)    ; IR: bracket: the trip runs when i != %4
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %11, i32 %13, i32 %14)    ; IR: br i1 %5 / %15 not taken: a = ap & NOT e
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %13)    ; IR: bracket
  %15 = call ptr @malloc(i64 4)    ; IR: %11 = call @malloc(1): object j+1, a slot block of one byte cell = one handle slot  (host call, one per trip: 3 in all)
  %16 = getelementptr inbounds [3 x ptr], ptr %3, i64 0, i64 %9    ; IR: the table entry of object j+1
  store ptr %15, ptr %16, align 8    ; IR: table[j+1] = the block of %11  (classical)
  %17 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 %12)    ; IR: %12 = add i32 %10, %3
  %18 = call i32 @cq_template_trunc_i32_to_i8(i32 %17)    ; IR: %13 = trunc i32 %12 to i8
  store i32 %18, ptr %15, align 4    ; IR: store i8 %13, ptr %11: p[0] = (unsigned char)(x + i)  (slot store: the cell takes the handle, no gate)
  %19 = add nuw nsw i32 %12, 1    ; IR: %14 = add nuw nsw i32 %10, 1  (classical; also this trip's object tag j+1)
  %20 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_lh(i32 %14, i32 %19, i32 %10)    ; IR: next %7 = a ? %11 (object j+1) : last
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %10)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %11)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %13)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %17)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %18)
  %21 = add nuw nsw i64 %9, 1
  %22 = icmp ult i64 %21, 3    ; IR: br i1 %15, label %6, label %9, bounded by min(K, B) = 3 trips: after trip 2, i = 3 >= x & 3 on every branch  [B]
  br i1 %22, label %8, label %23
23:
  %24 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %20, i32 0)    ; IR: %8 = icmp eq ptr %7, null: tag == 0
  %25 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %20, i32 1)    ; IR: %17 = load i8, ptr %7: object 1 addressed iff tag == 1
  %26 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %20, i32 2)    ; IR: %17: object 2 addressed iff tag == 2 (object 3 is the complement)  [B]
  %27 = load ptr, ptr %3, align 8    ; IR: table[1]  (classical)
  %28 = load i32, ptr %27, align 4    ; IR: %17: object 1's cell 0 (the handle in its slot, no gate)
  %29 = getelementptr inbounds [3 x ptr], ptr %3, i64 0, i64 1
  %30 = load ptr, ptr %29, align 8    ; IR: table[2]
  %31 = load i32, ptr %30, align 4    ; IR: %17: object 2's cell 0
  %32 = getelementptr inbounds [3 x ptr], ptr %3, i64 0, i64 2
  %33 = load ptr, ptr %32, align 8    ; IR: table[3]  [B]
  %34 = load i32, ptr %33, align 4    ; IR: %17: object 3's cell 0
  %35 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i8(i32 %26, i32 %31, i32 %34)    ; IR: %17: tag == 2 ? obj2[0] : obj3[0]  (innermost: the complement)
  %36 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i8(i32 %25, i32 %28, i32 %35)    ; IR: %17 = load i8, ptr %7: tag == 1 ? obj1[0] : ...
  %37 = call i32 @cq_template_zext_i8_to_i32(i32 %36)    ; IR: %18 = zext i8 %17 to i32
  %38 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_lh(i32 %24, i32 7, i32 %37)    ; IR: %20 = phi i32 [ %18, %16 ], [ 7, %6 ]: null ? 7 : the load  [result rail]
  call void @cq_template_zext_i8_to_i32_unc(i32 %37, i32 %36)    ; IR: uncompute %18
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %37)    ; IR: release the %18 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_select_i8_unc(i32 %36, i32 %25, i32 %28, i32 %35)    ; IR: uncompute %17
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %36)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_select_i8_unc(i32 %35, i32 %26, i32 %31, i32 %34)    ; IR: uncompute the innermost select
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %35)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl_unc(i32 %26, i32 %20, i32 2)    ; IR: uncompute the object-2 flag
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %26)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl_unc(i32 %25, i32 %20, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute the object-1 flag
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %25)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl_unc(i32 %24, i32 %20, i32 0)    ; IR: uncompute %8
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %24)    ; IR: release the %8 rail (|0>)
  br label %39
39:
  %40 = phi i64 [ 2, %23 ], [ %50, %39 ]    ; IR: reverse of the loop: trip 2 down to 0  [B]
  %41 = phi i32 [ %20, %23 ], [ %47, %39 ]    ; IR: %7 as written by this trip
  %42 = phi i32 [ %14, %23 ], [ %46, %39 ]    ; IR: predicate of this trip
  %43 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: %13 of this trip (the trip object's cell)
  %44 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: %12 of this trip
  %45 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: %5 / %15 of this trip
  %46 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: predicate of reaching this trip's test
  %47 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: %7 incoming to this trip
  %48 = trunc nuw nsw i64 %40 to i32    ; IR: i of that trip (classical)
  %49 = add nuw nsw i32 %48, 1    ; IR: its object tag
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_lh_unc(i32 %41, i32 %42, i32 %49, i32 %47)    ; IR: uncompute next %7
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %41)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_trunc_i32_to_i8_unc(i32 %43, i32 %44)    ; IR: uncompute %13, the cell of the trip's object (no read of it is left)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %43)    ; IR: release the %13 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %44, i32 %4, i32 %48)    ; IR: uncompute %12
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %44)    ; IR: release the %12 rail (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %45)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %46, i32 %45, i32 %42)    ; IR: uncompute the trip predicate (the last one too: B <= K, nothing is kept)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %45)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %42)    ; IR: release the predicate (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl_unc(i32 %45, i32 %5, i32 %48)    ; IR: uncompute %5 / %15
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %45)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  %50 = add nsw i64 %40, -1
  %51 = icmp sge i64 %50, 0
  br i1 %51, label %39, label %52
52:
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %46)    ; IR: release the |1> seed directly (rule 7: known basis state)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %47)    ; IR: release incoming null of phi %7 (never written, |0>)
  call void @cq_template_and_i32_hl_unc(i32 %5, i32 %4, i32 3)    ; IR: uncompute %4
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %5)    ; IR: release the %4 rail (|0>)
  %53 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %38)    ; IR: %21 = cq_measure_si32(%20)
  ret i32 %53    ; IR: ret i32 %21
}

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 4, 9, 5, 2.
; Checked: mul_overflow: r + o, r = x * c wrapped, o its overflow flag; add_overflow_qq: overflow ? INT_MAX : x + y;
; add_sat: uadd_sat(x, c) (each measured).
; Clean: mul_overflow's overflow flag; add_overflow_qq's wrapped sum and overflow flag.
; Kept: the user registers (x; x and y; x); the measured result rails (mul_overflow: the product and the zext'd flag).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x (mul_overflow, add_sat); Ry(tx) on x and Ry(ty) on y (add_overflow_qq).
; The with.overflow intrinsics return the aggregate { iN, i1 }: the wrapped result and the overflow flag. The handle
; ABI gives one rail per template, so the aggregate is TWO templates over the same operands (rule 4; the convention of
; 81's op / op_exc twins): the value is the ordinary wrapping opcode template (mul_i32 for umul, add_i32 for sadd:
; that IS the wrapped result) and the flag is cq_template_<u|s><op>_overflow_<W>[_hl|_lh], an i1 rail, each with its
; own _unc. extractvalue selects the rail; zext i1 -> i32 is the cast template. llvm.uadd.sat (clang's fold of
; s = x + c; if (s < x) s = ~0u) is the single saturating template cq_template_uadd_sat_<W> (§1.2).
source_filename = "overflow_intrinsics.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %4, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %5 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 %2)    ; IR: %5 = umul.with.overflow(%4, %2): element 0, the wrapped product (%7)  [measured]
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_umul_overflow_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 %2)    ; IR: %5: element 1, the overflow flag (%6)
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_zext_i1_to_i32(i32 %6)    ; IR: %8 = zext i1 %6 to i32  [measured]
  call void @cq_template_umul_overflow_i32_hl_unc(i32 %6, i32 %4, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %6

  %8 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %5)    ; IR: %9 = cq_measure_ui32(%7)
  %9 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %7)    ; IR: %10 = cq_measure_si32(%8)
  %10 = add i32 %9, %8    ; IR: %11 = add i32 %10, %9  (classical)

define i32 @add_overflow_qq(i32 noundef %0, i32 noundef %1, double noundef %2, double noundef %3) {
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %2)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %5, double %2)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %2)  [Ry]
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %1)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_si32(%1, %3)  [register y]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %6, double %3)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_si32(%1, %3)  [Ry]
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32(i32 %5, i32 %6)    ; IR: %7 = sadd.with.overflow(%5, %6): element 0, the wrapped sum (%9)
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_sadd_overflow_i32(i32 %5, i32 %6)    ; IR: %7: element 1, the overflow flag (%8)
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_lh(i32 %8, i32 2147483647, i32 %7)    ; IR: %10 = select i1 %8, i32 2147483647, i32 %9  [result rail]
  call void @cq_template_sadd_overflow_i32_unc(i32 %8, i32 %5, i32 %6)    ; IR: uncompute %8
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %8)    ; IR: release the %8 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_unc(i32 %7, i32 %5, i32 %6)    ; IR: uncompute %9
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release the %9 rail (|0>)

  ret i32 %10    ; IR: ret i32 %11

  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %4, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [Ry]

  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %5)    ; IR: %6 = cq_measure_ui32(%5)
  ret i32 %6    ; IR: ret i32 %6
}

name: 93_i128
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 25, 4, 5, 2.
; Checked: mul_i128: (((x | 1 << 64) * c) >> 64) as 64 bits; div_i128: ((hi << 64 | lo) / (x | 1 << 64)) as 64 bits
; (each measured).
; Clean: every i128 intermediate (the zext, the or, the product or quotient, the shift).
; Kept: the user register x of each function; the truncated result rail (measured).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x (each function).
; 128-bit integers are a WIDTH VARIANT (rule 25): every i128 opcode is the same template family at W = 128
; (zext_i64_to_i128, or_i128_hl, mul_i128_hl, lshr_i128_hl, udiv_i128_lh, trunc_i128_to_i64), with classical i128
; operands passed as i128 values. Note on division: at -O1 the IR still holds `udiv i128` (the __udivti3 libcall
; appears only at codegen, below the IR), so it lowers as the udiv template like 11's i32 udiv (rule 4; §2 fixes
; udiv(a, 0)); the backend's circuit reference for it is compiler-rt's __udivti3 (udivmodti4.c), which is in the
; source bundle for lifting if a direct 128-bit divider is not provided. -O1 rewrote p + (c << 64) in mul_i128 into
; (x | 1 << 64) * c; the lowering follows the IR, not the C.
source_filename = "i128.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_or_i128_hl(i32 %5, i128 18446744073709551616)    ; IR: %7 = or disjoint i128 %5, 1 << 64

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 24, 20, 4, 9, 5, 6, 7, 2.
; Checked: now + ok + expected: the final cell, the cmpxchg success flag and the loaded value (measured).
; Clean: the cmpxchg equality flag; the classical initial-value rail c (never entangled, freed directly, rule 7); the old
; x rail (rule 6: dead after the cmpxchg select, its last reader; x + c is kept and a bijection in x) and t = (x + c) - c.
; Kept: the fetch-add result x + c and the cmpxchg select
; (the cell's later values: one of them is the measured `now`, the loaded value is the measured `expected`); the zext'd
; flag (measured).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x.
; THREADS ARE OUT OF THE MODEL (rule 24): a reversible circuit is sequential, so every atomic op has single-thread
; semantics and lowers as the plain op it wraps: store atomic = store, load atomic = load, atomicrmw add = load + add
; + store (its result is the old value), cmpxchg = load + icmp eq + select + store returning { loaded, equal } as two
; rails (64's aggregate), fence = nothing (no gate, no host call). cell is a non-escaping alloca written with a quantum
; value, so it is a SLOT OF HANDLES (31, rule 20): the classical initial store is promoted to a fresh rail holding c,
; and every later store/load moves a handle. The cmpxchg's loaded value (%10, "expected" after a failed exchange) and
; the final cell (%12) and the flag are measured; the rest is uncomputed.

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"

  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %2)    ; IR: store i32 %2, ptr %5: the classical initial value as a rail (the slot holds handles)
  store i32 %7, ptr %5, align 4    ; IR: store i32 %2, ptr %5  (store the handle)

  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %8, i32 %2)    ; IR: %7: old + %2  [the new cell]

  %12 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %11, i32 %8, i32 %10)    ; IR: %8: cell = equal ? %7 (the old value) : loaded  [the new cell]
  store i32 %12, ptr %5, align 4    ; IR: %8: store the new cell's handle
